data.reason: Set.range e = L.1 is the actual predicate that every element of L occurs as some e n, so e is an enumeration/surjection of L. The languages are represented as subtypes of infinite sets of integers, matching the universe and infinite-language requirement. The C1 clause has one generator g and, for each L∈C1, a member-dependent t after which every g n is in L and differs from all earlier g m; this matches non-uniform sample-free generation. The C2 clause fixes the same g and t for every L∈C2 with the same freshness condition, matching uniform sample-free generation. The negated sample-based clause quantifies over h:List ℤ→ℤ, every L∈C1∪C2, and every enumeration e of L, and requires after some t that h(prefix of length n) lies in L and avoids the prefix; this matches sample-based generation in the limit. statement.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

namespace Fcs76

def Language : Type := {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}

def prefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => prefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def UniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.BijOn e Set.univ L

def GeneratableInLimit (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Enumerates e (L : Set ℤ) →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (prefixOf e n) ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧
          h (prefixOf e n) ∉ prefixOf e n

end Fcs76

data.source_fragment: definitions of languages over integers, sample-free freshness, non-uniform and uniform generation without samples, enumeration of a language, and sample-based generation in the limit
data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

data.source_fragment: definitions of languages over integers, sample-free freshness, non-uniform and uniform generation without samples, enumeration of a language as a surjective range, and sample-based generation in the limit
data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

data.reason: Set.range e = L.1 is the actual predicate that every element of L occurs as some e n, so e is an enumeration/surjection of L. The languages are represented as subtypes of infinite sets of integers, matching the universe and infinite-language requirement. The C1 clause has one generator g and, for each L∈C1, a member-dependent t after which every g n is in L and differs from all earlier g m; this matches non-uniform sample-free generation. The C2 clause fixes the same g and t for every L∈C2 with the same freshness condition, matching uniform sample-free generation. The negated sample-based clause quantifies over h:List ℤ→ℤ, every L∈C1∪C2, and every enumeration e of L, and requires after some t that h(prefix of length n) lies in L and avoids the prefix; this matches sample-based generation in the limit. No material discrepancy found.

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

namespace Fcs76

def Language : Type := {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}

def prefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => prefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def UniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.BijOn e Set.univ L

def GeneratableInLimit (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Enumerates e (L : Set ℤ) →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (prefixOf e n) ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧
          h (prefixOf e n) ∉ prefixOf e n

end Fcs76

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

{L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}

def fcs76PrefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => fcs76PrefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def fcs76Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def fcs76NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → fcs76Fresh g n L

def fcs76UniformGeneratable (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → fcs76Fresh g n L

def fcs76Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.BijOn e Set.univ L

def fcs76GeneratableInLimit (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, fcs76Enumerates e (L : Set ℤ) →

          h (fcs76PrefixOf e n) ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧

def fcs76Language : Type := {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}

def fcs76PrefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => fcs76PrefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def fcs76Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def fcs76NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → fcs76Fresh g n L

def fcs76UniformGeneratable (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → fcs76Fresh g n L

def fcs76Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.range e = L

def fcs76GeneratableInLimit (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, fcs76Enumerates e L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (fcs76PrefixOf e n) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (fcs76PrefixOf e n) ∉ fcs76PrefixOf e n

data.source_fragment: definitions of languages over integers, sample-free freshness, non-uniform and uniform generation without samples, enumeration of a language as a surjective range, and sample-based generation in the limit
data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

data.reason: Set.range e = L.1 is the actual predicate that every element of L occurs as some e n, so e is an enumeration/surjection of L. The languages are represented as subtypes of infinite sets of integers, matching the universe and infinite-language requirement. The C1 clause has one generator g and, for each L∈C1, a member-dependent t after which every g n is in L and differs from all earlier g m; this matches non-uniform sample-free generation. The C2 clause fixes the same g and t for every L∈C2 with the same freshness condition, matching uniform sample-free generation. The negated sample-based clause quantifies over h:List ℤ→ℤ, every L∈C1∪C2, and every enumeration e of L, and requires after some t that h(prefix of length n) lies in L and avoids the prefix; this matches sample-based generation in the limit. No material discrepancy found.

statement.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

namespace Fcs76

def Language : Type := {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}

def prefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => prefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def UniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.BijOn e Set.univ L

def GeneratableInLimit (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Enumerates e (L : Set ℤ) →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (prefixOf e n) ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧
          h (prefixOf e n) ∉ prefixOf e n

end Fcs76

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

  | n + 1 => prefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def UniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

          h (prefixOf e n) ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧
          h (prefixOf e n) ∉ prefixOf e n

end Fcs76

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

def fcs76Language : Type := {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}

def fcs76PrefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => fcs76PrefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def fcs76Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def fcs76NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → fcs76Fresh g n L

def fcs76UniformGeneratable (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → fcs76Fresh g n L

def fcs76Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.range e = L

def fcs76GeneratableInLimit (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, fcs76Enumerates e L.1 →

data.reason: Set.range e = L.1 is the actual predicate that every element of L occurs as some e n, so e is an enumeration/surjection of L. The languages are represented as subtypes of infinite sets of integers, matching the universe and infinite-language requirement. The C1 clause has one generator g and, for each L∈C1, a member-dependent t after which every g n is in L and differs from all earlier g m; this matches non-uniform sample-free generation. The C2 clause fixes the same g and t for every L∈C2 with the same freshness condition, matching uniform sample-free generation. The negated sample-based clause quantifies over h:List ℤ→ℤ, every L∈C1∪C2, and every enumeration e of L, and requires after some t that h(prefix of length n) lies in L and avoids the prefix; this matches sample-based generation in the limit. No material discrepancy found.

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

namespace Fcs76

def Language : Type := {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}

def prefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => prefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def UniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.BijOn e Set.univ L

def GeneratableInLimit (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Enumerates e (L : Set ℤ) →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (prefixOf e n) ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧
          h (prefixOf e n) ∉ prefixOf e n

end Fcs76

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

  g n ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

          h (prefixOf e n) ∉ prefixOf e n

end Fcs76

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

def fcs76PrefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ

  | n + 1 => fcs76PrefixOf e n ++ [e n]

  g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → fcs76Fresh g n L

    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → fcs76Fresh g n L

def fcs76Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.range e = L

def fcs76GeneratableInLimit (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, fcs76Enumerates e L.1 →

data.reason: Set.range e = L.1 is the actual predicate that every element of L occurs as some e n, so e is an enumeration/surjection of L. The languages are represented as subtypes of infinite sets of integers, matching the universe and infinite-language requirement. The C1 clause has one generator g and, for each L∈C1, a member-dependent t after which every g n is in L and differs from all earlier g m; this matches non-uniform sample-free generation. The C2 clause fixes the same g and t for every L∈C2 with the same freshness condition, matching uniform sample-free generation. The negated sample-based clause quantifies over h:List ℤ→ℤ, every L∈C1∪C2, and every enumeration e of L, and requires after some t that h(prefix of length n) lies in L and avoids the prefix; this matches sample-based generation in the limit. No material discrepancy found.

statement.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

namespace Fcs76

def Language : Type := {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}

def prefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => prefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def UniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.BijOn e Set.univ L

def GeneratableInLimit (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Enumerates e (L : Set ℤ) →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (prefixOf e n) ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧
          h (prefixOf e n) ∉ prefixOf e n

end Fcs76

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

def fcs76PrefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => fcs76PrefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def fcs76Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def fcs76NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → fcs76Fresh g n L

def fcs76UniformGeneratable (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → fcs76Fresh g n L

def fcs76Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.BijOn e Set.univ L

def fcs76GeneratableInLimit (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, fcs76Enumerates e L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (fcs76PrefixOf e n) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (fcs76PrefixOf e n) ∉ fcs76PrefixOf e n

def mOfFn {m} [Monad m] {α : Type u} : ∀ {n}, (Fin n → m α) → m (Vector α n)

  | _ + 1, f => do

    let v ← mOfFn fun i => f i.succ

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

∃ C1 C2 : Set {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
  (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C1 →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
      g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
  (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C2 →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
      g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
  ¬ (∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ (C1 ∪ C2) →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))

The C1 clause has one generator g and, for each L∈C1, a member-dependent t after which every g n is in L and differs from all earlier g m; this matches non-uniform sample-free generation. The C2 clause fixes the same g and t for every L∈C2 with the same freshness condition, matching uniform sample-free generation. The negated sample-based clause quantifies over h:List ℤ→ℤ, every L∈C1∪C2, and every enumeration e of L, and requires after some t that h(prefix of length n) lies in L and avoids the prefix; this matches sample-based generation in the limit. No material discrepancy found.

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

namespace Fcs76

def Language : Type := {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}

def prefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => prefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def UniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.BijOn e Set.univ L

def GeneratableInLimit (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Enumerates e (L : Set ℤ) →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (prefixOf e n) ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧
          h (prefixOf e n) ∉ prefixOf e n

end Fcs76

data.source_fragment: definitions of languages over integers, sample-free freshness, non-uniform and uniform generation without samples, enumeration of a language as a surjective range, and sample-based generation in the limit
data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

The languages are represented as subtypes of infinite sets of integers, matching the universe and infinite-language requirement. The C1 clause has one generator g and, for each L∈C1, a member-dependent t after which every g n is in L and differs from all earlier g m; this matches non-uniform sample-free generation. statement.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

namespace Fcs76

def Language : Type := {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}

def prefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => prefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def UniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.BijOn e Set.univ L

def GeneratableInLimit (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Enumerates e (L : Set ℤ) →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (prefixOf e n) ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧
          h (prefixOf e n) ∉ prefixOf e n

end Fcs76

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

  g n ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def fcs76Language : Type := {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}

def fcs76PrefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => fcs76PrefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def fcs76Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def fcs76NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → fcs76Fresh g n L

def fcs76UniformGeneratable (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → fcs76Fresh g n L

def fcs76Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.BijOn e Set.univ L

def fcs76GeneratableInLimit (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, fcs76Enumerates e (L : Set ℤ) →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (fcs76PrefixOf e n) ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧
          h (fcs76PrefixOf e n) ∉ fcs76PrefixOf e n

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

data.source_fragment: definitions of languages over integers, sample-free freshness, non-uniform and uniform generation without samples, enumeration of a language as a surjective range, and sample-based generation in the limit
data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

data.reason: Set.range e = L.1 is the actual predicate that every element of L occurs as some e n, so e is an enumeration/surjection of L. The languages are represented as subtypes of infinite sets of integers, matching the universe and infinite-language requirement. The C1 clause has one generator g and, for each L∈C1, a member-dependent t after which every g n is in L and differs from all earlier g m; this matches non-uniform sample-free generation. The C2 clause fixes the same g and t for every L∈C2 with the same freshness condition, matching uniform sample-free generation. The negated sample-based clause quantifies over h:List ℤ→ℤ, every L∈C1∪C2, and every enumeration e of L, and requires after some t that h(prefix of length n) lies in L and avoids the prefix; this matches sample-based generation in the limit. No material discrepancy found.

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

namespace Fcs76

def Language : Type := {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}

def prefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => prefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def UniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.BijOn e Set.univ L

def GeneratableInLimit (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Enumerates e (L : Set ℤ) →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (prefixOf e n) ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧
          h (prefixOf e n) ∉ prefixOf e n

end Fcs76

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => prefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def UniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.BijOn e Set.univ L

def GeneratableInLimit (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Enumerates e (L : Set ℤ) →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (prefixOf e n) ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧
          h (prefixOf e n) ∉ prefixOf e n

end Fcs76

data.source_fragment: definitions of languages over integers, sample-free freshness, non-uniform and uniform generation without samples, enumeration of a language, and sample-based generation in the limit
data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

data.reason: Set.range e = L.1 is the actual predicate that every element of L occurs as some e n, so e is an enumeration/surjection of L. The languages are represented as subtypes of infinite sets of integers, matching the universe and infinite-language requirement. The C1 clause has one generator g and, for each L∈C1, a member-dependent t after which every g n is in L and differs from all earlier g m; this matches non-uniform sample-free generation. The C2 clause fixes the same g and t for every L∈C2 with the same freshness condition, matching uniform sample-free generation. The negated sample-based clause quantifies over h:List ℤ→ℤ, every L∈C1∪C2, and every enumeration e of L, and requires after some t that h(prefix of length n) lies in L and avoids the prefix; this matches sample-based generation in the limit. No material discrepancy found.

statement.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

namespace Fcs76

def Language : Type := {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}

def prefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => prefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def UniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.BijOn e Set.univ L

def GeneratableInLimit (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Enumerates e (L : Set ℤ) →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (prefixOf e n) ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧
          h (prefixOf e n) ∉ prefixOf e n

end Fcs76

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

result.statement: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
result.proof: Take the nonnegative integers as points p_n = n and the negative integers as points m_n = −n−1. Let C₁ be the languages whose carrier contains some tail {p_{N+j} : j ≥ 0}, and C₂ the languages whose carrier contains every m_n. The sequence (p_n) is injective and generates each member of C₁ after its cutoff, giving non-uniform sample-free generation; the sequence (m_n) generates each member of C₂ from time zero, giving uniform sample-free generation. Freshness reduces to membership together with absence of earlier repetition, which holds because both sequences are injective. For the negative clause, assume some sample-based generator G generates the union in the limit. Build nested finite injective prefixes together with strictly increasing cutoffs: given a stage prefix s and cutoff N, enumerate s followed by the positive tail from N; this enumeration belongs to C₁, so G must eventually output a fresh value, which cannot be a previously listed element and hence is some p_k with k ≥ N. Extend the prefix by that observed enumeration prefix and append the next negative point m_n, choosing a fresh larger cutoff so that p_k occurs neither in the new prefix nor in its future positive tail. Induction shows p_k is never reproduced later. The nested prefixes converge to an injective sequence x whose range is infinite and contains every negative point, so it is the carrier of a language in C₂ that x enumerates. At each stage time the prefix of x agrees with the recorded stage prefix, so G outputs p_k, which lies outside this limiting language; since these failures occur arbitrarily late, G fails to generate in the limit, a contradiction. Hence the union is not generatable in the limit, and the constructed collections witness the claim.

nodes.claim: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
nodes.statement:
theorem fcs76_collections_exist :
  ∃ C1 C2 : Set {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
    (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C1 →
      ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
        g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
    (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C2 →
      ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
        g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
    ¬ (∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
      ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ (C1 ∪ C2) →
        ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
          ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
              List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))

def Language : Type := {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}

def prefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => prefixOf e n ++ [e n]

  g n ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

  Set.BijOn e Set.univ L

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

data.reason: Set.range e = L.1 is the actual predicate that every element of L occurs as some e n, so e is an enumeration/surjection of L. The languages are represented as subtypes of infinite sets of integers, matching the universe and infinite-language requirement. The C1 clause has one generator g and, for each L∈C1, a member-dependent t after which every g n is in L and differs from all earlier g m; this matches non-uniform sample-free generation. The C2 clause fixes the same g and t for every L∈C2 with the same freshness condition, matching uniform sample-free generation. The negated sample-based clause quantifies over h:List ℤ→ℤ, every L∈C1∪C2, and every enumeration e of L, and requires after some t that h(prefix of length n) lies in L and avoids the prefix; this matches sample-based generation in the limit. No material discrepancy found.

statement.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

namespace Fcs76

def Language : Type := {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}

def prefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []

data.source_fragment: definitions of languages over integers, sample-free freshness, non-uniform and uniform generation without samples, enumeration of a language as a surjective range, and sample-based generation in the limit
data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

nodes.claim: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
nodes.statement:
theorem fcs76_collections_exist :
  ∃ C1 C2 : Set {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
    (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C1 →
      ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
        g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
    (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C2 →
      ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
        g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
    ¬ (∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
      ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ (C1 ∪ C2) →
        ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
          ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
              List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))

data.helper_source:
namespace Fcs76

def Language : Type := {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}

def prefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => prefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def UniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.BijOn e Set.univ L

def GeneratableInLimit (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,

def fcs76PrefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => fcs76PrefixOf e n ++ [e n]

  g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → fcs76Fresh g n L

data.source_fragment: definitions of languages over integers, sample-free freshness, non-uniform and uniform generation without samples, enumeration of a language as a surjective range, and sample-based generation in the limit
data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

The languages are represented as subtypes of infinite sets of integers, matching the universe and infinite-language requirement. The C1 clause has one generator g and, for each L∈C1, a member-dependent t after which every g n is in L and differs from all earlier g m; this matches non-uniform sample-free generation. statement.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

namespace Fcs76

def Language : Type := {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}

def prefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => prefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def UniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.BijOn e Set.univ L

def GeneratableInLimit (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Enumerates e (L : Set ℤ) →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (prefixOf e n) ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧
          h (prefixOf e n) ∉ prefixOf e n

end Fcs76

data.source_fragment: definitions of languages over integers, sample-free freshness, non-uniform and uniform generation without samples, enumeration of a language, and sample-based generation in the limit
data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

def fcs76Language : Type := {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}

def fcs76PrefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => fcs76PrefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def fcs76Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def fcs76NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → fcs76Fresh g n L

def fcs76UniformGeneratable (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → fcs76Fresh g n L

def fcs76Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.range e = L

def fcs76GeneratableInLimit (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, fcs76Enumerates e L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (fcs76PrefixOf e n) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (fcs76PrefixOf e n) ∉ fcs76PrefixOf e n

data.source_fragment: definitions of languages over integers, sample-free freshness, non-uniform and uniform generation without samples, enumeration of a language as a surjective range, and sample-based generation in the limit
data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

namespace Fcs76

def Language : Type := {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}

def prefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => prefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def UniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.BijOn e Set.univ L

def GeneratableInLimit (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Enumerates e (L : Set ℤ) →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (prefixOf e n) ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧
          h (prefixOf e n) ∉ prefixOf e n

end Fcs76

  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => prefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def UniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.BijOn e Set.univ L

def GeneratableInLimit (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Enumerates e (L : Set ℤ) →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (prefixOf e n) ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧
          h (prefixOf e n) ∉ prefixOf e n

end Fcs76

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. data.source_fragment: definitions of languages over integers, sample-free freshness, non-uniform and uniform generation without samples, enumeration of a language as a surjective range, and sample-based generation in the limit
data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

The languages are represented as subtypes of infinite sets of integers, matching the universe and infinite-language requirement. The C1 clause has one generator g and, for each L∈C1, a member-dependent t after which every g n is in L and differs from all earlier g m; this matches non-uniform sample-free generation.
