result.statement: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
result.proof: Take the nonnegative integers as points p_n = n and the negative integers as points m_n = −n−1. Let C₁ be the languages whose carrier contains some tail {p_{N+j} : j ≥ 0}, and C₂ the languages whose carrier contains every m_n. The sequence (p_n) is injective and generates each member of C₁ after its cutoff, giving non-uniform sample-free generation; the sequence (m_n) generates each member of C₂ from time zero, giving uniform sample-free generation. Freshness reduces to membership together with absence of earlier repetition, which holds because both sequences are injective. For the negative clause, assume some sample-based generator G generates the union in the limit. Build nested finite injective prefixes together with strictly increasing cutoffs: given a stage prefix s and cutoff N, enumerate s followed by the positive tail from N; this enumeration belongs to C₁, so G must eventually output a fresh value, which cannot be a previously listed element and hence is some p_k with k ≥ N. Extend the prefix by that observed enumeration prefix and append the next negative point m_n, choosing a fresh larger cutoff so that p_k occurs neither in the new prefix nor in its future positive tail. Induction shows p_k is never reproduced later. The nested prefixes converge to an injective sequence x whose range is infinite and contains every negative point, so it is the carrier of a language in C₂ that x enumerates. At each stage time the prefix of x agrees with the recorded stage prefix, so G outputs p_k, which lies outside this limiting language; since these failures occur arbitrarily late, G fails to generate in the limit, a contradiction. Hence the union is not generatable in the limit, and the constructed collections witness the claim.

let neg : ℕ → ℤ := fun n => (-(n : ℤ) - 1)
let last : ℕ → List ℤ := fun n => if n = 0 then [] else [neg (n-1)]
let State := ((List ℤ × List ℤ) × (ℕ × ℤ)) × (List ℤ × ℕ)
let full : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.1
let q : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.2
let cut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.1.2.1
let recv : State → ℤ := fun p => p.1.2.2
let prev : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.2.1
let prevCut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.2.2
let mk : List ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → State :=
  fun f qq c r p pc => (((f, qq), (c, r)), (p, pc))
let Pre : ℕ → State → Prop := fun n p =>
  (full p).Nodup ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), z < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), neg n < z) ∧
  n ≤ (full p).length ∧
  (full p) = (q p) ++ (last n) ∧
  (∃ rest : List ℤ, (q p) = (prev p) ++ rest) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (0 < (recv p) ∧ (recv p) = h (q p) ∧ (recv p) ∉ (q p) ∧ (recv p) < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ))) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (prevCut p) < (cut p)) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (∀ z ∈ (q p), z ∈ (prev p) ∨ ((prevCut p : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ z))

    intro z hz

  rcases ProofSteps.diag_tail h hgen (full p) (cut p) (n+1) hpnd hp_lt hgtm with
    ⟨qq, N', v, hpref, hnd, hgrow, hqlt, hqgt, hvpos, hveq, hvnot, hNlt, hvlt, hsep⟩
  have hn0 : n + 1 ≠ 0 := by omega
  have hlast : last (n + 1) = [neg n] := by simp [last, hn0]

  have hfull_eq_sing : full p' = qq ++ [neg n] := by
    simp only [p', full', full, mk]
    rw [hlast]
  have hq_gt_neg : ∀ z ∈ qq, neg n < z := by
    intro z hz
    rcases hsep z hz with hzs | hzN
    · exact hp_gt z hzs
    · have hneg0 : neg n < 0 := by dsimp [neg]; omega
      have h0le : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (cut p : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.zero_le (cut p)

classical
let neg : ℕ → ℤ := fun n => (-(n : ℤ) - 1)
let last : ℕ → List ℤ := fun n => if n = 0 then [] else [neg (n-1)]
let State := ((List ℤ × List ℤ) × (ℕ × ℤ)) × (List ℤ × ℕ)
let full : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.1
let q : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.2
let cut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.1.2.1
let recv : State → ℤ := fun p => p.1.2.2
let prev : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.2.1
let prevCut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.2.2
let mk : List ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → State :=
  fun f qq c r p pc => (((f, qq), (c, r)), (p, pc))
let Pre : ℕ → State → Prop := fun n p =>
  (full p).Nodup ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), z < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), neg n < z) ∧
  n ≤ (full p).length ∧
  (full p) = (q p) ++ (last n) ∧
  (∃ rest : List ℤ, (q p) = (prev p) ++ rest) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (0 < (recv p) ∧ (recv p) = h (q p) ∧ (recv p) ∉ (q p) ∧ (recv p) < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ))) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (prevCut p) < (cut p)) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (∀ z ∈ (q p), z ∈ (prev p) ∨ ((prevCut p : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ z))
skip
let baseState : State := mk [] [] 0 0 [] 0
have hbase : Pre 0 baseState := by
  simp [Pre, baseState, full, q, cut, recv, prev, prevCut, mk, last]
have mainstep : ∀ (n : ℕ) (p : State), Pre n p → ∃ p' : State, Pre (n+1) p' := by
  intro n p hp
  unfold Pre at hp
  rcases hp with ⟨hpnd, hp_lt, hp_gt, hplen, hpfq, hpqprev, hprec, hpcut, hpsep⟩
  have hgtm : ∀ z ∈ full p, neg (n+1) < z := by
    intro z hz
    have hn : neg (n+1) < neg n := by
      dsimp [neg]
      omega
    exact lt_trans hn (hp_gt z hz)
  rcases ProofSteps.diag_tail h hgen (full p) (cut p) (n+1) hpnd hp_lt hgtm with
    ⟨qq, N', v, hpref, hnd, hgrow, hqlt, hqgt, hvpos, hveq, hvnot, hNlt, hvlt, hsep⟩
  have hn0 : n + 1 ≠ 0 := by omega
  have hlast : last (n + 1) = [neg n] := by simp [last, hn0]
  let full' : List ℤ := qq ++ last (n+1)
  let p' : State := mk full' qq N' v (full p) (cut p)
  have hfull_eq_sing : full p' = qq ++ [neg n] := by
    simp only [p', full', full, mk]
    rw [hlast]
  have hq_gt_neg : ∀ z ∈ qq, neg n < z := by
    intro z hz
    rcases hsep z hz with hzs | hzN
    · exact hp_gt z hzs
    · have hneg0 : neg n < 0 := by dsimp [neg]; omega
      have h0le : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (cut p : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.zero_le (cut p)
      have h0lez : (0 : ℤ) ≤ z := le_trans h0le hzN
      exact lt_of_lt_of_le hneg0 h0lez
  have hfull_nd : (full p').Nodup := by
    have hneg_nd : [neg n].Nodup := by simp
    have hdisj : List.Disjoint qq [neg n] := by
      intro z hz hzsing
      have hzneg : z = neg n := by simpa using hzsing
      have hzgt : neg n < z := hq_gt_neg z hz

result.statement: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
result.proof: Take the nonnegative integers as points p_n = n and the negative integers as points m_n = −n−1. Let C₁ be the languages whose carrier contains some tail {p_{N+j} : j ≥ 0}, and C₂ the languages whose carrier contains every m_n. The sequence (p_n) is injective and generates each member of C₁ after its cutoff, giving non-uniform sample-free generation; the sequence (m_n) generates each member of C₂ from time zero, giving uniform sample-free generation. Freshness reduces to membership together with absence of earlier repetition, which holds because both sequences are injective. For the negative clause, assume some sample-based generator G generates the union in the limit. Build nested finite injective prefixes together with strictly increasing cutoffs: given a stage prefix s and cutoff N, enumerate s followed by the positive tail from N; this enumeration belongs to C₁, so G must eventually output a fresh value, which cannot be a previously listed element and hence is some p_k with k ≥ N. Extend the prefix by that observed enumeration prefix and append the next negative point m_n, choosing a fresh larger cutoff so that p_k occurs neither in the new prefix nor in its future positive tail. Induction shows p_k is never reproduced later. The nested prefixes converge to an injective sequence x whose range is infinite and contains every negative point, so it is the carrier of a language in C₂ that x enumerates. At each stage time the prefix of x agrees with the recorded stage prefix, so G outputs p_k, which lies outside this limiting language; since these failures occur arbitrarily late, G fails to generate in the limit, a contradiction. Hence the union is not generatable in the limit, and the constructed collections witness the claim.

let neg : ℕ → ℤ := fun n => (-(n : ℤ) - 1)

  (∀ z ∈ (full p), z < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧

let last : ℕ → List ℤ := fun n => if n = 0 then [] else [neg (n-1)]

let full : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.1
let q : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.2
let cut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.1.2.1
let recv : State → ℤ := fun p => p.1.2.2
let prev : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.2.1
let prevCut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.2.2
let mk : List ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → State :=
  fun f qq c r p pc => (((f, qq), (c, r)), (p, pc))
let Pre : ℕ → State → Prop := fun n p =>
  (full p).Nodup ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), z < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), neg n < z) ∧
  n ≤ (full p).length ∧
  (full p) = (q p) ++ (last n) ∧
  (∃ rest : List ℤ, (q p) = (prev p) ++ rest) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (0 < (recv p) ∧ (recv p) = h (q p) ∧ (recv p) ∉ (q p) ∧ (recv p) < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ))) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (prevCut p) < (cut p)) ∧

    exact List.Nodup.append hnd hneg_nd hdisj

    intro z hz

      exact hz

    rcases hzm with hzq | hzsing

  fun n => Nat.rec ⟨baseState, hbase⟩

result.statement: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
result.proof: Take the nonnegative integers as points p_n = n and the negative integers as points m_n = −n−1. Let C₁ be the languages whose carrier contains some tail {p_{N+j} : j ≥ 0}, and C₂ the languages whose carrier contains every m_n. The sequence (p_n) is injective and generates each member of C₁ after its cutoff, giving non-uniform sample-free generation; the sequence (m_n) generates each member of C₂ from time zero, giving uniform sample-free generation. Freshness reduces to membership together with absence of earlier repetition, which holds because both sequences are injective. For the negative clause, assume some sample-based generator G generates the union in the limit. Build nested finite injective prefixes together with strictly increasing cutoffs: given a stage prefix s and cutoff N, enumerate s followed by the positive tail from N; this enumeration belongs to C₁, so G must eventually output a fresh value, which cannot be a previously listed element and hence is some p_k with k ≥ N. Extend the prefix by that observed enumeration prefix and append the next negative point m_n, choosing a fresh larger cutoff so that p_k occurs neither in the new prefix nor in its future positive tail. Induction shows p_k is never reproduced later. The nested prefixes converge to an injective sequence x whose range is infinite and contains every negative point, so it is the carrier of a language in C₂ that x enumerates. At each stage time the prefix of x agrees with the recorded stage prefix, so G outputs p_k, which lies outside this limiting language; since these failures occur arbitrarily late, G fails to generate in the limit, a contradiction. Hence the union is not generatable in the limit, and the constructed collections witness the claim.

let neg : ℕ → ℤ := fun n => (-(n : ℤ) - 1)
let last : ℕ → List ℤ := fun n => if n = 0 then [] else [neg (n-1)]
let State := ((List ℤ × List ℤ) × (ℕ × ℤ)) × (List ℤ × ℕ)
let full : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.1
let q : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.2
let cut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.1.2.1
let recv : State → ℤ := fun p => p.1.2.2
let prev : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.2.1
let prevCut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.2.2
let mk : List ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → State :=
  fun f qq c r p pc => (((f, qq), (c, r)), (p, pc))
let Pre : ℕ → State → Prop := fun n p =>
  (full p).Nodup ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), z < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), neg n < z) ∧
  n ≤ (full p).length ∧
  (full p) = (q p) ++ (last n) ∧
  (∃ rest : List ℤ, (q p) = (prev p) ++ rest) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (0 < (recv p) ∧ (recv p) = h (q p) ∧ (recv p) ∉ (q p) ∧ (recv p) < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ))) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (prevCut p) < (cut p)) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (∀ z ∈ (q p), z ∈ (prev p) ∨ ((prevCut p : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ z))

let baseState : State := mk [] [] 0 0 [] 0

have mainstep : ∀ (n : ℕ) (p : State), Pre n p → ∃ p' : State, Pre (n+1) p' := by
  intro n p hp
  unfold Pre at hp
  rcases hp with ⟨hpnd, hp_lt, hp_gt, hplen, hpfq, hpqprev, hprec, hpcut, hpsep⟩
  have hgtm : ∀ z ∈ full p, neg (n+1) < z := by
    intro z hz
    have hn : neg (n+1) < neg n := by
      dsimp [neg]
      omega
    exact lt_trans hn (hp_gt z hz)
  rcases ProofSteps.diag_tail h hgen (full p) (cut p) (n+1) hpnd hp_lt hgtm with
    ⟨qq, N', v, hpref, hnd, hgrow, hqlt, hqgt, hvpos, hveq, hvnot, hNlt, hvlt, hsep⟩
  have hn0 : n + 1 ≠ 0 := by omega
  have hlast : last (n + 1) = [neg n] := by simp [last, hn0]
  let full' : List ℤ := qq ++ last (n+1)
  let p' : State := mk full' qq N' v (full p) (cut p)
  have hfull_eq_sing : full p' = qq ++ [neg n] := by
    simp only [p', full', full, mk]
    rw [hlast]
  have hq_gt_neg : ∀ z ∈ qq, neg n < z := by
    intro z hz
    rcases hsep z hz with hzs | hzN
    · exact hp_gt z hzs
    · have hneg0 : neg n < 0 := by dsimp [neg]; omega
      have h0le : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (cut p : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.zero_le (cut p)
      have h0lez : (0 : ℤ) ≤ z := le_trans h0le hzN
      exact lt_of_lt_of_le hneg0 h0lez
  have hfull_nd : (full p').Nodup := by
    have hneg_nd : [neg n].Nodup := by simp
    have hdisj : List.Disjoint qq [neg n] := by

      have hzneg : z = neg n := by simpa using hzsing

      rw [hzneg] at hzgt
      exact (lt_irrefl (neg n) hzgt)
    rw [hfull_eq_sing]

    intro z hz
    have hzm : z ∈ qq ++ [neg n] := by
      rw [hfull_eq_sing] at hz
      exact hz
    rw [List.mem_append] at hzm
    rcases hzm with hzq | hzsing
    · simpa [p', cut, mk] using hqlt z hzq
    · have hzneg : z = neg n := by simpa using hzsing

      have hneg0 : neg n < 0 := by dsimp [neg]; omega

    have hNlt' : cut p < N' := by exact_mod_cast hNlt
    simpa [p', prevCut, cut, mk] using hNlt'
  have hsep' : (n+1 = 0 ∨ ∀ z ∈ q p', z ∈ prev p' ∨ (prevCut p' : ℤ) ≤ z) := by
    right
    intro z hz
    have hz' : z ∈ qq := by simpa [p', q, mk] using hz

      simpa [p', prev, mk] using hzs
    · right

declarations.doc:
When `s` is an infinite set, `nth` agrees with `Nat.Subtype.orderIsoOfNat`. -/
theorem nth_eq_orderIsoOfNat (hf : (Set.ofPred p).Infinite) :
    nth p = (↑) ∘ @Nat.Subtype.orderIsoOfNat (Set.ofPred p) hf.to_subtype :=
  funext <| nth_apply_eq_orderIsoOfNat hf

theorem nth_strictMono (hf : (Set.ofPred p).Infinite) : StrictMono (nth p) := by
  rw [nth_eq_orderIsoOfNat hf]
  exact (Subtype.strictMono_coe _).comp (OrderIso.strictMono _)

theorem nth_injective (hf : (Set.ofPred p).Infinite) : Function.Injective (nth p) :=
  (nth_strictMono hf).injective

theorem nth_monotone (hf : (Set.ofPred p).Infinite) : Monotone (nth p) :=
  (nth_strictMono hf).monotone

theorem nth_lt_nth (hf : (Set.ofPred p).Infinite) {k n} : nth p k < nth p n ↔ k < n :=
  (nth_strictMono hf).lt_iff_lt

theorem nth_le_nth (hf : (Set.ofPred p).Infinite) {k n} : nth p k ≤ nth p n ↔ k ≤ n :=
  (nth_strictMono hf).le_iff_le

theorem range_nth_of_infinite (hf : (Set.ofPred p).Infinite) :
    Set.range (nth p) = Set.ofPred p := by
  rw [nth_eq_orderIsoOfNat hf]
  have := hf.to_subtype
  classical exact Nat.Subtype.coe_comp_ofNat_range

theorem nth_mem_of_infinite (hf : (Set.ofPred p).Infinite) (n : ℕ) : p (nth p n) :=
  Set.range_subset_iff.1 (range_nth_of_infinite hf).le n

result.statement: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
result.proof: Take the nonnegative integers as points p_n = n and the negative integers as points m_n = −n−1. Let C₁ be the languages whose carrier contains some tail {p_{N+j} : j ≥ 0}, and C₂ the languages whose carrier contains every m_n. The sequence (p_n) is injective and generates each member of C₁ after its cutoff, giving non-uniform sample-free generation; the sequence (m_n) generates each member of C₂ from time zero, giving uniform sample-free generation. Freshness reduces to membership together with absence of earlier repetition, which holds because both sequences are injective. For the negative clause, assume some sample-based generator G generates the union in the limit. Build nested finite injective prefixes together with strictly increasing cutoffs: given a stage prefix s and cutoff N, enumerate s followed by the positive tail from N; this enumeration belongs to C₁, so G must eventually output a fresh value, which cannot be a previously listed element and hence is some p_k with k ≥ N. Extend the prefix by that observed enumeration prefix and append the next negative point m_n, choosing a fresh larger cutoff so that p_k occurs neither in the new prefix nor in its future positive tail. Induction shows p_k is never reproduced later. The nested prefixes converge to an injective sequence x whose range is infinite and contains every negative point, so it is the carrier of a language in C₂ that x enumerates. At each stage time the prefix of x agrees with the recorded stage prefix, so G outputs p_k, which lies outside this limiting language; since these failures occur arbitrarily late, G fails to generate in the limit, a contradiction. Hence the union is not generatable in the limit, and the constructed collections witness the claim.

theorem Nodup.get_inj_iff {l : List α} (h : Nodup l) {i j : Fin l.length} :

let neg : ℕ → ℤ := fun n => (-(n : ℤ) - 1)
let last : ℕ → List ℤ := fun n => if n = 0 then [] else [neg (n-1)]
let State := ((List ℤ × List ℤ) × (ℕ × ℤ)) × (List ℤ × ℕ)
let full : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.1
let q : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.2
let cut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.1.2.1
let recv : State → ℤ := fun p => p.1.2.2
let prev : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.2.1
let prevCut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.2.2
let mk : List ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → State :=
  fun f qq c r p pc => (((f, qq), (c, r)), (p, pc))
let Pre : ℕ → State → Prop := fun n p =>
  (full p).Nodup ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), z < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), neg n < z) ∧
  n ≤ (full p).length ∧
  (full p) = (q p) ++ (last n) ∧
  (∃ rest : List ℤ, (q p) = (prev p) ++ rest) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (0 < (recv p) ∧ (recv p) = h (q p) ∧ (recv p) ∉ (q p) ∧ (recv p) < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ))) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (prevCut p) < (cut p)) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (∀ z ∈ (q p), z ∈ (prev p) ∨ ((prevCut p : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ z))

let full : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.1
let q : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.2
let cut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.1.2.1
let recv : State → ℤ := fun p => p.1.2.2
let prev : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.2.1
let prevCut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.2.2

  fun f qq c r p pc => (((f, qq), (c, r)), (p, pc))
let Pre : ℕ → State → Prop := fun n p =>
  (full p).Nodup ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), z < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), neg n < z) ∧
  n ≤ (full p).length ∧
  (full p) = (q p) ++ (last n) ∧

  rcases ProofSteps.diag_tail h hgen (full p) (cut p) (n+1) hpnd hp_lt hgtm with
    ⟨qq, N', v, hpref, hnd, hgrow, hqlt, hqgt, hvpos, hveq, hvnot, hNlt, hvlt, hsep⟩

      exact (lt_irrefl (neg n) hzgt)
    rw [hfull_eq_sing]
    exact List.Nodup.append hnd hneg_nd hdisj
  have hfull_lt : ∀ z ∈ full p', z < (cut p' : ℤ) := by
    intro z hz
    have hzm : z ∈ qq ++ [neg n] := by

    rw [List.mem_append] at hzm
    rcases hzm with hzq | hzsing
    · simpa [p', cut, mk] using hqlt z hzq
    · have hzneg : z = neg n := by simpa using hzsing

    rw [List.mem_append] at hzm
    rcases hzm with hzq | hzsing
    · exact hqgt z hzq

    rw [hfull_eq_sing]
    simp

  have hfull_eq : full p' = q p' ++ last (n+1) := by

    intro z hz

result.statement: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
result.proof: Take the nonnegative integers as points p_n = n and the negative integers as points m_n = −n−1. Let C₁ be the languages whose carrier contains some tail {p_{N+j} : j ≥ 0}, and C₂ the languages whose carrier contains every m_n. The sequence (p_n) is injective and generates each member of C₁ after its cutoff, giving non-uniform sample-free generation; the sequence (m_n) generates each member of C₂ from time zero, giving uniform sample-free generation. Freshness reduces to membership together with absence of earlier repetition, which holds because both sequences are injective. For the negative clause, assume some sample-based generator G generates the union in the limit. Build nested finite injective prefixes together with strictly increasing cutoffs: given a stage prefix s and cutoff N, enumerate s followed by the positive tail from N; this enumeration belongs to C₁, so G must eventually output a fresh value, which cannot be a previously listed element and hence is some p_k with k ≥ N. Extend the prefix by that observed enumeration prefix and append the next negative point m_n, choosing a fresh larger cutoff so that p_k occurs neither in the new prefix nor in its future positive tail. Induction shows p_k is never reproduced later. The nested prefixes converge to an injective sequence x whose range is infinite and contains every negative point, so it is the carrier of a language in C₂ that x enumerates. At each stage time the prefix of x agrees with the recorded stage prefix, so G outputs p_k, which lies outside this limiting language; since these failures occur arbitrarily late, G fails to generate in the limit, a contradiction. Hence the union is not generatable in the limit, and the constructed collections witness the claim.

  have hfull_lt : ∀ z ∈ full p', z < (cut p' : ℤ) := by
    intro z hz
    have hzm : z ∈ qq ++ [neg n] := by
      rw [hfull_eq_sing] at hz
      exact hz
    rw [List.mem_append] at hzm
    rcases hzm with hzq | hzsing
    · simpa [p', cut, mk] using hqlt z hzq
    · have hzneg : z = neg n := by simpa using hzsing
      rw [hzneg]
      have hneg0 : neg n < 0 := by dsimp [neg]; omega
      have h0le : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (cut p : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.zero_le (cut p)
      have hnegcut : neg n < (cut p : ℤ) := lt_of_lt_of_le hneg0 h0le
      simpa [p', cut, mk] using (lt_trans hnegcut hNlt)
  have hfull_gt : ∀ z ∈ full p', neg (n+1) < z := by
    intro z hz
    have hzm : z ∈ qq ++ [neg n] := by
      rw [hfull_eq_sing] at hz
      exact hz
    rw [List.mem_append] at hzm
    rcases hzm with hzq | hzsing
    · exact hqgt z hzq
    · have hzneg : z = neg n := by simpa using hzsing
      rw [hzneg]
      have hneglt : neg (n+1) < neg n := by dsimp [neg]; omega
      exact hneglt
  have hfull_len : n + 1 ≤ (full p').length := by
    rw [hfull_eq_sing]
    simp
    omega
  have hfull_eq : full p' = q p' ++ last (n+1) := by
    simp [p', full', full, q, mk]
  have hqprev : ∃ rest : List ℤ, q p' = prev p' ++ rest := by
    rcases hpref with ⟨rest, hr⟩
    refine ⟨rest, ?_⟩
    simpa [p', q, prev, mk] using hr
  have hrec' : (n+1 = 0 ∨ (0 < recv p' ∧ recv p' = h (q p') ∧ recv p' ∉ q p' ∧ recv p' < (cut p' : ℤ))) := by
    right
    refine ⟨hvpos, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · simpa [p', recv, q, mk] using hveq
    · simpa [p', recv, q, mk] using hvnot
    · simpa [p', recv, cut, mk] using hvlt
  have hcut' : (n+1 = 0 ∨ prevCut p' < cut p') := by
    right
    have hNlt' : cut p < N' := by exact_mod_cast hNlt
    simpa [p', prevCut, cut, mk] using hNlt'
  have hsep' : (n+1 = 0 ∨ ∀ z ∈ q p', z ∈ prev p' ∨ (prevCut p' : ℤ) ≤ z) := by
    right
    intro z hz
    have hz' : z ∈ qq := by simpa [p', q, mk] using hz
    rcases hsep z hz' with hzs | hzN
    · left
      simpa [p', prev, mk] using hzs
    · right
      simpa [p', prevCut, mk] using hzN
  have hp' : Pre (n+1) p' := by
    exact ⟨hfull_nd, hfull_lt, hfull_gt, hfull_len, hfull_eq, hqprev, hrec', hcut', hsep'⟩
  exact ⟨p', hp'⟩
let recs : ∀ n : ℕ, { p : State // Pre n p } :=
  fun n => Nat.rec ⟨baseState, hbase⟩
    (fun n ih => ⟨Classical.choose (mainstep n ih.1 ih.2), Classical.choose_spec (mainstep n ih.1 ih.2)⟩) n
let F : ℕ → State := fun n => (recs n).1
have HP : ∀ n, Pre n (F n) := by
  intro n
  exact (recs n).2
let x : ℕ → ℤ := fun n => (full (F (n + 1))).get ⟨n, by
  have hpx : Pre (n + 1) (F (n + 1)) := by exact HP (n + 1)
  unfold Pre at hpx
  rcases hpx with ⟨_, _, _, hlen, _, _, _, _, _⟩
  omega⟩
let stepRes : ∀ (n : ℕ) (p : State), Pre n p →
    {p' : State // Pre (n+1) p' ∧ prev p' = full p ∧ prevCut p' = cut p} := by
  intro n p hp
  unfold Pre at hp
  rcases hp with ⟨hpnd, hp_lt, hp_gt, hplen, hpfq, hpqprev, hprec, hpcut, hpsep⟩
  have hgtm : ∀ z ∈ full p, neg (n+1) < z := by
    intro z hz
    have hn : neg (n+1) < neg n := by
      dsimp [neg]
      omega
    exact lt_trans hn (hp_gt z hz)
  let dt := ProofSteps.diag_tail h hgen (full p) (cut p) (n+1) hpnd hp_lt hgtm
  let qq : List ℤ := Classical.choose dt
  let N' : ℕ := Classical.choose (Classical.choose_spec dt)
  let v : ℤ := Classical.choose (Classical.choose_spec (Classical.choose_spec dt))
  rcases Classical.choose_spec (Classical.choose_spec (Classical.choose_spec dt)) with
    ⟨hpref, hnd, hgrow, hqlt, hqgt, hvpos, hveq, hvnot, hNlt, hvlt, hsep⟩
  have hpref' : ∃ rest : List ℤ, qq = full p ++ rest := by
    simpa [qq] using hpref
  have hnd' : qq.Nodup := by
    simpa [qq] using hnd
  have hgrow' : (full p).length < qq.length := by
    simpa [qq] using hgrow
  have hqlt' : ∀ z ∈ qq, z < ((N' : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
    intro z hz
    simpa [qq, N'] using hqlt z hz
  have hqgt' : ∀ z ∈ qq, neg (n+1) < z := by
    intro z hz
    simpa [qq, neg] using hqgt z hz
  have hvpos' : (0 : ℤ) < v := by
    simpa [v] using hvpos
  have hveq' : v = h qq := by
    simpa [qq, v] using hveq
  have hvnot' : v ∉ qq := by
    simpa [qq, v] using hvnot
  have hNlt' : (cut p : ℤ) < (N' : ℤ) := by
    simpa [N'] using hNlt
  have hvlt' : v < (N' : ℤ) := by
    simpa [N', v] using hvlt
  have hsep' : ∀ z ∈ qq, z ∈ full p ∨ (cut p : ℤ) ≤ z := by
    intro z hz
    simpa [qq] using hsep z hz
  have hn0 : n + 1 ≠ 0 := by omega
  have hlast : last (n + 1) = [neg n] := by simp [last, hn0]
  let full' : List ℤ := qq ++ last (n+1)
  let p' : State := mk full' qq N' v (full p) (cut p)
  have hfull_eq_sing : full p' = qq ++ [neg n] := by
    simp only [p', full', full, mk]
    rw [hlast]
  have hq_gt_neg : ∀ z ∈ qq, neg n < z := by
    intro z hz
    rcases hsep' z hz with hzs | hzN
    · exact hp_gt z hzs
    · have hneg0 : neg n < 0 := by dsimp [neg]; omega
      have h0le : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (cut p : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.zero_le (cut p)
      have h0lez : (0 : ℤ) ≤ z := le_trans h0le hzN
      exact lt_of_lt_of_le hneg0 h0lez
  have hfull_nd : (full p').Nodup := by
    have hneg_nd : [neg n].Nodup := by simp
    have hdisj : List.Disjoint qq [neg n] := by
      intro z hz hzsing
      have hzneg : z = neg n := by simpa using hzsing
      have hzgt : neg n < z := hq_gt_neg z hz
      rw [hzneg] at hzgt
      exact (lt_irrefl (neg n) hzgt)
    rw [hfull_eq_sing]
    exact List.Nodup.append hnd' hneg_nd hdisj
  have hfull_lt : ∀ z ∈ full p', z < (cut p' : ℤ) := by
    intro z hz
    have hzm : z ∈ qq ++ [neg n] := by
      rw [hfull_eq_sing] at hz
      exact hz
    rw [List.mem_append] at hzm
    rcases hzm with hzq | hzsing
    · simpa [p', cut, mk] using hqlt' z hzq
    · have hzneg : z = neg n := by simpa using hzsing
      rw [hzneg]
      have hneg0 : neg n < 0 := by dsimp [neg]; omega
      have h0le : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (cut p : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.zero_le (cut p)
      have hnegcut : neg n < (cut p : ℤ) := lt_of_lt_of_le hneg0 h0le
      simpa [p', cut, mk] using (lt_trans hnegcut hNlt')
  have hfull_gt : ∀ z ∈ full p', neg (n+1) < z := by
    intro z hz
    have hzm : z ∈ qq ++ [neg n] := by
      rw [hfull_eq_sing] at hz
      exact hz
    rw [List.mem_append] at hzm
    rcases hzm with hzq | hzsing
    · exact hqgt' z hzq
    · have hzneg : z = neg n := by simpa using hzsing
      rw [hzneg]
      have hneglt : neg (n+1) < neg n := by dsimp [neg]; omega
      exact hneglt
  have hfull_len : n + 1 ≤ (full p').length := by
    rw [hfull_eq_sing]
    simp
    omega
  have hfull_eq : full p' = q p' ++ last (n+1) := by
    simp [p', full', full, q, mk]
  have hqprev : ∃ rest : List ℤ, q p' = prev p' ++ rest := by
    rcases hpref' with ⟨rest, hr⟩
    refine ⟨rest, ?_⟩
    simpa [p', q, prev, mk] using hr
  have hrec' : (n+1 = 0 ∨ (0 < recv p' ∧ recv p' = h (q p') ∧ recv p' ∉ q p' ∧ recv p' < (cut p' : ℤ))) := by
    right
    refine ⟨hvpos', ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · simpa [p', recv, q, mk] using hveq'
    · simpa [p', recv, q, mk] using hvnot'
    · simpa [p', recv, cut, mk] using hvlt'
  have hcut' : (n+1 = 0 ∨ prevCut p' < cut p') := by
    right
    have hNlt'' : cut p < N' := by exact_mod_cast hNlt'
    simpa [p', prevCut, cut, mk] using hNlt''
  have hsep'' : (n+1 = 0 ∨ ∀ z ∈ q p', z ∈ prev p' ∨ (prevCut p' : ℤ) ≤ z) := by
    right
    intro z hz
    have hz' : z ∈ qq := by simpa [p', q, mk] using hz
    rcases hsep' z hz' with hzs | hzN
    · left
      simpa [p', prev, mk] using hzs
    · right
      simpa [p', prevCut, mk] using hzN
  have hp' : Pre (n+1) p' := by
    exact ⟨hfull_nd, hfull_lt, hfull_gt, hfull_len, hfull_eq, hqprev, hrec', hcut', hsep''⟩
  exact ⟨p', hp', by simp [p', prev, mk], by simp [p', prevCut, mk]⟩
let recG : ∀ n : ℕ, { p : State // Pre n p } :=
  fun n => Nat.rec ⟨baseState, hbase⟩
    (fun n ih => ⟨(stepRes n ih.1 ih.2).1, (stepRes n ih.1 ih.2).2.1⟩) n
let G : ℕ → State := fun n => (recG n).1
have HPG : ∀ n, Pre n (G n) := by
  intro n
  exact (recG n).2
have hprevG : ∀ n, prev (G (n + 1)) = full (G n) := by
  intro n
  simpa [G, recG] using (stepRes n (G n) (HPG n)).2.2.1
have hprevCutG : ∀ n, prevCut (G (n + 1)) = cut (G n) := by
  intro n
  simpa [G, recG] using (stepRes n (G n) (HPG n)).2.2.2
have hprefix_step : ∀ k : ℕ, List.IsPrefix (full (G k)) (full (G (k + 1))) := by
  intro k
  have hpk := HPG (k + 1)
  unfold Pre at hpk
  rcases hpk with ⟨hpnd, hp_lt, hp_gt, hplen, hpfq, hpqprev, hprec, hpcut, hpsep⟩
  rcases hpqprev with ⟨rest, hr⟩
  have hqstep : q (G (k + 1)) = full (G k) ++ rest := by
    rw [hr, hprevG k]
  have hfullstep : full (G (k + 1)) = full (G k) ++ (rest ++ last (k + 1)) := by
    rw [hpfq, hqstep]
    simp [List.append_assoc]
  rw [hfullstep]
  exact List.prefix_append (full (G k)) (rest ++ last (k + 1))
have hprefix : ∀ a b : ℕ, a ≤ b → List.IsPrefix (full (G a)) (full (G b)) := by
  intro a b hab
  exact Nat.le_induction (m := a)
    (P := fun b _ => List.IsPrefix (full (G a)) (full (G b)))
    (List.prefix_refl (full (G a)))
    (fun k hk ih => List.IsPrefix.trans ih (hprefix_step k))
    b hab
let xG : ℕ → ℤ := fun n =>
  (full (G (n + 1))).get ⟨n, by
    have hp : Pre (n + 1) (G (n + 1)) := HPG (n + 1)
    unfold Pre at hp
    rcases hp with ⟨hnd, hlt, hgt, hlen, hfull, hq, hrec, hcut, hsep⟩
    omega⟩
refine ⟨xG, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
intro a b habx
by_cases hle : a ≤ b
have hprefa : List.IsPrefix (full (G (a+1))) (full (G (b+1))) := hprefix (a+1) (b+1) (by omega)
have hndb : (full (G (b+1))).Nodup := by
  have hpb := HPG (b+1)
  unfold Pre at hpb
  exact hpb.1
have hia : a < (full (G (a+1))).length := by
  have hpa := HPG (a+1)
  unfold Pre at hpa
  exact Nat.lt_of_succ_le hpa.2.2.2.1
have hlenb := List.IsPrefix.length_le hprefa
have hib : a < (full (G (b+1))).length := lt_of_lt_of_le hia hlenb
dsimp only [xG] at habx
have hga : (full (G (a+1))).get ⟨a, hia⟩ = (full (G (b+1))).get ⟨a, hib⟩ :=
  ProofSteps.prefix_get_eq (full (G (a+1))) (full (G (b+1))) hprefa ⟨a, hia⟩
have hb : b < (full (G (b+1))).length := by
  have hpb := HPG (b+1)
  unfold Pre at hpb
  exact Nat.lt_of_succ_le hpb.2.2.2.1
have hmain : (full (G (b+1))).get ⟨a, hib⟩ = (full (G (b+1))).get ⟨b, hb⟩ := by
  exact hga.symm.trans habx
exact congrArg Fin.val ((List.Nodup.get_inj_iff hndb).mp hmain)
have hba : b ≤ a := le_of_not_ge hle
have hprefb : List.IsPrefix (full (G (b+1))) (full (G (a+1))) := hprefix (b+1) (a+1) (by omega)
have hnda : (full (G (a+1))).Nodup := by
  have hpa := HPG (a+1)
  unfold Pre at hpa
  exact hpa.1
have hb : b < (full (G (b+1))).length := by
  have hpb := HPG (b+1)
  unfold Pre at hpb
  exact Nat.lt_of_succ_le hpb.2.2.2.1
have hlen := List.IsPrefix.length_le hprefb
have hbia : b < (full (G (a+1))).length := lt_of_lt_of_le hb hlen
have ha : a < (full (G (a+1))).length := by
  have hpa := HPG (a+1)
  unfold Pre at hpa
  exact Nat.lt_of_succ_le hpa.2.2.2.1
dsimp only [xG] at habx
have hgb : (full (G (b+1))).get ⟨b, hb⟩ = (full (G (a+1))).get ⟨b, hbia⟩ :=
  ProofSteps.prefix_get_eq (full (G (b+1))) (full (G (a+1))) hprefb ⟨b, hb⟩
have hmain : (full (G (a+1))).get ⟨b, hbia⟩ = (full (G (a+1))).get ⟨a, ha⟩ := by
  exact hgb.symm.trans habx.symm
exact (congrArg Fin.val ((List.Nodup.get_inj_iff hnda).mp hmain)).symm

  have hz_lt_v : e (i : ℕ) < v := by

intro z hz
rcases List.mem_ofFn.mp hz with ⟨i, hiz⟩
rw [← hiz]
by_cases hi_lt : (i : ℕ) < s.length
· have hmemi : s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩ ∈ s := List.get_mem s ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩
  have hgt : (-(n : ℤ) - 1) < s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩ := hs_gt (s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩) hmemi
  rw [hpre (i : ℕ) hi_lt]
  exact hgt
· have hi_ge : s.length ≤ (i : ℕ) := Nat.le_of_not_gt hi_lt

nodes.claim: There exists a sequence of good stages realizing the recursion, yielding an injective integer sequence x whose range is infinite, contains every negative point -n-1, and satisfies that for every stage n the generator outputs a positive point not in the limiting language at the stage's record time, with record times arbitrarily large.

For a good stage prefix s with cutoff N and lower bound avoiding the next negative point, the diag_step construction yields q extending s, nodup, length-growing, all below larger N', avoiding -n-1, plus the fresh positive record v equal to h q, not in q, and below N'; the cutoff strictly increases.
nodes.statement:
lemma ProofSteps.diag_core (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    (hgen : ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
      L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
          {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))
    (s : List ℤ) (N n : ℕ)
    (hs_nd : s.Nodup)
    (hs_lt : ∀ z ∈ s, z < (N : ℤ))
    (hs_gt : ∀ z ∈ s, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) < z) :
    ∃ q : List ℤ, ∃ N' : ℕ, ∃ v : ℤ,
      (∃ rest : List ℤ, q = s ++ rest) ∧
      q.Nodup ∧
      s.length < q.length ∧
      (∀ z ∈ q, z < (N' : ℤ)) ∧
      (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∉ q ∧
      0 < v ∧
      v = h q ∧
      v ∉ q ∧
      (N : ℤ) < (N' : ℤ) ∧
      v < (N' : ℤ)

rcases hp with ⟨hp_nd, hrest, hv_eq, hk, hv_not, hvN, hv0, hvN'⟩
have hNN' : (N : ℤ) < (N' : ℤ) := by omega
refine ⟨List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ)), N', v, hrest, hp_nd, ?_, ?_, ?_, hv0, hv_eq, hv_not, hNN', hvN'⟩
simpa [List.length_ofFn] using hsr
rcases hk with ⟨k, hkN, hek⟩
have hk_ge_s : s.length ≤ k := by
  by_contra hnot
  have hklt : k < s.length := Nat.lt_of_not_ge hnot
  have hmem_k : e k ∈ s := by
    rw [hpre k hklt]
    exact List.get_mem s ⟨k, hklt⟩
  have hltN_k : e k < (N : ℤ) := hs_lt (e k) hmem_k
  have : v < (N : ℤ) := by simpa [hek] using hltN_k
  omega
have hrk : r ≤ k := by
  by_contra hnot
  have hk_lt_r : k < r := Nat.lt_of_not_ge hnot
  have hmem_kp : v ∈ List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ)) := by
    rw [List.mem_ofFn]
    exact ⟨⟨k, hk_lt_r⟩, hek⟩

nodes.claim: For any sequence of lists with nested prefixes and nodupness, the diagonal nth element of the (n+1)th list is injective.

Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
nodes.statement:
theorem fcs76_collections_exist :
  ∃ C1 C2 : Set {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
    (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C1 →
      ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
        g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
    (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C2 →
      ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
        g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
    ¬ (∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
      ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ (C1 ∪ C2) →
        ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
          ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
              List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))

result.statement: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
result.proof: Take the nonnegative integers as points p_n = n and the negative integers as points m_n = −n−1. Let C₁ be the languages whose carrier contains some tail {p_{N+j} : j ≥ 0}, and C₂ the languages whose carrier contains every m_n. The sequence (p_n) is injective and generates each member of C₁ after its cutoff, giving non-uniform sample-free generation; the sequence (m_n) generates each member of C₂ from time zero, giving uniform sample-free generation. Freshness reduces to membership together with absence of earlier repetition, which holds because both sequences are injective. For the negative clause, assume some sample-based generator G generates the union in the limit. Build nested finite injective prefixes together with strictly increasing cutoffs: given a stage prefix s and cutoff N, enumerate s followed by the positive tail from N; this enumeration belongs to C₁, so G must eventually output a fresh value, which cannot be a previously listed element and hence is some p_k with k ≥ N. Extend the prefix by that observed enumeration prefix and append the next negative point m_n, choosing a fresh larger cutoff so that p_k occurs neither in the new prefix nor in its future positive tail. Induction shows p_k is never reproduced later. The nested prefixes converge to an injective sequence x whose range is infinite and contains every negative point, so it is the carrier of a language in C₂ that x enumerates. At each stage time the prefix of x agrees with the recorded stage prefix, so G outputs p_k, which lies outside this limiting language; since these failures occur arbitrarily late, G fails to generate in the limit, a contradiction. Hence the union is not generatable in the limit, and the constructed collections witness the claim.

· exact hv_eq

· simpa [q] using hsr

  have hi_r : (i : ℕ) < r := i.isLt
  have hi_lt_k : (i : ℕ) < k := by omega
  have hv_tail : v = (N : ℤ) + ((k : ℤ) - (s.length : ℤ)) := by

  have hz_lt_v : e (i : ℕ) < v := by

nodes.claim: There exists a sequence of good stages realizing the recursion, yielding an injective integer sequence x whose range is infinite, contains every negative point -n-1, and satisfies that for every stage n the generator outputs a positive point not in the limiting language at the stage's record time, with record times arbitrarily large.

For a good stage prefix s with cutoff N and lower bound avoiding the next negative point, the diag_step construction yields q extending s, nodup, length-growing, all below larger N', avoiding -n-1, plus the fresh positive record v equal to h q, not in q, and below N'; the cutoff strictly increases.

lemma ProofSteps.diag_core (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    (hgen : ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
      L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
          {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))
    (s : List ℤ) (N n : ℕ)
    (hs_nd : s.Nodup)
    (hs_lt : ∀ z ∈ s, z < (N : ℤ))
    (hs_gt : ∀ z ∈ s, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) < z) :
    ∃ q : List ℤ, ∃ N' : ℕ, ∃ v : ℤ,
      (∃ rest : List ℤ, q = s ++ rest) ∧
      q.Nodup ∧
      s.length < q.length ∧
      (∀ z ∈ q, z < (N' : ℤ)) ∧
      (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∉ q ∧
      0 < v ∧
      v = h q ∧
      v ∉ q ∧
      (N : ℤ) < (N' : ℤ) ∧
      v < (N' : ℤ)

simpa [List.length_ofFn] using hsr

  have hklt : k < s.length := Nat.lt_of_not_ge hnot

  exact hv_not hmem_kp
intro z hz
rcases List.mem_ofFn.mp hz with ⟨i, hiz⟩
rw [← hiz]
by_cases hi_lt : (i : ℕ) < s.length
· have hmemi : s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩ ∈ s := List.get_mem s ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩
  have hltN : s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩ < (N : ℤ) := hs_lt (s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩) hmemi

    omega
  omega
intro hmem

· have hmemi : s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩ ∈ s := List.get_mem s ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩
  have hgt : -(n : ℤ) - 1 < s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩ := hs_gt (s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩) hmemi
  rw [hpre (i : ℕ) hi_lt] at hiz
  omega

rcases ProofSteps.diag_step h hgen s N hs_nd hs_lt with ⟨e, N', r, v, hpre, htail, hsr, hp⟩
rcases hp with ⟨hp_nd, hrest, hv_eq, hk, hv_not, hvN, hv0, hvN'⟩
refine ⟨List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ)), N', hrest, hp_nd, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
simpa [List.length_ofFn] using hsr
rcases hk with ⟨k, hkN, hek⟩
have hk_ge_s : s.length ≤ k := by
  by_contra hnot
  have hklt : k < s.length := Nat.lt_of_not_ge hnot
  have hmem_k : e k ∈ s := by
    rw [hpre k hklt]
    exact List.get_mem s ⟨k, hklt⟩
  have hltN_k : e k < (N : ℤ) := hs_lt (e k) hmem_k
  have : v < (N : ℤ) := by simpa [hek] using hltN_k
  omega
have hrk : r ≤ k := by
  by_contra hnot
  have hk_lt_r : k < r := Nat.lt_of_not_ge hnot
  have hmem_kp : v ∈ List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ)) := by
    rw [List.mem_ofFn]
    exact ⟨⟨k, hk_lt_r⟩, hek⟩
  exact hv_not hmem_kp
intro z hz
rcases List.mem_ofFn.mp hz with ⟨i, hiz⟩
rw [← hiz]
by_cases hi_lt : (i : ℕ) < s.length
· have hmemi : s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩ ∈ s := List.get_mem s ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩
  have hltN : s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩ < (N : ℤ) := hs_lt (s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩) hmemi
  rw [hpre (i : ℕ) hi_lt]
  omega
· have hi_ge : s.length ≤ (i : ℕ) := Nat.le_of_not_gt hi_lt
  have hi_r : (i : ℕ) < r := i.isLt
  have hi_lt_k : (i : ℕ) < k := by omega
  have hz_lt_v : e (i : ℕ) < v := by
    rw [htail (i : ℕ) hi_ge]
    rw [← hek]
    rw [htail k hk_ge_s]
    omega
  omega
intro hmem
rcases List.mem_ofFn.mp hmem with ⟨i, hiz⟩
by_cases hi_lt : (i : ℕ) < s.length
· have hmemi : s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩ ∈ s := List.get_mem s ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩
  have hgt : -(n : ℤ) - 1 < s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩ := hs_gt (s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩) hmemi
  rw [hpre (i : ℕ) hi_lt] at hiz
  omega
· have hi_ge : s.length ≤ (i : ℕ) := Nat.le_of_not_gt hi_lt
  rw [htail (i : ℕ) hi_ge] at hiz
  omega

nodes.claim: For every N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) is the range of i ↦ (N + i : ℤ), and that range is infinite.
nodes.body:
ext x
constructor
rintro hx
have hx' : (N : ℤ) ≤ x := by simpa [Set.mem_Ici] using hx
let i : ℕ := (x - (N : ℤ)).toNat
refine ⟨i, ?_⟩
change (N : ℤ) + (i : ℤ) = x
have hnonneg : 0 ≤ x - (N : ℤ) := by omega
have hcast : (i : ℤ) = x - (N : ℤ) := by
  exact Int.toNat_of_nonneg hnonneg
omega
rintro ⟨j, rfl⟩
simpa [Set.mem_Ici] using (by omega : (N : ℤ) ≤ (N : ℤ) + (j : ℤ))

nodes.claim: Given generator h and its union property, a finite injective prefix f : Fin l → ℤ and cutoff N, there is a longer finite injective prefix f' starting with f, a fresh positive value p_k with k ≥ N achieved by h on the stage enumeration, and a larger cutoff N' avoiding p_k on future positive tails.
nodes.body:
skip
let e : ℕ → ℤ := fun n => if hln : n < s.length then s.get ⟨n, hln⟩ else (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ)
have h1 : ∀ (n : ℕ) (hlt : n < s.length), e n = s.get ⟨n, hlt⟩ := by
  intro n hlt
  simp [e, hlt]
have h2 : ∀ n : ℕ, s.length ≤ n → e n = (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ) := by
  intro n hn
  simp [e, hn, not_lt_of_ge hn]
have hci : Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ Set.range e := ProofSteps.stage_enum_range_ci s N e h2
have hinf : (Set.range e).Infinite := ProofSteps.stage_enum_range_infinite s N e h2
let L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} := ⟨Set.range e, hinf⟩
have hC1 : L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
    {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) := by
  left
  exact ⟨N, hci⟩
obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := hgen L hC1 e rfl
let r : ℕ := max t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1))
have hsr : s.length < r := by
  dsimp [r]
  exact Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le (Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le (Nat.lt_succ_self s.length) (Nat.le_max_left (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
    (Nat.le_max_right t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
have hsr_le : s.length ≤ r := Nat.le_of_lt hsr
have hNr : N ≤ r := by
  dsimp [r]
  exact Nat.le_trans (Nat.le_trans (Nat.le_succ N) (Nat.le_max_right (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
    (Nat.le_max_right t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
have htr : h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ Set.range e ∧
    h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ))) ∉ List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ)) :=
    ht r (Nat.le_max_left t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
let p : List ℤ := List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ))
let v : ℤ := h p
rcases htr.1 with ⟨m, hm⟩
have hmv : e m = v := by
  simpa [v, p] using hm
have hv_notin_p : v ∉ p := by
  simpa [p, v] using htr.2
have hm_ge_r : r ≤ m := by
  by_contra hcontra
  have hmr : m < r := Nat.lt_of_not_ge hcontra
  have hmem : e m ∈ p := by
    dsimp [p]
    rw [List.mem_ofFn]
    exact ⟨⟨m, hmr⟩, rfl⟩
  exact hv_notin_p (hmv ▸ hmem)
have hm_ge_s : s.length ≤ m := le_trans hsr_le hm_ge_r
have hm_tail : e m = (N + (m - s.length) : ℤ) := h2 m hm_ge_s
have hv_tail : v = (N + (m - s.length) : ℤ) := by
  rw [← hmv, hm_tail]
have hNm : N ≤ m := le_trans hNr hm_ge_r
have hk : ∃ k : ℕ, N ≤ k ∧ e k = v := ⟨m, hNm, hmv⟩
let N' : ℕ := N + (m - s.length) + 1
have hv_ge_N : (N : ℤ) ≤ v := by
  rw [hv_tail]
  exact_mod_cast Nat.le_add_right N (m - s.length)
have hm_gt_s : s.length < m := lt_of_lt_of_le hsr hm_ge_r
have hv_pos : 0 < v := by
  rw [hv_tail]
  have hN_nonneg : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (N : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.zero_le N
  omega
have hv_lt_N' : v < (N' : ℤ) := by
  rw [hv_tail]
  dsimp [N']
  omega
have hinj_fin : Function.Injective (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ)) := by
  intro i j hij
  change e (i : ℕ) = e (j : ℕ) at hij
  apply Fin.ext
  by_cases hi : (i : ℕ) < s.length
  · by_cases hj : (j : ℕ) < s.length
    · have hgeti : e (i : ℕ) = s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩ := h1 (i : ℕ) hi
      have hgetj : e (j : ℕ) = s.get ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩ := h1 (j : ℕ) hj
      have hsij : s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩ = s.get ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩ := by
        rw [← hgeti, ← hgetj]
        exact hij
      have hfin : (⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩ : Fin s.length) = ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩ :=
        (hs_nd.get_inj_iff).mp hsij
      exact congrArg (fun x : Fin s.length => (x : ℕ)) hfin
    · have hj_ge : s.length ≤ (j : ℕ) := Nat.le_of_not_gt hj
      have hi_ltN : e (i : ℕ) < (N : ℤ) := by
        rw [h1 (i : ℕ) hi]
        exact hs_lt (s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩) (List.get_mem s ⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩)
      have hj_geN : (N : ℤ) ≤ e (j : ℕ) := by
        rw [h2 (j : ℕ) hj_ge]
        exact_mod_cast Nat.le_add_right N ((j : ℕ) - s.length)
      omega
  · have hi_ge : s.length ≤ (i : ℕ) := Nat.le_of_not_gt hi
    by_cases hj : (j : ℕ) < s.length
    · have hj_ltN : e (j : ℕ) < (N : ℤ) := by
        rw [h1 (j : ℕ) hj]
        exact hs_lt (s.get ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩) (List.get_mem s ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩)
      have hi_geN : (N : ℤ) ≤ e (i : ℕ) := by
        rw [h2 (i : ℕ) hi_ge]
        exact_mod_cast Nat.le_add_right N ((i : ℕ) - s.length)
      omega
    · have hj_ge : s.length ≤ (j : ℕ) := Nat.le_of_not_gt hj
      rw [h2 (i : ℕ) hi_ge, h2 (j : ℕ) hj_ge] at hij
      omega
have hp_nd : p.Nodup := by
  dsimp [p]
  rw [List.nodup_ofFn]
  exact hinj_fin
have hp_take : List.take s.length p = s := by
  apply List.ext_getElem
  · simp [p, List.length_take, List.length_ofFn]
    omega
  · intro i hi₁ hi₂
    simp [p, List.getElem_take, List.getElem_ofFn]
    exact h1 i hi₂
have hp_extend : ∃ rest : List ℤ, p = s ++ rest := by
  refine ⟨List.drop s.length p, ?_⟩
  calc
    p = List.take s.length p ++ List.drop s.length p := (List.take_append_drop s.length p).symm
    _ = s ++ List.drop s.length p := by rw [hp_take]

refine ⟨e, N', r, v, h1, h2, hsr, hp_nd, hp_extend, rfl, hk,
    hv_notin_p, hv_ge_N, hv_pos, hv_lt_N'⟩

nodes.claim: For lists l₁ l₂ and a prefix proof h : l₁ <+: l₂, the Fin-indexed get of l₁ at i equals the get of l₂ at the same natural index, with the proof transported by IsPrefix.length_le.

lemma ProofSteps.prefix_get_eq {α} (l₁ l₂ : List α)
    (hpref : List.IsPrefix l₁ l₂) (i : Fin l₁.length) :
    l₁.get i = l₂.get ⟨i.1, lt_of_lt_of_le i.2 (List.IsPrefix.length_le hpref)⟩

nodes.claim: For any sequence of lists with nested prefixes and nodupness, the diagonal nth element of the (n+1)th list is injective.
nodes.statement:
lemma ProofSteps.diag_prefix_injective {α : Type} (l : ℕ → List α)
    (hprefix : ∀ a b : ℕ, a ≤ b → List.IsPrefix (l a) (l b))
    (hnd : ∀ k : ℕ, (l k).Nodup)
    (hlen : ∀ n : ℕ, n < (l (n+1)).length) :
    Function.Injective (fun n : ℕ => (l (n+1)).get ⟨n, hlen n⟩)
nodes.body:
by
    intro a b hab
    by_cases hle : a ≤ b
    · have hp : List.IsPrefix (l (a+1)) (l (b+1)) := hprefix (a+1) (b+1) (Nat.succ_le_succ hle)
      have hget : (l (b+1)).get ⟨a, lt_of_lt_of_le (hlen a) (List.IsPrefix.length_le hp)⟩ =
          (l (b+1)).get ⟨b, hlen b⟩ := by
        exact (ProofSteps.prefix_get_eq (l (a+1)) (l (b+1)) hp ⟨a, hlen a⟩).symm.trans hab
      have hfin := (List.Nodup.get_inj_iff (hnd (b+1))).mp hget
      simpa using congrArg Fin.val hfin
    · have hba : b ≤ a := le_of_not_ge hle
      have hp : List.IsPrefix (l (b+1)) (l (a+1)) := hprefix (b+1) (a+1) (Nat.succ_le_succ hba)
      have hget : (l (a+1)).get ⟨b, lt_of_lt_of_le (hlen b) (List.IsPrefix.length_le hp)⟩ =
          (l (a+1)).get ⟨a, hlen a⟩ := by
        exact (ProofSteps.prefix_get_eq (l (b+1)) (l (a+1)) hp ⟨b, hlen b⟩).symm.trans hab.symm
      have hfin := (List.Nodup.get_inj_iff (hnd (a+1))).mp hget
      simpa using (congrArg Fin.val hfin).symm

nodes.claim: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
nodes.statement:
theorem fcs76_collections_exist :
  ∃ C1 C2 : Set {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
    (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C1 →
      ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
        g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
    (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C2 →
      ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
        g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
    ¬ (∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
      ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ (C1 ∪ C2) →
        ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
          ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
              List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))

nodes.claim: Given generator h and its union property, a finite injective prefix f : Fin l → ℤ and cutoff N, there is a longer finite injective prefix f' starting with f, a fresh positive value p_k with k ≥ N achieved by h on the stage enumeration, and a larger cutoff N' avoiding p_k on future positive tails.
nodes.proof_hint: Construct the stage enumeration by pasting f and the positive tail from N; define the resulting infinite language L as its range; prove L lies in C1 and apply hgen; the obtained fresh integer is a positive tail element p_k not in the earlier prefix; extend f by the enumeration prefix through time t and append the next negative point, then choose N' = k+1.

nodes.claim: For a good stage prefix s with cutoff N and lower bound m_n, the diag_step construction yields q extending s, nodup, growing, below a larger cutoff N', all entries above m_n, plus the fresh positive record v = h q not in q and below N'.
nodes.proof_hint: rcases ProofSteps.diag_step; let q = List.ofFn e r; derive upper bound by showing r <= k from v notin q, and lower bound from the prefix/tail description with hs_gt and nonnegativity; use omega for the cutoff comparisons.

nodes.claim: For a good stage prefix s with cutoff N and lower bound avoiding the next negative point, the diag_step construction yields q extending s, nodup, length-growing, all below larger N', avoiding -n-1, plus the fresh positive record v equal to h q, not in q, and below N'; the cutoff strictly increases.
nodes.proof_hint: rcases ProofSteps.diag_step into e,N',r,v; take q = List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e i); copy the diag_next_spec upper and avoidance arguments, and retain hv_eq, hv_not, hv0, hvN' plus prove N<N' from N≤v and v<N'.

nodes.claim: For a good stage prefix s and cutoff N with lower bound -n, the diag_step construction produces a finite prefix q extending s by at least one element, nodup, all entries below a strictly larger cutoff N', and avoiding the next negative point -n-1.
nodes.proof_hint: rcases ProofSteps.diag_step into e,N',r,v; take q = List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e i); use the prefix-extension, nodup, acuteness and v<N' facts plus hs_low to derive all bounds by omega.

nodes.claim: For a good stage prefix s with cutoff N and lower bound -n-1, the diag_step construction yields q extending s, nodup, growing, all below a strictly larger N', all above -n-1, a fresh positive record v = h q with v not in q and below N', and every entry of q lies either in s or is at least N.
nodes.proof_hint: Rcases ProofSteps.diag_step; take q = List.ofFn e r; upper bound by case analysis on the index using r ≤ k (from v notin q) and the piecewise description, lower bound from s lower and nonnegative tails, and tail separation directly from the piecewise description.

nodes.claim: For lists l₁ l₂ and a prefix proof h : l₁ <+: l₂, the Fin-indexed get of l₁ at i equals the get of l₂ at the same natural index, with the proof transported by IsPrefix.length_le.
nodes.proof_hint: rw both sides with List.get_eq_getElem, then apply List.IsPrefix.getElem.

nodes.claim: For any sequence of lists with nested prefixes and nodupness, the diagonal nth element of the (n+1)th list is injective.
nodes.proof_hint: Use the established prefix get equality and List.Nodup.get_inj_iff; split on whether a ≤ b and run the symmetric argument for the other case.

nodes.claim: There exists a sequence of good stages realizing the recursion, yielding an injective integer sequence x whose range is infinite, contains every negative point -n-1, and satisfies that for every stage n the generator outputs a positive point not in the limiting language at the stage's record time, with record times arbitrarily large.

lemma ProofSteps.diag_full (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    (hgen : ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
      L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
          {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))
    (s : List ℤ) (N n : ℕ)
    (hs_nd : s.Nodup)
    (hs_lt : ∀ z ∈ s, z < (N : ℤ))
    (hs_gt : ∀ z ∈ s, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) < z) :
    ∃ q : List ℤ, ∃ N' : ℕ, ∃ v : ℤ,
      (∃ rest : List ℤ, q = s ++ rest) ∧

      s.length < q.length ∧
      (∀ z ∈ q, z < (N' : ℤ)) ∧
      (∀ z ∈ q, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) < z) ∧
      0 < v ∧
      v = h q ∧
      v ∉ q ∧
      (N : ℤ) < (N' : ℤ) ∧

let neg : ℕ → ℤ := fun n => (-(n : ℤ) - 1)
let last : ℕ → List ℤ := fun n => if n = 0 then [] else [neg (n-1)]
let State := ((List ℤ × List ℤ) × (ℕ × ℤ)) × (List ℤ × ℕ)
let full : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.1
let q : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.2
let cut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.1.2.1
let recv : State → ℤ := fun p => p.1.2.2
let prev : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.2.1
let prevCut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.2.2
let mk : List ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → State :=
  fun f qq c r p pc => (((f, qq), (c, r)), (p, pc))
let Pre : ℕ → State → Prop := fun n p =>
  (full p).Nodup ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), z < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), neg n < z) ∧
  n ≤ (full p).length ∧
  (full p) = (q p) ++ (last n) ∧
  (∃ rest : List ℤ, (q p) = (prev p) ++ rest) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (0 < (recv p) ∧ (recv p) = h (q p) ∧ (recv p) ∉ (q p) ∧ (recv p) < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ))) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (prevCut p) < (cut p)) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (∀ z ∈ (q p), z ∈ (prev p) ∨ ((prevCut p : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ z))
skip
let baseState : State := mk [] [] 0 0 [] 0
have hbase : Pre 0 baseState := by
  simp [Pre, baseState, full, q, cut, recv, prev, prevCut, mk, last]
have mainstep : ∀ (n : ℕ) (p : State), Pre n p → ∃ p' : State, Pre (n+1) p' := by
  intro n p hp
  unfold Pre at hp
  rcases hp with ⟨hpnd, hp_lt, hp_gt, hplen, hpfq, hpqprev, hprec, hpcut, hpsep⟩
  have hgtm : ∀ z ∈ full p, neg (n+1) < z := by
    intro z hz
    have hn : neg (n+1) < neg n := by
      dsimp [neg]
      omega
    exact lt_trans hn (hp_gt z hz)
  rcases ProofSteps.diag_tail h hgen (full p) (cut p) (n+1) hpnd hp_lt hgtm with
    ⟨qq, N', v, hpref, hnd, hgrow, hqlt, hqgt, hvpos, hveq, hvnot, hNlt, hvlt, hsep⟩
  have hn0 : n + 1 ≠ 0 := by omega
  have hlast : last (n + 1) = [neg n] := by simp [last, hn0]
  let full' : List ℤ := qq ++ last (n+1)
  let p' : State := mk full' qq N' v (full p) (cut p)
  have hfull_eq_sing : full p' = qq ++ [neg n] := by
    simp only [p', full', full, mk]
    rw [hlast]
  have hq_gt_neg : ∀ z ∈ qq, neg n < z := by
    intro z hz
    rcases hsep z hz with hzs | hzN
    · exact hp_gt z hzs
    · have hneg0 : neg n < 0 := by dsimp [neg]; omega
      have h0le : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (cut p : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.zero_le (cut p)
      have h0lez : (0 : ℤ) ≤ z := le_trans h0le hzN
      exact lt_of_lt_of_le hneg0 h0lez
  have hfull_nd : (full p').Nodup := by
    have hneg_nd : [neg n].Nodup := by simp
    have hdisj : List.Disjoint qq [neg n] := by
      intro z hz hzsing
      have hzneg : z = neg n := by simpa using hzsing
      have hzgt : neg n < z := hq_gt_neg z hz
      rw [hzneg] at hzgt
      exact (lt_irrefl (neg n) hzgt)
    rw [hfull_eq_sing]
    exact List.Nodup.append hnd hneg_nd hdisj

let neg : ℕ → ℤ := fun n => (-(n : ℤ) - 1)
let last : ℕ → List ℤ := fun n => if n = 0 then [] else [neg (n-1)]
let State := ((List ℤ × List ℤ) × (ℕ × ℤ)) × (List ℤ × ℕ)
let full : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.1
let q : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.2
let cut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.1.2.1
let recv : State → ℤ := fun p => p.1.2.2
let prev : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.2.1
let prevCut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.2.2
let mk : List ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → State :=
  fun f qq c r p pc => (((f, qq), (c, r)), (p, pc))
let Pre : ℕ → State → Prop := fun n p =>
  (full p).Nodup ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), z < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), neg n < z) ∧
  n ≤ (full p).length ∧
  (full p) = (q p) ++ (last n) ∧
  (∃ rest : List ℤ, (q p) = (prev p) ++ rest) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (0 < (recv p) ∧ (recv p) = h (q p) ∧ (recv p) ∉ (q p) ∧ (recv p) < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ))) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (prevCut p) < (cut p)) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (∀ z ∈ (q p), z ∈ (prev p) ∨ ((prevCut p : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ z))
skip
let baseState : State := mk [] [] 0 0 [] 0
have hbase : Pre 0 baseState := by
  simp [Pre, baseState, full, q, cut, recv, prev, prevCut, mk, last]
have mainstep : ∀ (n : ℕ) (p : State), Pre n p → ∃ p' : State, Pre (n+1) p' := by
  intro n p hp
  unfold Pre at hp
  rcases hp with ⟨hpnd, hp_lt, hp_gt, hplen, hpfq, hpqprev, hprec, hpcut, hpsep⟩
  have hgtm : ∀ z ∈ full p, neg (n+1) < z := by
    intro z hz
    have hn : neg (n+1) < neg n := by
      dsimp [neg]
      omega
    exact lt_trans hn (hp_gt z hz)
  rcases ProofSteps.diag_tail h hgen (full p) (cut p) (n+1) hpnd hp_lt hgtm with
    ⟨qq, N', v, hpref, hnd, hgrow, hqlt, hqgt, hvpos, hveq, hvnot, hNlt, hvlt, hsep⟩
  have hn0 : n + 1 ≠ 0 := by omega
  have hlast : last (n + 1) = [neg n] := by simp [last, hn0]
  let full' : List ℤ := qq ++ last (n+1)
  let p' : State := mk full' qq N' v (full p) (cut p)
  have hfull_eq_sing : full p' = qq ++ [neg n] := by
    simp only [p', full', full, mk]
    rw [hlast]
  have hq_gt_neg : ∀ z ∈ qq, neg n < z := by
    intro z hz
    rcases hsep z hz with hzs | hzN
    · exact hp_gt z hzs
    · have hneg0 : neg n < 0 := by dsimp [neg]; omega
      have h0le : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (cut p : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.zero_le (cut p)
      have h0lez : (0 : ℤ) ≤ z := le_trans h0le hzN
      exact lt_of_lt_of_le hneg0 h0lez
  have hfull_nd : (full p').Nodup := by
    have hneg_nd : [neg n].Nodup := by simp
    have hdisj : List.Disjoint qq [neg n] := by
      intro z hz hzsing
      have hzneg : z = neg n := by simpa using hzsing
      have hzgt : neg n < z := hq_gt_neg z hz
      rw [hzneg] at hzgt
      exact (lt_irrefl (neg n) hzgt)
    rw [hfull_eq_sing]
    exact List.Nodup.append hnd hneg_nd hdisj
  have hfull_lt : ∀ z ∈ full p', z < (cut p' : ℤ) := by
    intro z hz
    have hzm : z ∈ qq ++ [neg n] := by
      rw [hfull_eq_sing] at hz
      exact hz
    rw [List.mem_append] at hzm
    rcases hzm with hzq | hzsing
    · simpa [p', cut, mk] using hqlt z hzq
    · have hzneg : z = neg n := by simpa using hzsing
      rw [hzneg]
      have hneg0 : neg n < 0 := by dsimp [neg]; omega
      have h0le : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (cut p : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.zero_le (cut p)
      have hnegcut : neg n < (cut p : ℤ) := lt_of_lt_of_le hneg0 h0le
      simpa [p', cut, mk] using (lt_trans hnegcut hNlt)
  have hfull_gt : ∀ z ∈ full p', neg (n+1) < z := by
    intro z hz
    have hzm : z ∈ qq ++ [neg n] := by
      rw [hfull_eq_sing] at hz
      exact hz
    rw [List.mem_append] at hzm
    rcases hzm with hzq | hzsing
    · exact hqgt z hzq
    · have hzneg : z = neg n := by simpa using hzsing
      rw [hzneg]
      have hneglt : neg (n+1) < neg n := by dsimp [neg]; omega
      exact hneglt
  have hfull_len : n + 1 ≤ (full p').length := by
    rw [hfull_eq_sing]
    simp
    omega
  have hfull_eq : full p' = q p' ++ last (n+1) := by
    simp [p', full', full, q, mk]
  have hqprev : ∃ rest : List ℤ, q p' = prev p' ++ rest := by
    rcases hpref with ⟨rest, hr⟩
    refine ⟨rest, ?_⟩
    simpa [p', q, prev, mk] using hr
  have hrec' : (n+1 = 0 ∨ (0 < recv p' ∧ recv p' = h (q p') ∧ recv p' ∉ q p' ∧ recv p' < (cut p' : ℤ))) := by
    right
    refine ⟨hvpos, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · simpa [p', recv, q, mk] using hveq
    · simpa [p', recv, q, mk] using hvnot
    · simpa [p', recv, cut, mk] using hvlt
  have hcut' : (n+1 = 0 ∨ prevCut p' < cut p') := by
    right
    have hNlt' : cut p < N' := by exact_mod_cast hNlt
    simpa [p', prevCut, cut, mk] using hNlt'
  have hsep' : (n+1 = 0 ∨ ∀ z ∈ q p', z ∈ prev p' ∨ (prevCut p' : ℤ) ≤ z) := by
    right
    intro z hz
    have hz' : z ∈ qq := by simpa [p', q, mk] using hz
    rcases hsep z hz' with hzs | hzN
    · left
      simpa [p', prev, mk] using hzs
    · right
      simpa [p', prevCut, mk] using hzN
  have hp' : Pre (n+1) p' := by
    exact ⟨hfull_nd, hfull_lt, hfull_gt, hfull_len, hfull_eq, hqprev, hrec', hcut', hsep'⟩
  exact ⟨p', hp'⟩
let recs : ∀ n : ℕ, { p : State // Pre n p } :=
  fun n => Nat.rec ⟨baseState, hbase⟩
    (fun n ih => ⟨Classical.choose (mainstep n ih.1 ih.2), Classical.choose_spec (mainstep n ih.1 ih.2)⟩) n
let F : ℕ → State := fun n => (recs n).1
have HP : ∀ n, Pre n (F n) := by
  intro n
  exact (recs n).2
let x : ℕ → ℤ := fun n => (full (F (n + 1))).get ⟨n, by
  have hpx : Pre (n + 1) (F (n + 1)) := by exact HP (n + 1)
  unfold Pre at hpx
  rcases hpx with ⟨_, _, _, hlen, _, _, _, _, _⟩
  omega⟩

    {p' : State // Pre (n+1) p' ∧ prev p' = full p ∧ prevCut p' = cut p} := by
  intro n p hp
  unfold Pre at hp
  rcases hp with ⟨hpnd, hp_lt, hp_gt, hplen, hpfq, hpqprev, hprec, hpcut, hpsep⟩

    intro z hz
    have hn : neg (n+1) < neg n := by
      dsimp [neg]
      omega

  let dt := ProofSteps.diag_tail h hgen (full p) (cut p) (n+1) hpnd hp_lt hgtm
  let qq : List ℤ := Classical.choose dt
  let N' : ℕ := Classical.choose (Classical.choose_spec dt)

result.statement: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
result.proof: Take the nonnegative integers as points p_n = n and the negative integers as points m_n = −n−1. Let C₁ be the languages whose carrier contains some tail {p_{N+j} : j ≥ 0}, and C₂ the languages whose carrier contains every m_n. The sequence (p_n) is injective and generates each member of C₁ after its cutoff, giving non-uniform sample-free generation; the sequence (m_n) generates each member of C₂ from time zero, giving uniform sample-free generation. Freshness reduces to membership together with absence of earlier repetition, which holds because both sequences are injective. For the negative clause, assume some sample-based generator G generates the union in the limit. Build nested finite injective prefixes together with strictly increasing cutoffs: given a stage prefix s and cutoff N, enumerate s followed by the positive tail from N; this enumeration belongs to C₁, so G must eventually output a fresh value, which cannot be a previously listed element and hence is some p_k with k ≥ N. Extend the prefix by that observed enumeration prefix and append the next negative point m_n, choosing a fresh larger cutoff so that p_k occurs neither in the new prefix nor in its future positive tail. Induction shows p_k is never reproduced later. The nested prefixes converge to an injective sequence x whose range is infinite and contains every negative point, so it is the carrier of a language in C₂ that x enumerates. At each stage time the prefix of x agrees with the recorded stage prefix, so G outputs p_k, which lies outside this limiting language; since these failures occur arbitrarily late, G fails to generate in the limit, a contradiction. Hence the union is not generatable in the limit, and the constructed collections witness the claim.

  (∀ z ∈ (full p), z < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧

let neg : ℕ → ℤ := fun n => (-(n : ℤ) - 1)
let last : ℕ → List ℤ := fun n => if n = 0 then [] else [neg (n-1)]
let State := ((List ℤ × List ℤ) × (ℕ × ℤ)) × (List ℤ × ℕ)
let full : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.1
let q : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.2
let cut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.1.2.1
let recv : State → ℤ := fun p => p.1.2.2
let prev : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.2.1
let prevCut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.2.2
let mk : List ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → State :=
  fun f qq c r p pc => (((f, qq), (c, r)), (p, pc))
let Pre : ℕ → State → Prop := fun n p =>
  (full p).Nodup ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), z < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), neg n < z) ∧
  n ≤ (full p).length ∧
  (full p) = (q p) ++ (last n) ∧
  (∃ rest : List ℤ, (q p) = (prev p) ++ rest) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (0 < (recv p) ∧ (recv p) = h (q p) ∧ (recv p) ∉ (q p) ∧ (recv p) < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ))) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (prevCut p) < (cut p)) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (∀ z ∈ (q p), z ∈ (prev p) ∨ ((prevCut p : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ z))

  simp [Pre, baseState, full, q, cut, recv, prev, prevCut, mk, last]
have mainstep : ∀ (n : ℕ) (p : State), Pre n p → ∃ p' : State, Pre (n+1) p' := by
  intro n p hp
  unfold Pre at hp
  rcases hp with ⟨hpnd, hp_lt, hp_gt, hplen, hpfq, hpqprev, hprec, hpcut, hpsep⟩
  have hgtm : ∀ z ∈ full p, neg (n+1) < z := by
    intro z hz
    have hn : neg (n+1) < neg n := by
      dsimp [neg]
      omega
    exact lt_trans hn (hp_gt z hz)
  rcases ProofSteps.diag_tail h hgen (full p) (cut p) (n+1) hpnd hp_lt hgtm with
    ⟨qq, N', v, hpref, hnd, hgrow, hqlt, hqgt, hvpos, hveq, hvnot, hNlt, hvlt, hsep⟩
  have hn0 : n + 1 ≠ 0 := by omega
  have hlast : last (n + 1) = [neg n] := by simp [last, hn0]
  let full' : List ℤ := qq ++ last (n+1)
  let p' : State := mk full' qq N' v (full p) (cut p)
  have hfull_eq_sing : full p' = qq ++ [neg n] := by
    simp only [p', full', full, mk]
    rw [hlast]
  have hq_gt_neg : ∀ z ∈ qq, neg n < z := by
    intro z hz
    rcases hsep z hz with hzs | hzN
    · exact hp_gt z hzs
    · have hneg0 : neg n < 0 := by dsimp [neg]; omega
      have h0le : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (cut p : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.zero_le (cut p)
      have h0lez : (0 : ℤ) ≤ z := le_trans h0le hzN
      exact lt_of_lt_of_le hneg0 h0lez
  have hfull_nd : (full p').Nodup := by
    have hneg_nd : [neg n].Nodup := by simp
    have hdisj : List.Disjoint qq [neg n] := by
      intro z hz hzsing
      have hzneg : z = neg n := by simpa using hzsing
      have hzgt : neg n < z := hq_gt_neg z hz
      rw [hzneg] at hzgt
      exact (lt_irrefl (neg n) hzgt)
    rw [hfull_eq_sing]
    exact List.Nodup.append hnd hneg_nd hdisj
  have hfull_lt : ∀ z ∈ full p', z < (cut p' : ℤ) := by
    intro z hz
    have hzm : z ∈ qq ++ [neg n] := by
      rw [hfull_eq_sing] at hz
      exact hz
    rw [List.mem_append] at hzm
    rcases hzm with hzq | hzsing
    · simpa [p', cut, mk] using hqlt z hzq
    · have hzneg : z = neg n := by simpa using hzsing
      rw [hzneg]
      have hneg0 : neg n < 0 := by dsimp [neg]; omega
      have h0le : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (cut p : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.zero_le (cut p)
      have hnegcut : neg n < (cut p : ℤ) := lt_of_lt_of_le hneg0 h0le

  have hfull_gt : ∀ z ∈ full p', neg (n+1) < z := by
    intro z hz
    have hzm : z ∈ qq ++ [neg n] := by
      rw [hfull_eq_sing] at hz
      exact hz
    rw [List.mem_append] at hzm
    rcases hzm with hzq | hzsing
    · exact hqgt z hzq
    · have hzneg : z = neg n := by simpa using hzsing
      rw [hzneg]
      have hneglt : neg (n+1) < neg n := by dsimp [neg]; omega
      exact hneglt
  have hfull_len : n + 1 ≤ (full p').length := by
    rw [hfull_eq_sing]
    simp
    omega
  have hfull_eq : full p' = q p' ++ last (n+1) := by
    simp [p', full', full, q, mk]
  have hqprev : ∃ rest : List ℤ, q p' = prev p' ++ rest := by
    rcases hpref with ⟨rest, hr⟩
    refine ⟨rest, ?_⟩
    simpa [p', q, prev, mk] using hr

    right
    refine ⟨hvpos, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · simpa [p', recv, q, mk] using hveq
    · simpa [p', recv, q, mk] using hvnot
    · simpa [p', recv, cut, mk] using hvlt
  have hcut' : (n+1 = 0 ∨ prevCut p' < cut p') := by
    right
    have hNlt' : cut p < N' := by exact_mod_cast hNlt
    simpa [p', prevCut, cut, mk] using hNlt'
  have hsep' : (n+1 = 0 ∨ ∀ z ∈ q p', z ∈ prev p' ∨ (prevCut p' : ℤ) ≤ z) := by
    right
    intro z hz
    have hz' : z ∈ qq := by simpa [p', q, mk] using hz
    rcases hsep z hz' with hzs | hzN
    · left
      simpa [p', prev, mk] using hzs
    · right
      simpa [p', prevCut, mk] using hzN
  have hp' : Pre (n+1) p' := by
    exact ⟨hfull_nd, hfull_lt, hfull_gt, hfull_len, hfull_eq, hqprev, hrec', hcut', hsep'⟩
  exact ⟨p', hp'⟩
