nodes.claim: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
nodes.statement:
theorem fcs76_collections_exist :
  ∃ C1 C2 : Set {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
    (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C1 →
      ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
        g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
    (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C2 →
      ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
        g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
    ¬ (∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
      ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ (C1 ∪ C2) →
        ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
          ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
              List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))

lemma ProofSteps.diag_step (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    (hgen : ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
      L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
          {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))
    (s : List ℤ) (N : ℕ)
    (hs_nd : s.Nodup)
    (hs_lt : ∀ z ∈ s, z < (N : ℤ)) :
    ∃ e : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ N' : ℕ, ∃ r : ℕ, ∃ v : ℤ,
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (hlt : n < s.length), e n = s.get ⟨n, hlt⟩) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, s.length ≤ n → e n = (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ)) ∧
      s.length < r ∧
      let p : List ℤ := List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ));
      p.Nodup ∧
      (∃ rest : List ℤ, p = s ++ rest) ∧
      v = h p ∧
      (∃ k : ℕ, N ≤ k ∧ e k = v) ∧
      v ∉ p ∧
      (N : ℤ) ≤ v ∧
      0 < v ∧
      v < (N' : ℤ)

          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉

      v < (N' : ℤ)

lemma ProofSteps.diag_prefix_injective {α : Type} (l : ℕ → List α)
    (hprefix : ∀ a b : ℕ, a ≤ b → List.IsPrefix (l a) (l b))
    (hnd : ∀ k : ℕ, (l k).Nodup)
    (hlen : ∀ n : ℕ, n < (l (n+1)).length) :
    Function.Injective (fun n : ℕ => (l (n+1)).get ⟨n, hlen n⟩)

by
    intro a b hab
    by_cases hle : a ≤ b
    · have hp : List.IsPrefix (l (a+1)) (l (b+1)) := hprefix (a+1) (b+1) (Nat.succ_le_succ hle)
      have hget : (l (b+1)).get ⟨a, lt_of_lt_of_le (hlen a) (List.IsPrefix.length_le hp)⟩ =

      have hfin := (List.Nodup.get_inj_iff (hnd (b+1))).mp hget
      simpa using congrArg Fin.val hfin
    · have hba : b ≤ a := le_of_not_ge hle

      have hget : (l (a+1)).get ⟨b, lt_of_lt_of_le (hlen b) (List.IsPrefix.length_le hp)⟩ =

        exact (ProofSteps.prefix_get_eq (l (b+1)) (l (a+1)) hp ⟨b, hlen b⟩).symm.trans hab.symm
      have hfin := (List.Nodup.get_inj_iff (hnd (a+1))).mp hget
      simpa using (congrArg Fin.val hfin).symm

nodes.claim: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
nodes.statement:
theorem fcs76_collections_exist :
  ∃ C1 C2 : Set {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
    (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C1 →
      ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
        g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
    (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C2 →
      ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
        g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
    ¬ (∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
      ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ (C1 ∪ C2) →
        ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
          ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
              List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))

lemma ProofSteps.diag_full (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    (hgen : ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
      L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
          {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))
    (s : List ℤ) (N n : ℕ)
    (hs_nd : s.Nodup)
    (hs_lt : ∀ z ∈ s, z < (N : ℤ))
    (hs_gt : ∀ z ∈ s, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) < z) :
    ∃ q : List ℤ, ∃ N' : ℕ, ∃ v : ℤ,
      (∃ rest : List ℤ, q = s ++ rest) ∧
      q.Nodup ∧
      s.length < q.length ∧
      (∀ z ∈ q, z < (N' : ℤ)) ∧
      (∀ z ∈ q, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) < z) ∧
      0 < v ∧
      v = h q ∧
      v ∉ q ∧
      (N : ℤ) < (N' : ℤ) ∧
      v < (N' : ℤ)

    (hpref : List.IsPrefix l₁ l₂) (i : Fin l₁.length) :

lemma ProofSteps.diag_q_ofFn {State : Type} (full q : State → List ℤ) (G : ℕ → State) (neg : ℕ → ℤ)
    (hprefix : ∀ a b : ℕ, a ≤ b → List.IsPrefix (full (G a)) (full (G b)))
    (hqfull : ∀ n : ℕ, full (G (n + 1)) = q (G (n + 1)) ++ [neg n])
    (hdlen : ∀ n : ℕ, n < (full (G (n + 1))).length) :
    ∀ n : ℕ,
      List.ofFn (fun i : Fin (q (G (n + 1))).length =>
        (full (G (i.1 + 1))).get ⟨i.1, hdlen i.1⟩) = q (G (n + 1))

    (hnd : ∀ k : ℕ, (l k).Nodup)
    (hlen : ∀ n : ℕ, n < (l (n+1)).length) :
    Function.Injective (fun n : ℕ => (l (n+1)).get ⟨n, hlen n⟩)

lemma ProofSteps.diag_records_neg_diag {State : Type} (full q : State → List ℤ)
    (G : ℕ → State) (neg : ℕ → ℤ) (n m : ℕ)

    (hpref : List.IsPrefix (full (G (n + 1))) (full (G (m + 1))))
    (hsing : full (G (n + 1)) = q (G (n + 1)) ++ [neg n])
    (hmem : m < (full (G (n + 1))).length) :

result.statement: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
result.proof: Take the nonnegative integers as points p_n = n and the negative integers as points m_n = −n−1. Let C₁ be the languages whose carrier contains some tail {p_{N+j} : j ≥ 0}, and C₂ the languages whose carrier contains every m_n. The sequence (p_n) is injective and generates each member of C₁ after its cutoff, giving non-uniform sample-free generation; the sequence (m_n) generates each member of C₂ from time zero, giving uniform sample-free generation. Freshness reduces to membership together with absence of earlier repetition, which holds because both sequences are injective. For the negative clause, assume some sample-based generator G generates the union in the limit. Build nested finite injective prefixes together with strictly increasing cutoffs: given a stage prefix s and cutoff N, enumerate s followed by the positive tail from N; this enumeration belongs to C₁, so G must eventually output a fresh value, which cannot be a previously listed element and hence is some p_k with k ≥ N. Extend the prefix by that observed enumeration prefix and append the next negative point m_n, choosing a fresh larger cutoff so that p_k occurs neither in the new prefix nor in its future positive tail. Induction shows p_k is never reproduced later. The nested prefixes converge to an injective sequence x whose range is infinite and contains every negative point, so it is the carrier of a language in C₂ that x enumerates. At each stage time the prefix of x agrees with the recorded stage prefix, so G outputs p_k, which lies outside this limiting language; since these failures occur arbitrarily late, G fails to generate in the limit, a contradiction. Hence the union is not generatable in the limit, and the constructed collections witness the claim.

lemma ProofSteps.diag_full (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    (hgen : ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},

          {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))
    (s : List ℤ) (N n : ℕ)
    (hs_nd : s.Nodup)
    (hs_lt : ∀ z ∈ s, z < (N : ℤ))
    (hs_gt : ∀ z ∈ s, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) < z) :
    ∃ q : List ℤ, ∃ N' : ℕ, ∃ v : ℤ,

      s.length < q.length ∧
      (∀ z ∈ q, z < (N' : ℤ)) ∧
      (∀ z ∈ q, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) < z) ∧
      0 < v ∧
      v = h q ∧
      v ∉ q ∧
      (N : ℤ) < (N' : ℤ) ∧
      v < (N' : ℤ)

  toFun i := l.get i

    ⟨i, hl⟩⟩

nodes.claim: For State stages with nested prefixes and one stage splitting full = q ++ [neg n], the diagonal list over i < q(G(n+1)).length equals q(G(n+1)).
For State-valued stages G with full, q and tail last, if every stage satisfies full (G (k+1)) = q (G (k+1)) ++ last (k+1) and last (k+1) = [neg k], then full (G (k+1)) = q (G (k+1)) ++ [neg k].
nodes.statement:
lemma ProofSteps.hqfull_of_hpre
    {State : Type}
    (full q : State → List ℤ) (neg : ℕ → ℤ) (last : ℕ → List ℤ)
    (G : ℕ → State)
    (hpre : ∀ k : ℕ, full (G (k+1)) = q (G (k+1)) ++ last (k+1))
    (hlast : ∀ k : ℕ, last (k+1) = [neg k]) :
    ∀ k : ℕ, full (G (k+1)) = q (G (k+1)) ++ [neg k]
nodes.body: intro k; rw [hpre k, hlast k]

nodes.claim: For nested prefixes full of stages G satisfying full(G(n+1)) = q(G(n+1)) ++ [neg n], the list of diagonal entries x i = full(G(i+1)).get i over i < q(G(n+1)).length equals q(G(n+1)).
nodes.body:
intro n
rw [← List.ofFn_get (q (G (n + 1)))]
apply List.ext_get
simp
intro k h1 h2
simp [List.get_ofFn]
have h2q : k < (q (G (n + 1))).length := by simpa using h2
change List.get (full (G (k + 1))) ⟨k, hdlen k⟩ = List.get (q (G (n + 1))) ⟨k, h2q⟩
by_cases hle : k ≤ n
· have hpre : List.IsPrefix (full (G (k + 1))) (full (G (n + 1))) :=
    hprefix (k + 1) (n + 1) (by omega)
  have hget : (full (G (k + 1))).get ⟨k, hdlen k⟩ = (full (G (n + 1))).get ⟨k, lt_of_lt_of_le (hdlen k) (List.IsPrefix.length_le hpre)⟩ :=
    ProofSteps.prefix_get_eq (full (G (k + 1))) (full (G (n + 1))) hpre ⟨k, hdlen k⟩
  have hfullget : (full (G (n + 1))).get ⟨k, lt_of_lt_of_le (hdlen k) (List.IsPrefix.length_le hpre)⟩ = (q (G (n + 1))).get ⟨k, h2q⟩ := by
    simp [hqfull n, List.get_eq_getElem, List.getElem_append_left, h2q]
  exact hget.trans hfullget
· have hpre : List.IsPrefix (full (G (n + 1))) (full (G (k + 1))) :=
    hprefix (n + 1) (k + 1) (by omega)
  have hilfull : k < (full (G (n + 1))).length := by
    rw [hqfull n]
    simp [List.length_append, List.length_singleton]
    omega
  have hget : (full (G (n + 1))).get ⟨k, hilfull⟩ = (full (G (k + 1))).get ⟨k, lt_of_lt_of_le hilfull (List.IsPrefix.length_le hpre)⟩ :=
    ProofSteps.prefix_get_eq (full (G (n + 1))) (full (G (k + 1))) hpre ⟨k, hilfull⟩
  have hfullget : (full (G (n + 1))).get ⟨k, hilfull⟩ = (q (G (n + 1))).get ⟨k, h2q⟩ := by
    simp [hqfull n, List.get_eq_getElem, List.getElem_append_left, h2q]
  calc
    (full (G (k + 1))).get ⟨k, hdlen k⟩ = (full (G (k + 1))).get ⟨k, lt_of_lt_of_le hilfull (List.IsPrefix.length_le hpre)⟩ := by
      simp
    _ = (full (G (n + 1))).get ⟨k, hilfull⟩ := hget.symm
    _ = (q (G (n + 1))).get ⟨k, h2q⟩ := hfullget

nodes.claim: For a good stage prefix s with cutoff N and lower bound m_n, the diag_step construction yields q extending s, nodup, growing, below a larger cutoff N', all entries above m_n, plus the fresh positive record v = h q not in q and below N'.
nodes.body:
rcases ProofSteps.diag_step h hgen s N hs_nd hs_lt with ⟨e, N', r, v, hpre, htail, hsr, hrest, hv_eq, hk, hv_not, hNle_v, hvpos, hvN⟩
let q : List ℤ := List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ))
refine ⟨q, N', v, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
· exact hv_eq
· exact hrest
· simpa [q] using hsr
rcases hv_not with ⟨k, hNk, hk_eq⟩
have hk_ge_s : s.length ≤ k := by
  by_contra hnot
  have hklt : k < s.length := Nat.lt_of_not_ge hnot
  have hmem_k : e k ∈ s := by
    rw [hpre k hklt]
    exact List.get_mem s ⟨k, hklt⟩
  have hltN_k : e k < (N : ℤ) := hs_lt (e k) hmem_k
  have : v < (N : ℤ) := by simpa [hk_eq] using hltN_k
  omega
have hrk : r ≤ k := by
  by_contra hnot
  have hk_lt_r : k < r := Nat.lt_of_not_ge hnot
  have hmem_kq : v ∈ List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ)) := by
    rw [List.mem_ofFn]
    exact ⟨⟨k, hk_lt_r⟩, by simpa [hk_eq]⟩
  exact hNle_v hmem_kq
intro z hz
rcases List.mem_ofFn.mp hz with ⟨i, hiz⟩
rw [← hiz]
by_cases hi_lt : (i : ℕ) < s.length
· have hmemi : s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩ ∈ s := List.get_mem s ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩
  have hltN_i : s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩ < (N : ℤ) := hs_lt (s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩) hmemi
  rw [hpre (i : ℕ) hi_lt]
  omega
· have hi_ge : s.length ≤ (i : ℕ) := Nat.le_of_not_gt hi_lt
  have hi_r : (i : ℕ) < r := i.isLt
  have hi_lt_k : (i : ℕ) < k := by omega
  have hv_tail : v = (N : ℤ) + ((k : ℤ) - (s.length : ℤ)) := by
    rw [← hk_eq]
    exact htail k hk_ge_s
  have hz_lt_v : e (i : ℕ) < v := by
    rw [htail (i : ℕ) hi_ge, hv_tail]
    omega
  omega
intro z hz
rcases List.mem_ofFn.mp hz with ⟨i, hiz⟩
rw [← hiz]
by_cases hi_lt : (i : ℕ) < s.length
· have hmemi : s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩ ∈ s := List.get_mem s ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩
  have hgt : (-(n : ℤ) - 1) < s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩ := hs_gt (s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩) hmemi
  rw [hpre (i : ℕ) hi_lt]
  exact hgt
· have hi_ge : s.length ≤ (i : ℕ) := Nat.le_of_not_gt hi_lt
  rw [htail (i : ℕ) hi_ge]
  omega
exact hvN.1
simpa [q] using hk
simpa [q] using hNle_v
omega
exact hvN.2

lemma ProofSteps.diag_core (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    (hgen : ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
      L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
          {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))
    (s : List ℤ) (N n : ℕ)
    (hs_nd : s.Nodup)
    (hs_lt : ∀ z ∈ s, z < (N : ℤ))
    (hs_gt : ∀ z ∈ s, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) < z) :
    ∃ q : List ℤ, ∃ N' : ℕ, ∃ v : ℤ,
      (∃ rest : List ℤ, q = s ++ rest) ∧
      q.Nodup ∧
      s.length < q.length ∧
      (∀ z ∈ q, z < (N' : ℤ)) ∧
      (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∉ q ∧
      0 < v ∧
      v = h q ∧
      v ∉ q ∧
      (N : ℤ) < (N' : ℤ) ∧
      v < (N' : ℤ)
nodes.body:
rcases ProofSteps.diag_step h hgen s N hs_nd hs_lt with ⟨e, N', r, v, hpre, htail, hsr, hp⟩
rcases hp with ⟨hp_nd, hrest, hv_eq, hk, hv_not, hvN, hv0, hvN'⟩
have hNN' : (N : ℤ) < (N' : ℤ) := by omega
refine ⟨List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ)), N', v, hrest, hp_nd, ?_, ?_, ?_, hv0, hv_eq, hv_not, hNN', hvN'⟩
simpa [List.length_ofFn] using hsr
rcases hk with ⟨k, hkN, hek⟩
have hk_ge_s : s.length ≤ k := by
  by_contra hnot
  have hklt : k < s.length := Nat.lt_of_not_ge hnot
  have hmem_k : e k ∈ s := by
    rw [hpre k hklt]
    exact List.get_mem s ⟨k, hklt⟩
  have hltN_k : e k < (N : ℤ) := hs_lt (e k) hmem_k
  have : v < (N : ℤ) := by simpa [hek] using hltN_k
  omega
have hrk : r ≤ k := by
  by_contra hnot
  have hk_lt_r : k < r := Nat.lt_of_not_ge hnot
  have hmem_kp : v ∈ List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ)) := by
    rw [List.mem_ofFn]
    exact ⟨⟨k, hk_lt_r⟩, hek⟩
  exact hv_not hmem_kp
intro z hz
rcases List.mem_ofFn.mp hz with ⟨i, hiz⟩
rw [← hiz]
by_cases hi_lt : (i : ℕ) < s.length
· have hmemi : s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩ ∈ s := List.get_mem s ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩
  have hltN : s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩ < (N : ℤ) := hs_lt (s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩) hmemi
  rw [hpre (i : ℕ) hi_lt]
  omega
· have hi_ge : s.length ≤ (i : ℕ) := Nat.le_of_not_gt hi_lt
  have hi_r : (i : ℕ) < r := i.isLt
  have hi_lt_k : (i : ℕ) < k := by omega
  have hz_lt_v : e (i : ℕ) < v := by
    rw [htail (i : ℕ) hi_ge]
    rw [← hek]
    rw [htail k hk_ge_s]
    omega
  omega
intro hmem
rcases List.mem_ofFn.mp hmem with ⟨i, hiz⟩
by_cases hi_lt : (i : ℕ) < s.length
· have hmemi : s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩ ∈ s := List.get_mem s ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩
  have hgt : -(n : ℤ) - 1 < s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩ := hs_gt (s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩) hmemi
  rw [hpre (i : ℕ) hi_lt] at hiz
  omega
· have hi_ge : s.length ≤ (i : ℕ) := Nat.le_of_not_gt hi_lt
  rw [htail (i : ℕ) hi_ge] at hiz
  omega

nodes.claim: For every N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) is the range of i ↦ (N + i : ℤ), and that range is infinite.
nodes.body:

constructor
rintro hx
have hx' : (N : ℤ) ≤ x := by simpa [Set.mem_Ici] using hx

refine ⟨i, ?_⟩
change (N : ℤ) + (i : ℤ) = x
have hnonneg : 0 ≤ x - (N : ℤ) := by omega

  exact Int.toNat_of_nonneg hnonneg

rintro ⟨j, rfl⟩
simpa [Set.mem_Ici] using (by omega : (N : ℤ) ≤ (N : ℤ) + (j : ℤ))

nodes.claim: Given generator h and its union property, a finite injective prefix f : Fin l → ℤ and cutoff N, there is a longer finite injective prefix f' starting with f, a fresh positive value p_k with k ≥ N achieved by h on the stage enumeration, and a larger cutoff N' avoiding p_k on future positive tails.
nodes.body:
skip
let e : ℕ → ℤ := fun n => if hln : n < s.length then s.get ⟨n, hln⟩ else (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ)
have h1 : ∀ (n : ℕ) (hlt : n < s.length), e n = s.get ⟨n, hlt⟩ := by
  intro n hlt
  simp [e, hlt]
have h2 : ∀ n : ℕ, s.length ≤ n → e n = (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ) := by
  intro n hn
  simp [e, hn, not_lt_of_ge hn]
have hci : Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ Set.range e := ProofSteps.stage_enum_range_ci s N e h2
have hinf : (Set.range e).Infinite := ProofSteps.stage_enum_range_infinite s N e h2
let L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} := ⟨Set.range e, hinf⟩
have hC1 : L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
    {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) := by
  left
  exact ⟨N, hci⟩
obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := hgen L hC1 e rfl
let r : ℕ := max t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1))
have hsr : s.length < r := by
  dsimp [r]
  exact Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le (Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le (Nat.lt_succ_self s.length) (Nat.le_max_left (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
    (Nat.le_max_right t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
have hsr_le : s.length ≤ r := Nat.le_of_lt hsr
have hNr : N ≤ r := by
  dsimp [r]
  exact Nat.le_trans (Nat.le_trans (Nat.le_succ N) (Nat.le_max_right (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
    (Nat.le_max_right t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
have htr : h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ Set.range e ∧
    h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ))) ∉ List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ)) :=
    ht r (Nat.le_max_left t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
let p : List ℤ := List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ))
let v : ℤ := h p
rcases htr.1 with ⟨m, hm⟩
have hmv : e m = v := by
  simpa [v, p] using hm
have hv_notin_p : v ∉ p := by
  simpa [p, v] using htr.2
have hm_ge_r : r ≤ m := by
  by_contra hcontra
  have hmr : m < r := Nat.lt_of_not_ge hcontra
  have hmem : e m ∈ p := by
    dsimp [p]
    rw [List.mem_ofFn]
    exact ⟨⟨m, hmr⟩, rfl⟩
  exact hv_notin_p (hmv ▸ hmem)
have hm_ge_s : s.length ≤ m := le_trans hsr_le hm_ge_r
have hm_tail : e m = (N + (m - s.length) : ℤ) := h2 m hm_ge_s
have hv_tail : v = (N + (m - s.length) : ℤ) := by
  rw [← hmv, hm_tail]
have hNm : N ≤ m := le_trans hNr hm_ge_r
have hk : ∃ k : ℕ, N ≤ k ∧ e k = v := ⟨m, hNm, hmv⟩
let N' : ℕ := N + (m - s.length) + 1
have hv_ge_N : (N : ℤ) ≤ v := by
  rw [hv_tail]
  exact_mod_cast Nat.le_add_right N (m - s.length)
have hm_gt_s : s.length < m := lt_of_lt_of_le hsr hm_ge_r
have hv_pos : 0 < v := by
  rw [hv_tail]
  have hN_nonneg : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (N : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.zero_le N
  omega
have hv_lt_N' : v < (N' : ℤ) := by
  rw [hv_tail]
  dsimp [N']
  omega
have hinj_fin : Function.Injective (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ)) := by
  intro i j hij
  change e (i : ℕ) = e (j : ℕ) at hij
  apply Fin.ext
  by_cases hi : (i : ℕ) < s.length
  · by_cases hj : (j : ℕ) < s.length
    · have hgeti : e (i : ℕ) = s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩ := h1 (i : ℕ) hi
      have hgetj : e (j : ℕ) = s.get ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩ := h1 (j : ℕ) hj
      have hsij : s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩ = s.get ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩ := by
        rw [← hgeti, ← hgetj]
        exact hij
      have hfin : (⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩ : Fin s.length) = ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩ :=
        (hs_nd.get_inj_iff).mp hsij
      exact congrArg (fun x : Fin s.length => (x : ℕ)) hfin
    · have hj_ge : s.length ≤ (j : ℕ) := Nat.le_of_not_gt hj
      have hi_ltN : e (i : ℕ) < (N : ℤ) := by
        rw [h1 (i : ℕ) hi]
        exact hs_lt (s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩) (List.get_mem s ⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩)
      have hj_geN : (N : ℤ) ≤ e (j : ℕ) := by
        rw [h2 (j : ℕ) hj_ge]
        exact_mod_cast Nat.le_add_right N ((j : ℕ) - s.length)
      omega
  · have hi_ge : s.length ≤ (i : ℕ) := Nat.le_of_not_gt hi
    by_cases hj : (j : ℕ) < s.length
    · have hj_ltN : e (j : ℕ) < (N : ℤ) := by
        rw [h1 (j : ℕ) hj]
        exact hs_lt (s.get ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩) (List.get_mem s ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩)
      have hi_geN : (N : ℤ) ≤ e (i : ℕ) := by
        rw [h2 (i : ℕ) hi_ge]
        exact_mod_cast Nat.le_add_right N ((i : ℕ) - s.length)
      omega
    · have hj_ge : s.length ≤ (j : ℕ) := Nat.le_of_not_gt hj
      rw [h2 (i : ℕ) hi_ge, h2 (j : ℕ) hj_ge] at hij
      omega
have hp_nd : p.Nodup := by
  dsimp [p]
  rw [List.nodup_ofFn]
  exact hinj_fin
have hp_take : List.take s.length p = s := by
  apply List.ext_getElem
  · simp [p, List.length_take, List.length_ofFn]
    omega
  · intro i hi₁ hi₂
    simp [p, List.getElem_take, List.getElem_ofFn]
    exact h1 i hi₂
have hp_extend : ∃ rest : List ℤ, p = s ++ rest := by
  refine ⟨List.drop s.length p, ?_⟩
  calc
    p = List.take s.length p ++ List.drop s.length p := (List.take_append_drop s.length p).symm
    _ = s ++ List.drop s.length p := by rw [hp_take]

refine ⟨e, N', r, v, h1, h2, hsr, hp_nd, hp_extend, rfl, hk,
    hv_notin_p, hv_ge_N, hv_pos, hv_lt_N'⟩

nodes.claim: For s : List ℤ, N : ℕ and e : ℕ → ℤ with e n = (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ) whenever s.length ≤ n, one has Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ Set.range e.

intro x hx
rcases (by simpa [ProofSteps.pos_tail_range N] using hx : x ∈ Set.range (fun i : ℕ => (N + i : ℤ))) with ⟨j, hj⟩
refine ⟨s.length + j, ?_⟩
have hj' : (N : ℤ) + (j : ℤ) = x := by simpa using hj
have hval : e (s.length + j) = (N : ℤ) + (j : ℤ) := by
  have ht := he_tail (s.length + j) (Nat.le_add_right s.length j)
  omega
omega

nodes.claim: For s : List ℤ, N : ℕ and e : ℕ → ℤ with e n = (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ) whenever s.length ≤ n, the set Set.range e is infinite.

exact ProofSteps.stage_enum_range_ci s N e he_tail
have hinj : Function.Injective (fun i : ℕ => (N + i : ℤ)) := by

  norm_num at hab
  omega
simpa [ProofSteps.pos_tail_range N] using (Set.infinite_range_of_injective hinj)

let q : List ℤ := List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e i)
refine ⟨q, N', v, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
simpa [q] using hpext

intro z hz

  simpa [q] using hz

by_cases hi : (i : ℕ) < s.length

  exact hpref (i : ℕ) hi

exact lt_trans hzN hNltN'
have hi_ge : s.length ≤ (i : ℕ) := Nat.le_of_not_gt hi
have hz_tail : z = (N : ℤ) + (((i : ℕ) : ℤ) - (s.length : ℤ)) := by

rcases hk with ⟨k, hNk, hke⟩
have hkr : r ≤ k := by

have hik : (i : ℕ) < k := Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le hir hkr

have hktail : e k = (N : ℤ) + (((k : ℕ) : ℤ) - (s.length : ℤ)) := htail k hkge
have hv_tail : v = (N : ℤ) + (((k : ℕ) : ℤ) - (s.length : ℤ)) := by

have hzv : z < v := by

exact lt_trans hzv hvlt
intro z hz
have hz' : z ∈ List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ)) := by

rw [List.mem_ofFn] at hz'
rcases hz' with ⟨i, hzi⟩
by_cases hi : (i : ℕ) < s.length
· have hz_s : z = (s.get ⟨i, hi⟩ : ℤ) := by

    rw [← hzi]

exact hv0
simpa [q] using hveq
simpa [q] using hvnot
exact (lt_of_le_of_lt hNv hvlt)
exact hvlt
intro z hz
have hz' : z ∈ List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ)) := by
  simpa [q] using hz
rw [List.mem_ofFn] at hz'
rcases hz' with ⟨i, hzi⟩
by_cases hi : (i : ℕ) < s.length
· left

lemma ProofSteps.prefix_get_eq {α} (l₁ l₂ : List α)
    (hpref : List.IsPrefix l₁ l₂) (i : Fin l₁.length) :
    l₁.get i = l₂.get ⟨i.1, lt_of_lt_of_le i.2 (List.IsPrefix.length_le hpref)⟩

nodes.claim: For any sequence of lists with nested prefixes and nodupness, the diagonal nth element of the (n+1)th list is injective.
nodes.statement:
lemma ProofSteps.diag_prefix_injective {α : Type} (l : ℕ → List α)
    (hprefix : ∀ a b : ℕ, a ≤ b → List.IsPrefix (l a) (l b))

result.statement: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
result.proof: Take the nonnegative integers as points p_n = n and the negative integers as points m_n = −n−1. Let C₁ be the languages whose carrier contains some tail {p_{N+j} : j ≥ 0}, and C₂ the languages whose carrier contains every m_n. The sequence (p_n) is injective and generates each member of C₁ after its cutoff, giving non-uniform sample-free generation; the sequence (m_n) generates each member of C₂ from time zero, giving uniform sample-free generation. Freshness reduces to membership together with absence of earlier repetition, which holds because both sequences are injective. For the negative clause, assume some sample-based generator G generates the union in the limit. Build nested finite injective prefixes together with strictly increasing cutoffs: given a stage prefix s and cutoff N, enumerate s followed by the positive tail from N; this enumeration belongs to C₁, so G must eventually output a fresh value, which cannot be a previously listed element and hence is some p_k with k ≥ N. Extend the prefix by that observed enumeration prefix and append the next negative point m_n, choosing a fresh larger cutoff so that p_k occurs neither in the new prefix nor in its future positive tail. Induction shows p_k is never reproduced later. The nested prefixes converge to an injective sequence x whose range is infinite and contains every negative point, so it is the carrier of a language in C₂ that x enumerates. At each stage time the prefix of x agrees with the recorded stage prefix, so G outputs p_k, which lies outside this limiting language; since these failures occur arbitrarily late, G fails to generate in the limit, a contradiction. Hence the union is not generatable in the limit, and the constructed collections witness the claim.

refine List.ext_getElem ?_ ?_
  · simp only [List.length_ofFn]
  · intro i hiL hiR
    rw [List.getElem_ofFn hiL]
    rw [List.get_eq_getElem]
    rcases le_total i n with hle | hge
    · have hpref : List.IsPrefix (full (G (i + 1))) (full (G (n + 1))) :=
        hprefix (i + 1) (n + 1) (Nat.succ_le_succ hle)
      rw [show (full (G (i + 1))).getElem i (hdlen i) =
          (full (G (n + 1))).getElem i (lt_of_lt_of_le (hdlen i) (List.IsPrefix.length_le hpref)) from
        List.IsPrefix.getElem hpref (hdlen i)]
      rw [hsing]
      exact List.getElem_append_left hiR
    · have hpref : List.IsPrefix (full (G (n + 1))) (full (G (i + 1))) :=
        hprefix (n + 1) (i + 1) (Nat.succ_le_succ hge)
      have hifull : i < (full (G (n + 1))).length := by
        rw [hsing, List.length_append, List.length_singleton]
        exact Nat.lt_trans hiR (Nat.lt_succ_self _)
      rw [← show (full (G (n + 1))).getElem i hifull =
          (full (G (i + 1))).getElem i (hdlen i) from
        List.IsPrefix.getElem hpref hifull]
      rw [hsing]
      exact List.getElem_append_left hiR

result.statement: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
result.proof: Take the nonnegative integers as points p_n = n and the negative integers as points m_n = −n−1. Let C₁ be the languages whose carrier contains some tail {p_{N+j} : j ≥ 0}, and C₂ the languages whose carrier contains every m_n. The sequence (p_n) is injective and generates each member of C₁ after its cutoff, giving non-uniform sample-free generation; the sequence (m_n) generates each member of C₂ from time zero, giving uniform sample-free generation. Freshness reduces to membership together with absence of earlier repetition, which holds because both sequences are injective. For the negative clause, assume some sample-based generator G generates the union in the limit. Build nested finite injective prefixes together with strictly increasing cutoffs: given a stage prefix s and cutoff N, enumerate s followed by the positive tail from N; this enumeration belongs to C₁, so G must eventually output a fresh value, which cannot be a previously listed element and hence is some p_k with k ≥ N. Extend the prefix by that observed enumeration prefix and append the next negative point m_n, choosing a fresh larger cutoff so that p_k occurs neither in the new prefix nor in its future positive tail. Induction shows p_k is never reproduced later. The nested prefixes converge to an injective sequence x whose range is infinite and contains every negative point, so it is the carrier of a language in C₂ that x enumerates. At each stage time the prefix of x agrees with the recorded stage prefix, so G outputs p_k, which lies outside this limiting language; since these failures occur arbitrarily late, G fails to generate in the limit, a contradiction. Hence the union is not generatable in the limit, and the constructed collections witness the claim.

result.statement: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
result.proof: Take the nonnegative integers as points p_n = n and the negative integers as points m_n = −n−1. Let C₁ be the languages whose carrier contains some tail {p_{N+j} : j ≥ 0}, and C₂ the languages whose carrier contains every m_n. The sequence (p_n) is injective and generates each member of C₁ after its cutoff, giving non-uniform sample-free generation; the sequence (m_n) generates each member of C₂ from time zero, giving uniform sample-free generation. Freshness reduces to membership together with absence of earlier repetition, which holds because both sequences are injective. For the negative clause, assume some sample-based generator G generates the union in the limit. Build nested finite injective prefixes together with strictly increasing cutoffs: given a stage prefix s and cutoff N, enumerate s followed by the positive tail from N; this enumeration belongs to C₁, so G must eventually output a fresh value, which cannot be a previously listed element and hence is some p_k with k ≥ N. Extend the prefix by that observed enumeration prefix and append the next negative point m_n, choosing a fresh larger cutoff so that p_k occurs neither in the new prefix nor in its future positive tail. Induction shows p_k is never reproduced later. The nested prefixes converge to an injective sequence x whose range is infinite and contains every negative point, so it is the carrier of a language in C₂ that x enumerates. At each stage time the prefix of x agrees with the recorded stage prefix, so G outputs p_k, which lies outside this limiting language; since these failures occur arbitrarily late, G fails to generate in the limit, a contradiction. Hence the union is not generatable in the limit, and the constructed collections witness the claim.

Explanation: The rewrite tactic rewrites an expression 'e' using an equality 'a = b' by the following process. First, it looks for all 'a' in 'e'. Second, it tries to abstract these occurrences of 'a' to create a function 'm := fun _a => ...', called the *motive*, with the property that 'm a' is definitionally equal to 'e'. Third, we observe that 'congrArg' implies that 'm a = m b', which can be used with lemmas such as 'Eq.mpr' to change the goal. However, if 'e' depends on specific properties of 'a', then the motive 'm' might not typecheck.

Possible solutions: use rewrite's 'occs' configuration option to limit which occurrences are rewritten, or use 'simp' or 'conv' mode, which have strategies for certain kinds of dependencies (these tactics can handle proofs and 'Decidable' instances whose types depend on the rewritten term, and 'simp' can apply user-defined '@[congr]' theorems as well).

      v < (N' : ℤ)

  dsimp [N']

have hinj_fin : Function.Injective (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ)) := by
  intro i j hij
  change e (i : ℕ) = e (j : ℕ) at hij
  apply Fin.ext
  by_cases hi : (i : ℕ) < s.length
  · by_cases hj : (j : ℕ) < s.length
    · have hgeti : e (i : ℕ) = s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩ := h1 (i : ℕ) hi
      have hgetj : e (j : ℕ) = s.get ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩ := h1 (j : ℕ) hj
      have hsij : s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩ = s.get ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩ := by
        rw [← hgeti, ← hgetj]
        exact hij
      have hfin : (⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩ : Fin s.length) = ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩ :=
        (hs_nd.get_inj_iff).mp hsij
      exact congrArg (fun x : Fin s.length => (x : ℕ)) hfin
    · have hj_ge : s.length ≤ (j : ℕ) := Nat.le_of_not_gt hj
      have hi_ltN : e (i : ℕ) < (N : ℤ) := by
        rw [h1 (i : ℕ) hi]
        exact hs_lt (s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩) (List.get_mem s ⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩)
      have hj_geN : (N : ℤ) ≤ e (j : ℕ) := by
        rw [h2 (j : ℕ) hj_ge]
        exact_mod_cast Nat.le_add_right N ((j : ℕ) - s.length)
      omega
  · have hi_ge : s.length ≤ (i : ℕ) := Nat.le_of_not_gt hi
    by_cases hj : (j : ℕ) < s.length
    · have hj_ltN : e (j : ℕ) < (N : ℤ) := by
        rw [h1 (j : ℕ) hj]
        exact hs_lt (s.get ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩) (List.get_mem s ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩)
      have hi_geN : (N : ℤ) ≤ e (i : ℕ) := by
        rw [h2 (i : ℕ) hi_ge]
        exact_mod_cast Nat.le_add_right N ((i : ℕ) - s.length)
      omega
    · have hj_ge : s.length ≤ (j : ℕ) := Nat.le_of_not_gt hj
      rw [h2 (i : ℕ) hi_ge, h2 (j : ℕ) hj_ge] at hij
      omega
have hp_nd : p.Nodup := by
  dsimp [p]
  rw [List.nodup_ofFn]
  exact hinj_fin
have hp_take : List.take s.length p = s := by
  apply List.ext_getElem
  · simp [p, List.length_take, List.length_ofFn]
    omega
  · intro i hi₁ hi₂
    simp [p, List.getElem_take, List.getElem_ofFn]
    exact h1 i hi₂
have hp_extend : ∃ rest : List ℤ, p = s ++ rest := by

    p = List.take s.length p ++ List.drop s.length p := (List.take_append_drop s.length p).symm
    _ = s ++ List.drop s.length p := by rw [hp_take]

lemma ProofSteps.diag_prefix_injective {α : Type} (l : ℕ → List α)
    (hprefix : ∀ a b : ℕ, a ≤ b → List.IsPrefix (l a) (l b))
    (hnd : ∀ k : ℕ, (l k).Nodup)
    (hlen : ∀ n : ℕ, n < (l (n+1)).length) :
    Function.Injective (fun n : ℕ => (l (n+1)).get ⟨n, hlen n⟩)
nodes.body:
by
    intro a b hab
    by_cases hle : a ≤ b
    · have hp : List.IsPrefix (l (a+1)) (l (b+1)) := hprefix (a+1) (b+1) (Nat.succ_le_succ hle)
      have hget : (l (b+1)).get ⟨a, lt_of_lt_of_le (hlen a) (List.IsPrefix.length_le hp)⟩ =
          (l (b+1)).get ⟨b, hlen b⟩ := by
        exact (ProofSteps.prefix_get_eq (l (a+1)) (l (b+1)) hp ⟨a, hlen a⟩).symm.trans hab
      have hfin := (List.Nodup.get_inj_iff (hnd (b+1))).mp hget
      simpa using congrArg Fin.val hfin
    · have hba : b ≤ a := le_of_not_ge hle
      have hp : List.IsPrefix (l (b+1)) (l (a+1)) := hprefix (b+1) (a+1) (Nat.succ_le_succ hba)
      have hget : (l (a+1)).get ⟨b, lt_of_lt_of_le (hlen b) (List.IsPrefix.length_le hp)⟩ =
          (l (a+1)).get ⟨a, hlen a⟩ := by
        exact (ProofSteps.prefix_get_eq (l (b+1)) (l (a+1)) hp ⟨b, hlen b⟩).symm.trans hab.symm
      have hfin := (List.Nodup.get_inj_iff (hnd (a+1))).mp hget
      simpa using (congrArg Fin.val hfin).symm

nodes.claim: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
nodes.statement:
theorem fcs76_collections_exist :
  ∃ C1 C2 : Set {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
    (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C1 →
      ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
        g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
    (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C2 →
      ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
        g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
    ¬ (∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
      ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ (C1 ∪ C2) →
        ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
          ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
              List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))

declarations.name: LocallyFinite.exists_forall_eventually_atTop_eventually_eq'
declarations.doc:
Let `f : ℕ → Π a, β a` be a sequence of (dependent) functions on a topological space. Suppose
that the family of sets `s n = {x | f (n + 1) x ≠ f n x}` is locally finite. Then there exists a
function `F : Π a, β a` such that for any `x`, for sufficiently large values of `n`, we have
`f n y = F y` in a neighbourhood of `x`.

declarations.name: Filter.HasBasis.exists_antitone_subbasis

enumerated by natural numbers such that all sets have the form `s i`. More precisely, there is a

declarations.name: LocallyFinite.exists_forall_eventually_eq_prod
declarations.doc:
Let `f : ℕ → Π a, β a` be a sequence of (dependent) functions on a topological space. Suppose
that the family of sets `s n = {x | f (n + 1) x ≠ f n x}` is locally finite. Then there exists a
function `F : Π a, β a` such that for any `x`, we have `f n x = F x` on the product of an infinite
interval `[N, +∞)` and a neighbourhood of `x`.

We formulate the conclusion in terms of the product of filter `Filter.atTop` and `𝓝 x`.

declarations.name: Mathlib.Tactic.Sat.buildProof
declarations.source_snippet:
partial def buildProof (arr : Array (Array Int)) (ctx ctx' : Expr)
    (steps : Array LRATStep) : MetaM Expr := do
  let p := mkApp (mkConst ``Sat.Fmla.subsumes_self) ctx
  let mut db := (buildClauses arr ctx 0 arr.size ctx' p default).2
  for step in steps do
    match step with
    | LRATStep.del ds => db := ds.foldl (·.erase ·) db
    | LRATStep.add i ns pf =>
      let e := buildClause ns
      match buildProofStep db ns pf ctx e with
      | Except.ok proof =>
        if ns.isEmpty then return proof
        db := db.insert i { lits := ns, expr := e, proof }
      | Except.error msg => throwError msg
  throwError "failed to prove empty clause"
declarations.doc:
Build the main proof of `⊢ ctx.proof []` using the LRAT proof trace.

  * `arr`: The input CNF
  * `ctx`: The abbreviated formula, a constant like `foo.ctx_1`
  * `ctx'`: The definitional expansion of the formula, a tree of `Fmla.and` nodes
  * `steps`: The input LRAT proof trace

declarations.source_snippet:
def addNegEqProofsIdx : List (Expr × Nat) → MetaM (List (Expr × Nat))
  | [] => return []
  | (⟨h, i⟩::tl) => do
    let (iq, t) ← parseCompAndExpr (← inferType h)
    match iq with
    | Ineq.eq => do
      let nep :=
        mkAppN (← mkAppM `Iff.mpr #[← mkAppOptM ``neg_eq_zero #[none, none, t]]) #[h]
      let tl ← addNegEqProofsIdx tl
      return (h, i)::(nep, i)::tl
    | _ => return (h, i) :: (← addNegEqProofsIdx tl)
declarations.doc:
`addNegEqProofsIdx l` inspects a list `l` of pairs `(h, i)` where `h` proves
`tᵢ Rᵢ 0` and `i` records the original index of the hypothesis. For each
equality proof `t = 0` in the list, it appends a proof of `-t = 0` with the
same index `i`. All other entries are preserved.

  ∀ v : Valuation, v.satisfies_fmla f → v.satisfies c
declarations.doc: `f.proof c` asserts that `c` is derivable from `f`.

    (H : Fmla.subsumes f (Fmla.one c)) : f.proof c

declarations.name: Sat.Valuation.satisfies
declarations.source_snippet:
def Valuation.satisfies (v : Valuation) : Clause → Prop
  | [] => False
  | l::c => v.neg l → v.satisfies c
termination_by structural ps => ps
declarations.doc:
`v.satisfies c` asserts that clause `c` satisfied by the valuation.
It is written in a negative way: A clause like `a ∨ ¬b ∨ c` is rewritten as

declarations.name: Mathlib.Tactic.Sat.buildClauses
declarations.source_snippet:
partial def buildClauses (arr : Array (Array Int)) (ctx : Expr) (start stop : Nat)
    (f p : Expr) (accum : Nat × HashMap Nat Clause) : Nat × HashMap Nat Clause :=
  match stop - start with
  | 0 => panic! "empty"
  | 1 =>
    let c := f.appArg!
    let proof := mkApp3 (mkConst ``Sat.Fmla.proof_of_subsumes) ctx c p
    let n := accum.1 + 1
    (n, accum.2.insert n { lits := arr[start]!, expr := c, proof })
  | len =>
    let mid := start + len / 2
    let f₁ := f.appFn!.appArg!
    let f₂ := f.appArg!
    let p₁ := mkApp4 (mkConst ``Sat.Fmla.subsumes_left) ctx f₁ f₂ p
    let p₂ := mkApp4 (mkConst ``Sat.Fmla.subsumes_right) ctx f₁ f₂ p
    let accum := buildClauses arr ctx start mid f₁ p₁ accum
    buildClauses arr ctx mid stop f₂ p₂ accum
declarations.doc:
Constructs the proofs of `⊢ ctx.proof c` for each clause `c` in `ctx`.
The proofs are stashed in a `HashMap` keyed on the clause ID.

declarations.name: Mathlib.Tactic.Sat.LClause
declarations.source_snippet:
structure LClause where
                                                         
  lits : Array Int
                                               
  expr : Expr
                                                                           
                                                                                         
                                                         
  depth : Nat
declarations.doc:
A localized clause reference.
It is the same as `Clause` except that the proof is now a local variable.

declarations.name: Mathlib.Tactic.Sat.buildProofStep
declarations.source_snippet:
partial def buildProofStep (db : HashMap Nat Clause)
    (ns pf : Array Int) (ctx clause : Expr) : Except String Expr := Id.run do
  let mut lams := #[]
  let mut args := #[]
  let mut gctx : HashMap Nat LClause := {}
           
  for i in pf do
    let i := i.natAbs
    let some cl := db[i]? | return Except.error "missing clause"
    if !gctx.contains i then
      lams := lams.push (mkApp2 (mkConst ``Sat.Fmla.proof) ctx cl.expr)
      args := args.push cl.proof
      gctx := gctx.insert i {
        lits := cl.lits
        expr := cl.expr
        depth := args.size
      }
  let n := args.size
           
  let mut f :=
    (mkAppN · args) ∘
    lams.foldr (mkLambda `c default) ∘
    mkLambda `v default (mkConst ``Sat.Valuation) ∘
    mkLambda `hv default (mkApp2 (mkConst ``Sat.Valuation.satisfies_fmla) (mkBVar 0) ctx)
  let v depth := mkBVar (depth + 1)
  let hv depth := mkBVar depth
  lams := #[]
  let mut clause := clause
  let mut depth := 0
  let mut lctx : HashMap Int Nat := {}
  for i in ns do
    let l := clause.appFn!.appArg!
    clause := clause.appArg!
    lams := lams.push (mkApp2 (mkConst ``Sat.Valuation.neg) (v depth) l)
    depth := depth.succ
    lctx := lctx.insert i depth
  f := f ∘ lams.foldr (mkLambda `h default)
           
  for (step : Int) in pf do
    if step < 0 then return Except.error "unimplemented: RAT step"
    let some cl := gctx[step.toNat]? | return Except.error "missing clause"
    let mut unit := none
    for i in cl.lits do
      unless lctx.contains i do
        if unit.isSome then return Except.error s!"not unit: {cl.lits}"
        depth := depth.succ
        unit := some i
    let mut pr := mkApp2 (mkBVar (depth + n + 2 - cl.depth)) (v depth) (hv depth)
    for i in cl.lits do
      pr := mkApp pr <| mkBVar (match lctx[i]? with | some k => depth - k | _ => 0)
    let some u := unit | return Except.ok <| f pr
    let lit := toExpr <| Sat.Literal.ofInt u
    let nlit := toExpr <| Sat.Literal.ofInt (-u)
    let d1 := depth-1
    let app := mkApp3 (mkConst ``Sat.Valuation.by_cases) (v d1) nlit <|
      mkLambda `h default (mkApp2 (mkConst ``Sat.Valuation.neg) (v d1) lit) pr
    let dom := mkApp2 (mkConst ``Sat.Valuation.neg) (v d1) nlit
    f := fun e ↦ f <| mkApp app <| mkLambda `h default dom e
    lctx := lctx.insert (-u) depth
  return Except.error s!"no refutation: {ns}, {pf}, {lctx.toList}"
declarations.doc:
Construct an individual proof step `⊢ ctx.proof c`.

  * `db`: the current global context
  * `ns`, `clause`: the new clause
  * `pf`: the LRAT proof trace
  * `ctx`: the main formula

  The proof has three steps:

  1. Introduce local assumptions `have h1 : ctx.proof c1 := p1` for each clause `c1`
     referenced in the proof. We actually do all the introductions at once,
     as in `(fun h1 h2 h3 ↦ ...) p1 p2 p3`, because we want `p_i` to not be under any binders
     to avoid the cost of `instantiate` during typechecking and get the benefits of dag-like
     sharing in the `pi` (which are themselves previous proof steps which may be large terms).
     The hypotheses are in `gctx`, keyed on the clause ID.

  2. Unfold `⊢ ctx.proof [a, b, c]` to
     `∀ v, v.satisfies_fmla ctx → v.neg a → v.neg b → v.neg c → False` and `intro v hv ha hb hc`,
     storing each `ha : v.neg a` in `lctx`, keyed on the literal `a`.

  3. For each LRAT step `hc : ctx.proof [x, y]`, `hc v hv : v.neg x → v.neg y → False`.
     We look for a literal that is not falsified in the clause. Since it is a unit propagation
     step, there can be at most one such literal.
     * If `x` is the non-falsified clause, let `x'` denote the negated literal of `x`.
       Then `x'.negate` reduces to `x`, so `hnx : v.neg x'.negate |- hc v hv hnx hy : False`,
       so we construct the term
         `by_cases (fun hnx : v.neg x'.negate ↦ hc v hv hnx hy) (fun hx : v.neg x ↦ ...)`
       and `hx` is added to the local context.
     * If all clauses are falsified, then we are done: `hc v hv hx hy : False`.

      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →

          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉

      0 < v ∧

      v < (N' : ℤ)

nodes.claim: Given generator h and its union property, a finite injective prefix f : Fin l → ℤ and cutoff N, there is a longer finite injective prefix f' starting with f, a fresh positive value p_k with k ≥ N achieved by h on the stage enumeration, and a larger cutoff N' avoiding p_k on future positive tails.

skip
let e : ℕ → ℤ := fun n => if hln : n < s.length then s.get ⟨n, hln⟩ else (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ)
have h1 : ∀ (n : ℕ) (hlt : n < s.length), e n = s.get ⟨n, hlt⟩ := by
  intro n hlt
  simp [e, hlt]
have h2 : ∀ n : ℕ, s.length ≤ n → e n = (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ) := by
  intro n hn
  simp [e, hn, not_lt_of_ge hn]
have hci : Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ Set.range e := ProofSteps.stage_enum_range_ci s N e h2
have hinf : (Set.range e).Infinite := ProofSteps.stage_enum_range_infinite s N e h2
let L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} := ⟨Set.range e, hinf⟩
have hC1 : L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
    {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) := by
  left
  exact ⟨N, hci⟩
obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := hgen L hC1 e rfl
let r : ℕ := max t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1))
have hsr : s.length < r := by
  dsimp [r]
  exact Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le (Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le (Nat.lt_succ_self s.length) (Nat.le_max_left (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
    (Nat.le_max_right t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
have hsr_le : s.length ≤ r := Nat.le_of_lt hsr
have hNr : N ≤ r := by
  dsimp [r]
  exact Nat.le_trans (Nat.le_trans (Nat.le_succ N) (Nat.le_max_right (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
    (Nat.le_max_right t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
have htr : h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ Set.range e ∧
    h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ))) ∉ List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ)) :=
    ht r (Nat.le_max_left t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
let p : List ℤ := List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ))
let v : ℤ := h p
rcases htr.1 with ⟨m, hm⟩
have hmv : e m = v := by
  simpa [v, p] using hm
have hv_notin_p : v ∉ p := by
  simpa [p, v] using htr.2
have hm_ge_r : r ≤ m := by
  by_contra hcontra
  have hmr : m < r := Nat.lt_of_not_ge hcontra
  have hmem : e m ∈ p := by
    dsimp [p]
    rw [List.mem_ofFn]
    exact ⟨⟨m, hmr⟩, rfl⟩
  exact hv_notin_p (hmv ▸ hmem)
have hm_ge_s : s.length ≤ m := le_trans hsr_le hm_ge_r
have hm_tail : e m = (N + (m - s.length) : ℤ) := h2 m hm_ge_s
have hv_tail : v = (N + (m - s.length) : ℤ) := by
  rw [← hmv, hm_tail]
have hNm : N ≤ m := le_trans hNr hm_ge_r
have hk : ∃ k : ℕ, N ≤ k ∧ e k = v := ⟨m, hNm, hmv⟩
let N' : ℕ := N + (m - s.length) + 1
have hv_ge_N : (N : ℤ) ≤ v := by
  rw [hv_tail]
  exact_mod_cast Nat.le_add_right N (m - s.length)
have hm_gt_s : s.length < m := lt_of_lt_of_le hsr hm_ge_r
have hv_pos : 0 < v := by
  rw [hv_tail]
  have hN_nonneg : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (N : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.zero_le N
  omega
have hv_lt_N' : v < (N' : ℤ) := by
  rw [hv_tail]
  dsimp [N']
  omega
have hinj_fin : Function.Injective (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ)) := by
  intro i j hij
  change e (i : ℕ) = e (j : ℕ) at hij
  apply Fin.ext
  by_cases hi : (i : ℕ) < s.length
  · by_cases hj : (j : ℕ) < s.length
    · have hgeti : e (i : ℕ) = s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩ := h1 (i : ℕ) hi
      have hgetj : e (j : ℕ) = s.get ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩ := h1 (j : ℕ) hj
      have hsij : s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩ = s.get ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩ := by
        rw [← hgeti, ← hgetj]
        exact hij
      have hfin : (⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩ : Fin s.length) = ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩ :=
        (hs_nd.get_inj_iff).mp hsij
      exact congrArg (fun x : Fin s.length => (x : ℕ)) hfin
    · have hj_ge : s.length ≤ (j : ℕ) := Nat.le_of_not_gt hj
      have hi_ltN : e (i : ℕ) < (N : ℤ) := by
        rw [h1 (i : ℕ) hi]
        exact hs_lt (s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩) (List.get_mem s ⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩)
      have hj_geN : (N : ℤ) ≤ e (j : ℕ) := by
        rw [h2 (j : ℕ) hj_ge]
        exact_mod_cast Nat.le_add_right N ((j : ℕ) - s.length)
      omega
  · have hi_ge : s.length ≤ (i : ℕ) := Nat.le_of_not_gt hi
    by_cases hj : (j : ℕ) < s.length
    · have hj_ltN : e (j : ℕ) < (N : ℤ) := by
        rw [h1 (j : ℕ) hj]
        exact hs_lt (s.get ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩) (List.get_mem s ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩)
      have hi_geN : (N : ℤ) ≤ e (i : ℕ) := by
        rw [h2 (i : ℕ) hi_ge]
        exact_mod_cast Nat.le_add_right N ((i : ℕ) - s.length)
      omega
    · have hj_ge : s.length ≤ (j : ℕ) := Nat.le_of_not_gt hj
      rw [h2 (i : ℕ) hi_ge, h2 (j : ℕ) hj_ge] at hij
      omega
have hp_nd : p.Nodup := by
  dsimp [p]
  rw [List.nodup_ofFn]
  exact hinj_fin
have hp_take : List.take s.length p = s := by
  apply List.ext_getElem
  · simp [p, List.length_take, List.length_ofFn]

lemma ProofSteps.diag_prefix_injective {α : Type} (l : ℕ → List α)
    (hprefix : ∀ a b : ℕ, a ≤ b → List.IsPrefix (l a) (l b))
    (hnd : ∀ k : ℕ, (l k).Nodup)
    (hlen : ∀ n : ℕ, n < (l (n+1)).length) :
    Function.Injective (fun n : ℕ => (l (n+1)).get ⟨n, hlen n⟩)

by
    intro a b hab
    by_cases hle : a ≤ b
    · have hp : List.IsPrefix (l (a+1)) (l (b+1)) := hprefix (a+1) (b+1) (Nat.succ_le_succ hle)
      have hget : (l (b+1)).get ⟨a, lt_of_lt_of_le (hlen a) (List.IsPrefix.length_le hp)⟩ =
          (l (b+1)).get ⟨b, hlen b⟩ := by
        exact (ProofSteps.prefix_get_eq (l (a+1)) (l (b+1)) hp ⟨a, hlen a⟩).symm.trans hab
      have hfin := (List.Nodup.get_inj_iff (hnd (b+1))).mp hget
      simpa using congrArg Fin.val hfin
    · have hba : b ≤ a := le_of_not_ge hle
      have hp : List.IsPrefix (l (b+1)) (l (a+1)) := hprefix (b+1) (a+1) (Nat.succ_le_succ hba)
      have hget : (l (a+1)).get ⟨b, lt_of_lt_of_le (hlen b) (List.IsPrefix.length_le hp)⟩ =
          (l (a+1)).get ⟨a, hlen a⟩ := by
        exact (ProofSteps.prefix_get_eq (l (b+1)) (l (a+1)) hp ⟨b, hlen b⟩).symm.trans hab.symm
      have hfin := (List.Nodup.get_inj_iff (hnd (a+1))).mp hget
      simpa using (congrArg Fin.val hfin).symm

nodes.claim: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
nodes.statement:
theorem fcs76_collections_exist :
  ∃ C1 C2 : Set {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
    (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C1 →
      ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
        g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
    (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C2 →
      ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
        g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
    ¬ (∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
      ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ (C1 ∪ C2) →
        ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
          ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
              List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))

lemma ProofSteps.diag_tail (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    (hgen : ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
      L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
          {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e i)) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e i)) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e i))
    (s : List ℤ) (N n : ℕ)
    (hs_nd : s.Nodup)
    (hs_lt : ∀ z ∈ s, z < (N : ℤ))
    (hs_gt : ∀ z ∈ s, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) < z) :

      (∃ rest : List ℤ, q = s ++ rest) ∧
      q.Nodup ∧
      s.length < q.length ∧
      (∀ z ∈ q, z < (N' : ℤ)) ∧
      (∀ z ∈ q, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) < z) ∧
      0 < v ∧
      v = h q ∧
      v ∉ q ∧
      (N : ℤ) < (N' : ℤ) ∧
      v < (N' : ℤ) ∧

let neg : ℕ → ℤ := fun n => (-(n : ℤ) - 1)
let last : ℕ → List ℤ := fun n => if n = 0 then [] else [neg (n-1)]
let State := ((List ℤ × List ℤ) × (ℕ × ℤ)) × (List ℤ × ℕ)
let full : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.1
let q : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.2
let cut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.1.2.1
let recv : State → ℤ := fun p => p.1.2.2
let prev : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.2.1
let prevCut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.2.2
let mk : List ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → State :=
  fun f qq c r p pc => (((f, qq), (c, r)), (p, pc))
let Pre : ℕ → State → Prop := fun n p =>
  (full p).Nodup ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), z < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), neg n < z) ∧
  n ≤ (full p).length ∧
  (full p) = (q p) ++ (last n) ∧
  (∃ rest : List ℤ, (q p) = (prev p) ++ rest) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (0 < (recv p) ∧ (recv p) = h (q p) ∧ (recv p) ∉ (q p) ∧ (recv p) < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ))) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (prevCut p) < (cut p)) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (∀ z ∈ (q p), z ∈ (prev p) ∨ ((prevCut p : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ z))

let baseState : State := mk [] [] 0 0 [] 0
have hbase : Pre 0 baseState := by

have mainstep : ∀ (n : ℕ) (p : State), Pre n p → ∃ p' : State, Pre (n+1) p' := by
  intro n p hp
  unfold Pre at hp
  rcases hp with ⟨hpnd, hp_lt, hp_gt, hplen, hpfq, hpqprev, hprec, hpcut, hpsep⟩
  have hgtm : ∀ z ∈ full p, neg (n+1) < z := by
    intro z hz
    have hn : neg (n+1) < neg n := by
      dsimp [neg]
      omega
    exact lt_trans hn (hp_gt z hz)
  rcases ProofSteps.diag_tail h hgen (full p) (cut p) (n+1) hpnd hp_lt hgtm with
    ⟨qq, N', v, hpref, hnd, hgrow, hqlt, hqgt, hvpos, hveq, hvnot, hNlt, hvlt, hsep⟩
  have hn0 : n + 1 ≠ 0 := by omega
  have hlast : last (n + 1) = [neg n] := by simp [last, hn0]
  let full' : List ℤ := qq ++ last (n+1)
  let p' : State := mk full' qq N' v (full p) (cut p)
  have hfull_eq_sing : full p' = qq ++ [neg n] := by
    simp only [p', full', full, mk]
    rw [hlast]
  have hq_gt_neg : ∀ z ∈ qq, neg n < z := by
    intro z hz
    rcases hsep z hz with hzs | hzN
    · exact hp_gt z hzs
    · have hneg0 : neg n < 0 := by dsimp [neg]; omega
      have h0le : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (cut p : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.zero_le (cut p)
      have h0lez : (0 : ℤ) ≤ z := le_trans h0le hzN
      exact lt_of_lt_of_le hneg0 h0lez
  have hfull_nd : (full p').Nodup := by
    have hneg_nd : [neg n].Nodup := by simp
    have hdisj : List.Disjoint qq [neg n] := by
      intro z hz hzsing
      have hzneg : z = neg n := by simpa using hzsing
      have hzgt : neg n < z := hq_gt_neg z hz
      rw [hzneg] at hzgt
      exact (lt_irrefl (neg n) hzgt)
    rw [hfull_eq_sing]
    exact List.Nodup.append hnd hneg_nd hdisj
  have hfull_lt : ∀ z ∈ full p', z < (cut p' : ℤ) := by
    intro z hz
    have hzm : z ∈ qq ++ [neg n] := by
      rw [hfull_eq_sing] at hz
      exact hz
    rw [List.mem_append] at hzm
    rcases hzm with hzq | hzsing
    · simpa [p', cut, mk] using hqlt z hzq
    · have hzneg : z = neg n := by simpa using hzsing
      rw [hzneg]
      have hneg0 : neg n < 0 := by dsimp [neg]; omega
      have h0le : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (cut p : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.zero_le (cut p)

    intro z hz
    have hzm : z ∈ qq ++ [neg n] := by
      rw [hfull_eq_sing] at hz
      exact hz
    rw [List.mem_append] at hzm
    rcases hzm with hzq | hzsing
    · exact hqgt z hzq
    · have hzneg : z = neg n := by simpa using hzsing

      have hneglt : neg (n+1) < neg n := by dsimp [neg]; omega

  have hfull_len : n + 1 ≤ (full p').length := by
    rw [hfull_eq_sing]
    simp
    omega
  have hfull_eq : full p' = q p' ++ last (n+1) := by

    right
    refine ⟨hvpos, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · simpa [p', recv, q, mk] using hveq
    · simpa [p', recv, q, mk] using hvnot
    · simpa [p', recv, cut, mk] using hvlt
  have hcut' : (n+1 = 0 ∨ prevCut p' < cut p') := by
    right
    have hNlt' : cut p < N' := by exact_mod_cast hNlt
    simpa [p', prevCut, cut, mk] using hNlt'
  have hsep' : (n+1 = 0 ∨ ∀ z ∈ q p', z ∈ prev p' ∨ (prevCut p' : ℤ) ≤ z) := by
    right
    intro z hz
    have hz' : z ∈ qq := by simpa [p', q, mk] using hz
    rcases hsep z hz' with hzs | hzN
    · left
      simpa [p', prev, mk] using hzs
    · right
      simpa [p', prevCut, mk] using hzN
  have hp' : Pre (n+1) p' := by
    exact ⟨hfull_nd, hfull_lt, hfull_gt, hfull_len, hfull_eq, hqprev, hrec', hcut', hsep'⟩
  exact ⟨p', hp'⟩

let recG : ∀ n : ℕ, { p : State // Pre n p } :=

    (fun n ih => ⟨(stepRes n ih.1 ih.2).1, (stepRes n ih.1 ih.2).2.1⟩) n
let G : ℕ → State := fun n => (recG n).1

  intro n
  exact (recG n).2

    rw [hpfq, hqstep]
    simp [List.append_assoc]

result.statement: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
result.proof: Take the nonnegative integers as points p_n = n and the negative integers as points m_n = −n−1. Let C₁ be the languages whose carrier contains some tail {p_{N+j} : j ≥ 0}, and C₂ the languages whose carrier contains every m_n. The sequence (p_n) is injective and generates each member of C₁ after its cutoff, giving non-uniform sample-free generation; the sequence (m_n) generates each member of C₂ from time zero, giving uniform sample-free generation. Freshness reduces to membership together with absence of earlier repetition, which holds because both sequences are injective. For the negative clause, assume some sample-based generator G generates the union in the limit. Build nested finite injective prefixes together with strictly increasing cutoffs: given a stage prefix s and cutoff N, enumerate s followed by the positive tail from N; this enumeration belongs to C₁, so G must eventually output a fresh value, which cannot be a previously listed element and hence is some p_k with k ≥ N. Extend the prefix by that observed enumeration prefix and append the next negative point m_n, choosing a fresh larger cutoff so that p_k occurs neither in the new prefix nor in its future positive tail. Induction shows p_k is never reproduced later. The nested prefixes converge to an injective sequence x whose range is infinite and contains every negative point, so it is the carrier of a language in C₂ that x enumerates. At each stage time the prefix of x agrees with the recorded stage prefix, so G outputs p_k, which lies outside this limiting language; since these failures occur arbitrarily late, G fails to generate in the limit, a contradiction. Hence the union is not generatable in the limit, and the constructed collections witness the claim.

let neg : ℕ → ℤ := fun n => (-(n : ℤ) - 1)
let last : ℕ → List ℤ := fun n => if n = 0 then [] else [neg (n-1)]
let State := ((List ℤ × List ℤ) × (ℕ × ℤ)) × (List ℤ × ℕ)
let full : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.1
let q : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.2
let cut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.1.2.1
let recv : State → ℤ := fun p => p.1.2.2
let prev : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.2.1
let prevCut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.2.2
let mk : List ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → State :=
  fun f qq c r p pc => (((f, qq), (c, r)), (p, pc))
let Pre : ℕ → State → Prop := fun n p =>
  (full p).Nodup ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), z < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), neg n < z) ∧
  n ≤ (full p).length ∧
  (full p) = (q p) ++ (last n) ∧
  (∃ rest : List ℤ, (q p) = (prev p) ++ rest) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (0 < (recv p) ∧ (recv p) = h (q p) ∧ (recv p) ∉ (q p) ∧ (recv p) < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ))) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (prevCut p) < (cut p)) ∧

    intro z hz
    have hz' : z ∈ qq := by simpa [p', q, mk] using hz

    exact ⟨hfull_nd, hfull_lt, hfull_gt, hfull_len, hfull_eq, hqprev, hrec', hcut', hsep'⟩

let neg : ℕ → ℤ := fun n => (-(n : ℤ) - 1)
let last : ℕ → List ℤ := fun n => if n = 0 then [] else [neg (n-1)]
let State := ((List ℤ × List ℤ) × (ℕ × ℤ)) × (List ℤ × ℕ)
let full : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.1
let q : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.2
let cut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.1.2.1
let recv : State → ℤ := fun p => p.1.2.2
let prev : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.2.1
let prevCut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.2.2
let mk : List ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → State :=
  fun f qq c r p pc => (((f, qq), (c, r)), (p, pc))
let Pre : ℕ → State → Prop := fun n p =>
  (full p).Nodup ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), z < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), neg n < z) ∧
  n ≤ (full p).length ∧
  (full p) = (q p) ++ (last n) ∧
  (∃ rest : List ℤ, (q p) = (prev p) ++ rest) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (0 < (recv p) ∧ (recv p) = h (q p) ∧ (recv p) ∉ (q p) ∧ (recv p) < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ))) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (prevCut p) < (cut p)) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (∀ z ∈ (q p), z ∈ (prev p) ∨ ((prevCut p : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ z))

let baseState : State := mk [] [] 0 0 [] 0
have hbase : Pre 0 baseState := by
  simp [Pre, baseState, full, q, cut, recv, prev, prevCut, mk, last]
have mainstep : ∀ (n : ℕ) (p : State), Pre n p → ∃ p' : State, Pre (n+1) p' := by
  intro n p hp
  unfold Pre at hp
  rcases hp with ⟨hpnd, hp_lt, hp_gt, hplen, hpfq, hpqprev, hprec, hpcut, hpsep⟩
  have hgtm : ∀ z ∈ full p, neg (n+1) < z := by
    intro z hz
    have hn : neg (n+1) < neg n := by
      dsimp [neg]
      omega
    exact lt_trans hn (hp_gt z hz)
  rcases ProofSteps.diag_tail h hgen (full p) (cut p) (n+1) hpnd hp_lt hgtm with
    ⟨qq, N', v, hpref, hnd, hgrow, hqlt, hqgt, hvpos, hveq, hvnot, hNlt, hvlt, hsep⟩
  have hn0 : n + 1 ≠ 0 := by omega
  have hlast : last (n + 1) = [neg n] := by simp [last, hn0]
  let full' : List ℤ := qq ++ last (n+1)
  let p' : State := mk full' qq N' v (full p) (cut p)
  have hfull_eq_sing : full p' = qq ++ [neg n] := by
    simp only [p', full', full, mk]
    rw [hlast]
  have hq_gt_neg : ∀ z ∈ qq, neg n < z := by
    intro z hz
    rcases hsep z hz with hzs | hzN
    · exact hp_gt z hzs
    · have hneg0 : neg n < 0 := by dsimp [neg]; omega
      have h0le : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (cut p : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.zero_le (cut p)
      have h0lez : (0 : ℤ) ≤ z := le_trans h0le hzN
      exact lt_of_lt_of_le hneg0 h0lez
  have hfull_nd : (full p').Nodup := by
    have hneg_nd : [neg n].Nodup := by simp
    have hdisj : List.Disjoint qq [neg n] := by
      intro z hz hzsing
      have hzneg : z = neg n := by simpa using hzsing
      have hzgt : neg n < z := hq_gt_neg z hz
      rw [hzneg] at hzgt
      exact (lt_irrefl (neg n) hzgt)
    rw [hfull_eq_sing]
    exact List.Nodup.append hnd hneg_nd hdisj
  have hfull_lt : ∀ z ∈ full p', z < (cut p' : ℤ) := by
    intro z hz
    have hzm : z ∈ qq ++ [neg n] := by
      rw [hfull_eq_sing] at hz
      exact hz
    rw [List.mem_append] at hzm
    rcases hzm with hzq | hzsing
    · simpa [p', cut, mk] using hqlt z hzq
    · have hzneg : z = neg n := by simpa using hzsing
      rw [hzneg]
      have hneg0 : neg n < 0 := by dsimp [neg]; omega
      have h0le : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (cut p : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.zero_le (cut p)
      have hnegcut : neg n < (cut p : ℤ) := lt_of_lt_of_le hneg0 h0le

  have hfull_gt : ∀ z ∈ full p', neg (n+1) < z := by
    intro z hz
    have hzm : z ∈ qq ++ [neg n] := by
      rw [hfull_eq_sing] at hz
      exact hz
    rw [List.mem_append] at hzm
    rcases hzm with hzq | hzsing
    · exact hqgt z hzq
    · have hzneg : z = neg n := by simpa using hzsing

      have hneglt : neg (n+1) < neg n := by dsimp [neg]; omega

    rw [hfull_eq_sing]
    simp

result.statement: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
result.proof: Take the nonnegative integers as points p_n = n and the negative integers as points m_n = −n−1. Let C₁ be the languages whose carrier contains some tail {p_{N+j} : j ≥ 0}, and C₂ the languages whose carrier contains every m_n. The sequence (p_n) is injective and generates each member of C₁ after its cutoff, giving non-uniform sample-free generation; the sequence (m_n) generates each member of C₂ from time zero, giving uniform sample-free generation. Freshness reduces to membership together with absence of earlier repetition, which holds because both sequences are injective. For the negative clause, assume some sample-based generator G generates the union in the limit. Build nested finite injective prefixes together with strictly increasing cutoffs: given a stage prefix s and cutoff N, enumerate s followed by the positive tail from N; this enumeration belongs to C₁, so G must eventually output a fresh value, which cannot be a previously listed element and hence is some p_k with k ≥ N. Extend the prefix by that observed enumeration prefix and append the next negative point m_n, choosing a fresh larger cutoff so that p_k occurs neither in the new prefix nor in its future positive tail. Induction shows p_k is never reproduced later. The nested prefixes converge to an injective sequence x whose range is infinite and contains every negative point, so it is the carrier of a language in C₂ that x enumerates. At each stage time the prefix of x agrees with the recorded stage prefix, so G outputs p_k, which lies outside this limiting language; since these failures occur arbitrarily late, G fails to generate in the limit, a contradiction. Hence the union is not generatable in the limit, and the constructed collections witness the claim.

nodes.claim: Assuming a generator h : List ℤ → ℤ and its union-generation property hgen, construct the diagonal enumeration xG of an infinite C₂ language (containing every negative point) and derive False by applying hgen to a late stage where h output is a fresh positive record outside that language.
nodes.proof_hint: Recursively run diag_tail to build nested nodup prefixes and strictly increasing cutoffs; append negative points to make full stages. Define the diagonal sequence xG and use diag_prefix_injective for injectivity. Prove range xG is infinite and contains every negative point, so xG enumerates a C₂ language. Apply hgen, then choose a late stage whose List.ofFn equals the stage prefix q so the fresh record v = h q is positive but outside range xG, contradiction.

lemma ProofSteps.hqfull_of_hpre
    {State : Type}
    (full q : State → List ℤ) (neg : ℕ → ℤ) (last : ℕ → List ℤ)
    (G : ℕ → State)
    (hpre : ∀ k : ℕ, full (G (k+1)) = q (G (k+1)) ++ last (k+1))
    (hlast : ∀ k : ℕ, last (k+1) = [neg k]) :

lemma ProofSteps.negative_injective : Function.Injective (fun n : ℕ => (-(n : ℤ) - 1))

lemma ProofSteps.diag_tail (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    (hgen : ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
      L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
          {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e i)) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e i)) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e i))
    (s : List ℤ) (N n : ℕ)
    (hs_nd : s.Nodup)
    (hs_lt : ∀ z ∈ s, z < (N : ℤ))
    (hs_gt : ∀ z ∈ s, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) < z) :
    ∃ q : List ℤ, ∃ N' : ℕ, ∃ v : ℤ,
      (∃ rest : List ℤ, q = s ++ rest) ∧
      q.Nodup ∧
      s.length < q.length ∧
      (∀ z ∈ q, z < (N' : ℤ)) ∧
      (∀ z ∈ q, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) < z) ∧
      0 < v ∧
      v = h q ∧
      v ∉ q ∧
      (N : ℤ) < (N' : ℤ) ∧
      v < (N' : ℤ) ∧
      (∀ z ∈ q, z ∈ s ∨ (N : ℤ) ≤ z)

lemma ProofSteps.diag_q_ofFn_at {State : Type}
    (full q : State → List ℤ) (G : ℕ → State) (neg : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ)
    (hprefix : ∀ a b : ℕ, a ≤ b → List.IsPrefix (full (G a)) (full (G b)))
    (hsing : full (G (n + 1)) = q (G (n + 1)) ++ [neg n])
    (hdlen : ∀ k : ℕ, k < (full (G (k + 1))).length) :
    List.ofFn (fun i : Fin (q (G (n + 1))).length =>
      (full (G (i.1 + 1))).get ⟨i.1, hdlen i.1⟩) = q (G (n + 1))

lemma ProofSteps.diag_prefix_injective {α : Type} (l : ℕ → List α)
    (hprefix : ∀ a b : ℕ, a ≤ b → List.IsPrefix (l a) (l b))
    (hnd : ∀ k : ℕ, (l k).Nodup)
    (hlen : ∀ n : ℕ, n < (l (n+1)).length) :
    Function.Injective (fun n : ℕ => (l (n+1)).get ⟨n, hlen n⟩)

lemma ProofSteps.diag_records_neg_diag {State : Type} (full q : State → List ℤ)
    (G : ℕ → State) (neg : ℕ → ℤ) (n m : ℕ)
    (hm : m = (q (G (n + 1))).length)
    (hpref : List.IsPrefix (full (G (n + 1))) (full (G (m + 1))))
    (hsing : full (G (n + 1)) = q (G (n + 1)) ++ [neg n])
    (hmem : m < (full (G (n + 1))).length) :
    (full (G (m + 1))).get ⟨m, lt_of_lt_of_le hmem (List.IsPrefix.length_le hpref)⟩ = neg n

  (full p).Nodup ∧
