          {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) :
    ∃ x : ℕ → ℤ,
      Function.Injective x ∧
      (Set.range x).Infinite ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ Set.range x) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ r : ℕ, n ≤ r ∧
        0 < h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => x (i : ℕ))) ∧
        h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => x (i : ℕ))) ∉ Set.range x

let neg : ℕ → ℤ := fun n => (-(n : ℤ) - 1)
let last : ℕ → List ℤ := fun n => if n = 0 then [] else [neg (n-1)]
let State := ((List ℤ × List ℤ) × (ℕ × ℤ)) × (List ℤ × ℕ)
let full : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.1
let q : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.2
let cut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.1.2.1
let recv : State → ℤ := fun p => p.1.2.2
let prev : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.2.1
let prevCut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.2.2
let mk : List ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → State :=
  fun f qq c r p pc => (((f, qq), (c, r)), (p, pc))
let Pre : ℕ → State → Prop := fun n p =>
  (full p).Nodup ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), z < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), neg n < z) ∧
  n ≤ (full p).length ∧
  (full p) = (q p) ++ (last n) ∧
  (∃ rest : List ℤ, (q p) = (prev p) ++ rest) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (0 < (recv p) ∧ (recv p) = h (q p) ∧ (recv p) ∉ (q p) ∧ (recv p) < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ))) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (prevCut p) < (cut p)) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (∀ z ∈ (q p), z ∈ (prev p) ∨ ((prevCut p : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ z))
let baseState : State := mk [] [] 0 0 [] 0
have hbase : Pre 0 baseState := by
  simp [Pre, baseState, full, q, cut, recv, prev, prevCut, mk, last]
skip
let Gfull : (k : ℕ) → {s : State // Pre k s} :=
  Nat.rec ⟨baseState, hbase⟩ (fun k ih =>
    let s : State := ih.1
    let dt := ProofSteps.diag_tail h hgen (full s) (cut s) k ih.2.1 ih.2.2.1 ih.2.2.2.1
    let qq : List ℤ := Classical.choose dt
    let dt2 := Classical.choose_spec dt
    let N' : ℕ := Classical.choose dt2
    let dt3 := Classical.choose_spec dt2
    let v : ℤ := Classical.choose dt3
    let hspec := Classical.choose_spec dt3
    let s' : State := mk (qq ++ [neg k]) qq N' v (full s) (cut s)
    ⟨s', ?_⟩)
rcases hspec with ⟨hqf, hqnd, hqlen, hqlt, hqgt, hv0, hv_eq, hv_not, hcut_lt, hvN, hqsep⟩
rcases ih.2 with ⟨hnd, hlt, hgt, hlen, hfull, hqprev, hrec, hcut, hsep⟩
dsimp [Pre, s', full, q, cut, recv, prev, prevCut, mk]
refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
· apply List.Nodup.append
  · exact hqnd
  · simp
  · intro z hzq hzn
    rw [List.mem_singleton] at hzn
    subst z
    have : neg k < neg k := hqgt (neg k) hzq
    dsimp [neg] at this
    omega
· intro z hz
  rw [List.mem_append] at hz
  rcases hz with hzq | hzn
  · exact hqlt z hzq
  · rw [List.mem_singleton] at hzn
    subst z
    have hN : (0 : ℤ) < (N' : ℤ) := lt_trans hv0 hvN
    have hneg : neg k < (0 : ℤ) := by
      dsimp [neg]
      omega
    exact lt_trans hneg hN
· intro z hz
  rw [List.mem_append] at hz
  rcases hz with hzq | hzn
  · have hz' : neg k < z := hqgt z hzq
    have hneg : neg (k + 1) < neg k := by
      dsimp [neg]
      omega
    exact lt_trans hneg hz'
  · rw [List.mem_singleton] at hzn
    subst z
    dsimp [neg]
    omega
· rw [List.length_append, List.length_singleton]
  exact Nat.succ_le_succ (Nat.le_of_lt (lt_of_le_of_lt hlen hqlen))
· simpa [last, Nat.succ_ne_zero k, Nat.add_sub_cancel_right]
· exact hqf
· right
  exact ⟨hv0, hv_eq, hv_not, hvN⟩
· right
  simpa [N'] using hcut_lt
· right
  exact hqsep
let G : ℕ → State := fun k => (Gfull k).1
let HPG : ∀ k, Pre k (G k) := fun k => (Gfull k).2
have hpre : ∀ k, full (G (k+1)) = q (G (k+1)) ++ last (k+1) :=
  fun k => (HPG (k+1)).2.2.2.2.1
have hlast : ∀ k, last (k+1) = [neg k] := by
  intro k
  simp [last, Nat.succ_ne_zero k, Nat.add_sub_cancel_right]
have hfullG := ProofSteps.hqfull_of_hpre full q neg last G hpre hlast
have hprevG : ∀ k, prev (G (k+1)) = full (G k) := by
  intro k
  rfl
have hprevCutG : ∀ k, prevCut (G (k+1)) = cut (G k) := by
  intro k
  rfl
have hdlen : ∀ k, k < (full (G (k+1))).length := by
  intro k
  have hlen : k + 1 ≤ (full (G (k+1))).length := (HPG (k+1)).2.2.2.1
  omega
let xG : ℕ → ℤ := fun n => (full (G (n+1))).get ⟨n, hdlen n⟩
have hxG : ∀ k, xG k = (full (G (k+1))).get ⟨k, hdlen k⟩ := by
  intro k
  rfl
have hqprev_step : ∀ k, List.IsPrefix (full (G k)) (q (G (k+1))) := by
  intro k
  rcases (HPG (k+1)).2.2.2.2.2.1 with ⟨rest, hqeq⟩
  have h : List.IsPrefix (prev (G (k+1))) (q (G (k+1))) := by
    rw [hqeq]
    exact List.prefix_append (prev (G (k+1))) rest
  simpa [hprevG k] using h
have hstep_prefix : ∀ k, List.IsPrefix (full (G k)) (full (G (k+1))) := by
  intro k
  have hqfp : List.IsPrefix (q (G (k+1))) (full (G (k+1))) := by
    rw [hfullG k]
    exact List.prefix_append (q (G (k+1))) [neg k]
  exact List.IsPrefix.trans (hqprev_step k) hqfp
have hprefix : ∀ a b, a ≤ b → List.IsPrefix (full (G a)) (full (G b)) := by
  intro a b hab
  induction b generalizing a with
  | zero =>
      have ha0 : a = 0 := by omega
      subst a
      simpa using List.prefix_append (full (G 0)) []
  | succ b ih =>
      by_cases hle : a ≤ b
      · exact List.IsPrefix.trans (ih a hle) (hstep_prefix b)
      · have ha : a = b + 1 := by omega
        subst a
        simpa using List.prefix_append (full (G (b+1))) []
have hnodup : ∀ k, (full (G k)).Nodup := fun k => (HPG k).1
have hcut_inc : ∀ k, cut (G k) < cut (G (k+1)) := by
  intro k
  have h := (HPG (k+1)).2.2.2.2.2.2.2.1
  have hn : k + 1 ≠ 0 := Nat.succ_ne_zero k
  have hlt : prevCut (G (k+1)) < cut (G (k+1)) := h.resolve_left hn
  simpa [hprevCutG k] using hlt
have hsep : ∀ k, 1 ≤ k → ∀ z ∈ q (G k), z ∈ prev (G k) ∨ (prevCut (G k) : ℤ) ≤ z := by
  intro k hk
  have h := (HPG k).2.2.2.2.2.2.2.2
  have hn : k ≠ 0 := by omega
  exact h.resolve_left hn
have hneg_neg : ∀ k, neg k < 0 := by
  intro k
  dsimp [neg]
  omega
have hpre_spec := ProofSteps.diag_records_pre_spec h neg last
have hx_inj : Function.Injective xG :=
  ProofSteps.diag_prefix_injective (fun k => full (G k)) hprefix hnodup hdlen
have hrange : (Set.range xG).Infinite :=
  Set.infinite_range_of_injective hx_inj
have hqlen_ge : ∀ n, n ≤ (q (G (n+1))).length := by
  intro n
  have hlen : n + 1 ≤ (full (G (n+1))).length := (HPG (n+1)).2.2.2.1
  have hf := hfullG n
  rw [hf] at hlen
  simp at hlen
  omega
have hlate : ∀ n, h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin (q (G (n+1))).length => xG i)) ∉ Set.range xG :=
  fun n => ProofSteps.diag_records_nmem_from_spec
    h full q cut recv prev prevCut neg last G xG n Pre
    hpre_spec HPG hdlen hxG hprevG hprevCutG hprefix hlast hneg_neg

result.statement: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
result.proof: Take the nonnegative integers as points p_n = n and the negative integers as points m_n = −n−1. Let C₁ be the languages whose carrier contains some tail {p_{N+j} : j ≥ 0}, and C₂ the languages whose carrier contains every m_n. The sequence (p_n) is injective and generates each member of C₁ after its cutoff, giving non-uniform sample-free generation; the sequence (m_n) generates each member of C₂ from time zero, giving uniform sample-free generation. Freshness reduces to membership together with absence of earlier repetition, which holds because both sequences are injective. For the negative clause, assume some sample-based generator G generates the union in the limit. Build nested finite injective prefixes together with strictly increasing cutoffs: given a stage prefix s and cutoff N, enumerate s followed by the positive tail from N; this enumeration belongs to C₁, so G must eventually output a fresh value, which cannot be a previously listed element and hence is some p_k with k ≥ N. Extend the prefix by that observed enumeration prefix and append the next negative point m_n, choosing a fresh larger cutoff so that p_k occurs neither in the new prefix nor in its future positive tail. Induction shows p_k is never reproduced later. The nested prefixes converge to an injective sequence x whose range is infinite and contains every negative point, so it is the carrier of a language in C₂ that x enumerates. At each stage time the prefix of x agrees with the recorded stage prefix, so G outputs p_k, which lies outside this limiting language; since these failures occur arbitrarily late, G fails to generate in the limit, a contradiction. Hence the union is not generatable in the limit, and the constructed collections witness the claim.

data.main_source:
theorem ProofReviewed_diag_records (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    (hgen : ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
      L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
          {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) :
    ∃ x : ℕ → ℤ,
      Function.Injective x ∧
      (Set.range x).Infinite ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ Set.range x) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ r : ℕ, n ≤ r ∧
        0 < h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => x (i : ℕ))) ∧
        h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => x (i : ℕ))) ∉ Set.range x

theorem ProofReviewed_diag_records (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    (hgen : ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
      L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
          {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) :
    ∃ x : ℕ → ℤ,
      Function.Injective x ∧
      (Set.range x).Infinite ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ Set.range x) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ r : ℕ, n ≤ r ∧
        0 < h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => x (i : ℕ))) ∧
        h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => x (i : ℕ))) ∉ Set.range x

result.statement: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
result.proof: Take the nonnegative integers as points p_n = n and the negative integers as points m_n = −n−1. Let C₁ be the languages whose carrier contains some tail {p_{N+j} : j ≥ 0}, and C₂ the languages whose carrier contains every m_n. The sequence (p_n) is injective and generates each member of C₁ after its cutoff, giving non-uniform sample-free generation; the sequence (m_n) generates each member of C₂ from time zero, giving uniform sample-free generation. Freshness reduces to membership together with absence of earlier repetition, which holds because both sequences are injective. For the negative clause, assume some sample-based generator G generates the union in the limit. Build nested finite injective prefixes together with strictly increasing cutoffs: given a stage prefix s and cutoff N, enumerate s followed by the positive tail from N; this enumeration belongs to C₁, so G must eventually output a fresh value, which cannot be a previously listed element and hence is some p_k with k ≥ N. Extend the prefix by that observed enumeration prefix and append the next negative point m_n, choosing a fresh larger cutoff so that p_k occurs neither in the new prefix nor in its future positive tail. Induction shows p_k is never reproduced later. The nested prefixes converge to an injective sequence x whose range is infinite and contains every negative point, so it is the carrier of a language in C₂ that x enumerates. At each stage time the prefix of x agrees with the recorded stage prefix, so G outputs p_k, which lies outside this limiting language; since these failures occur arbitrarily late, G fails to generate in the limit, a contradiction. Hence the union is not generatable in the limit, and the constructed collections witness the claim.

    (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C2 →
      ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
        g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
    ¬ (∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,

          ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉

nodes.claim: For State-valued stages G with full, q and tail last, if every stage satisfies full (G (k+1)) = q (G (k+1)) ++ last (k+1) and last (k+1) = [neg k], then full (G (k+1)) = q (G (k+1)) ++ [neg k].
nodes.proof_hint: intro k; rewrite with hpre k and hlast k.

nodes.claim: For every N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) is the range of i ↦ (N + i : ℤ), and that range is infinite.
nodes.proof_hint: For range equality split into two inclusions via Nat subtraction and exact_mod_cast; for infinity use Set.infinite_range_of_injective with Nat.cast injectivity.

nodes.claim: The map n ↦ (-(n : ℤ) - 1) is injective.
nodes.proof_hint: Unfold inequality; use omega/norm_num on the two integer equations to deduce m = n from m < n.

nodes.claim: For s : List ℤ, N : ℕ and e : ℕ → ℤ with e n = (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ) whenever s.length ≤ n, one has Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ Set.range e.
nodes.proof_hint: Use pos_tail_range to write x in Ici N as N+j, choose n = s.length+j, then use the tail description and omega.

nodes.claim: For s : List ℤ, N : ℕ and e : ℕ → ℤ with e n = (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ) whenever s.length ≤ n, the set Set.range e is infinite.
nodes.proof_hint: Use stage_enum_range_ci and the fact that Set.Ici (N:ℤ) is infinite together with Set.Infinite.mono.

nodes.claim: Given generator h and its union property, a finite injective prefix f : Fin l → ℤ and cutoff N, there is a longer finite injective prefix f' starting with f, a fresh positive value p_k with k ≥ N achieved by h on the stage enumeration, and a larger cutoff N' avoiding p_k on future positive tails.
nodes.proof_hint: Construct the stage enumeration by pasting f and the positive tail from N; define the resulting infinite language L as its range; prove L lies in C1 and apply hgen; the obtained fresh integer is a positive tail element p_k not in the earlier prefix; extend f by the enumeration prefix through time t and append the next negative point, then choose N' = k+1.

nodes.claim: For a good stage prefix s with cutoff N and lower bound m_n, the diag_step construction yields q extending s, nodup, growing, below a larger cutoff N', all entries above m_n, plus the fresh positive record v = h q not in q and below N'.
nodes.proof_hint: rcases ProofSteps.diag_step; let q = List.ofFn e r; derive upper bound by showing r <= k from v notin q, and lower bound from the prefix/tail description with hs_gt and nonnegativity; use omega for the cutoff comparisons.

nodes.claim: For a good stage prefix s with cutoff N and lower bound avoiding the next negative point, the diag_step construction yields q extending s, nodup, length-growing, all below larger N', avoiding -n-1, plus the fresh positive record v equal to h q, not in q, and below N'; the cutoff strictly increases.
nodes.proof_hint: rcases ProofSteps.diag_step into e,N',r,v; take q = List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e i); copy the diag_next_spec upper and avoidance arguments, and retain hv_eq, hv_not, hv0, hvN' plus prove N<N' from N≤v and v<N'.

nodes.claim: For a good stage prefix s and cutoff N with lower bound -n, the diag_step construction produces a finite prefix q extending s by at least one element, nodup, all entries below a strictly larger cutoff N', and avoiding the next negative point -n-1.
nodes.proof_hint: rcases ProofSteps.diag_step into e,N',r,v; take q = List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e i); use the prefix-extension, nodup, acuteness and v<N' facts plus hs_low to derive all bounds by omega.

nodes.claim: For a good stage prefix s with cutoff N and lower bound -n-1, the diag_step construction yields q extending s, nodup, growing, all below a strictly larger N', all above -n-1, a fresh positive record v = h q with v not in q and below N', and every entry of q lies either in s or is at least N.

nodes.proof_hint: Use Nat.succ_ne_zero and rewrite the if with ite_eq_right, then Nat.add_sub_cancel_right.

nodes.claim: For stages whose full list at stage k+1 appends neg k after q, any value that first appears at or after stage n+1 but is not in q (G (n+1)) is either negative or at least cut (G (n+1)).

For r=t+1 rewrite full as q ++ [neg t]; the singleton tail is negative, and a q member either lies in prev (the previous full list, so apply induction to t) or is at least prevCut, which rewrites to cut (G t) and is at least cut (G (n+1)) by iterating hcut_inc. Handle r=0 as impossible.

lemma ProofSteps.hqfull_of_hpre
    {State : Type}
    (full q : State → List ℤ) (neg : ℕ → ℤ) (last : ℕ → List ℤ)
    (G : ℕ → State)
    (hpre : ∀ k : ℕ, full (G (k+1)) = q (G (k+1)) ++ last (k+1))
    (hlast : ∀ k : ℕ, last (k+1) = [neg k]) :
    ∀ k : ℕ, full (G (k+1)) = q (G (k+1)) ++ [neg k]
lemma ProofSteps.negative_injective : Function.Injective (fun n : ℕ => (-(n : ℤ) - 1))

lemma ProofSteps.diag_tail (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    (hgen : ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
      L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
          {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e i)) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e i)) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e i))
    (s : List ℤ) (N n : ℕ)
    (hs_nd : s.Nodup)
    (hs_lt : ∀ z ∈ s, z < (N : ℤ))
    (hs_gt : ∀ z ∈ s, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) < z) :
    ∃ q : List ℤ, ∃ N' : ℕ, ∃ v : ℤ,
      (∃ rest : List ℤ, q = s ++ rest) ∧
      q.Nodup ∧
      s.length < q.length ∧
      (∀ z ∈ q, z < (N' : ℤ)) ∧
      (∀ z ∈ q, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) < z) ∧
      0 < v ∧
      v = h q ∧
      v ∉ q ∧
      (N : ℤ) < (N' : ℤ) ∧
      v < (N' : ℤ) ∧
      (∀ z ∈ q, z ∈ s ∨ (N : ℤ) ≤ z)

lemma ProofSteps.diag_q_ofFn_at {State : Type}
    (full q : State → List ℤ) (G : ℕ → State) (neg : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ)
    (hprefix : ∀ a b : ℕ, a ≤ b → List.IsPrefix (full (G a)) (full (G b)))
    (hsing : full (G (n + 1)) = q (G (n + 1)) ++ [neg n])
    (hdlen : ∀ k : ℕ, k < (full (G (k + 1))).length) :
    List.ofFn (fun i : Fin (q (G (n + 1))).length =>
      (full (G (i.1 + 1))).get ⟨i.1, hdlen i.1⟩) = q (G (n + 1))

lemma ProofSteps.diag_prefix_injective {α : Type} (l : ℕ → List α)
    (hprefix : ∀ a b : ℕ, a ≤ b → List.IsPrefix (l a) (l b))
    (hnd : ∀ k : ℕ, (l k).Nodup)
    (hlen : ∀ n : ℕ, n < (l (n+1)).length) :
    Function.Injective (fun n : ℕ => (l (n+1)).get ⟨n, hlen n⟩)

lemma ProofSteps.diag_records_neg_diag {State : Type} (full q : State → List ℤ)
    (G : ℕ → State) (neg : ℕ → ℤ) (n m : ℕ)
    (hm : m = (q (G (n + 1))).length)
    (hpref : List.IsPrefix (full (G (n + 1))) (full (G (m + 1))))
    (hsing : full (G (n + 1)) = q (G (n + 1)) ++ [neg n])
    (hmem : m < (full (G (n + 1))).length) :
    (full (G (m + 1))).get ⟨m, lt_of_lt_of_le hmem (List.IsPrefix.length_le hpref)⟩ = neg n

lemma ProofSteps.diag_records_nmem
    (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    {State : Type}
    (full q : State → List ℤ)
    (cut : State → ℕ)
    (recv : State → ℤ)
    (prev : State → List ℤ)
    (prevCut : State → ℕ)
    (neg : ℕ → ℤ)
    (G : ℕ → State)
    (xG : ℕ → ℤ)
    (n : ℕ)
    (hdlen : ∀ k : ℕ, k < (full (G (k + 1))).length)
    (hxG : ∀ k : ℕ, xG k = (full (G (k + 1))).get ⟨k, hdlen k⟩)
    (hrec : 0 < recv (G (n + 1)) ∧ recv (G (n + 1)) = h (q (G (n + 1))) ∧ recv (G (n + 1)) ∉ q (G (n + 1)) ∧ recv (G (n + 1)) < (cut (G (n + 1)) : ℤ))
    (hlen_n : n ≤ (q (G (n + 1))).length)
    (hprefix : ∀ a b : ℕ, a ≤ b → List.IsPrefix (full (G a)) (full (G b)))
    (hfull : ∀ k : ℕ, full (G (k + 1)) = q (G (k + 1)) ++ [neg k])
    (hsep : ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → ∀ z ∈ q (G k), z ∈ prev (G k) ∨ (prevCut (G k) : ℤ) ≤ z)
    (hprev : ∀ k : ℕ, prev (G (k + 1)) = full (G k))
    (hprevCut : ∀ k : ℕ, prevCut (G (k + 1)) = cut (G k))
    (hcut_inc : ∀ k : ℕ, cut (G k) < cut (G (k + 1)))
    (hneg_neg : ∀ k : ℕ, neg k < 0) :
    h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin (q (G (n + 1))).length => xG (i : ℕ))) ∉ Set.range xG

lemma ProofSteps.diag_records_nmem_from_spec
    (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    {State : Type}
    (full q : State → List ℤ)
    (cut : State → ℕ)
    (recv : State → ℤ)
    (prev : State → List ℤ)
    (prevCut : State → ℕ)
    (neg : ℕ → ℤ)
    (last : ℕ → List ℤ)
    (G : ℕ → State)
    (xG : ℕ → ℤ)
    (n : ℕ)
    (Pre : ℕ → State → Prop)
    (hpre_spec : ∀ k p, Pre k p ↔

      (∀ z ∈ full p, z < (cut p : ℤ)) ∧

      full p = q p ++ last k ∧

      (k = 0 ∨ prevCut p < cut p) ∧
      (k = 0 ∨ ∀ z ∈ q p, z ∈ prev p ∨ (prevCut p : ℤ) ≤ z))
    (HPG : ∀ k, Pre k (G k))
    (hdlen : ∀ k, k < (full (G (k+1))).length)
    (hxG : ∀ k, xG k = (full (G (k+1))).get ⟨k, hdlen k⟩)
    (hprevG : ∀ k, prev (G (k+1)) = full (G k))
    (hprevCutG : ∀ k, prevCut (G (k+1)) = cut (G k))
    (hprefix : ∀ a b, a ≤ b → List.IsPrefix (full (G a)) (full (G b)))
    (hlast : ∀ k, last (k+1) = [neg k])
    (hneg_neg : ∀ k, neg k < 0) :
    h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin (q (G (n+1))).length => xG (i : ℕ))) ∉ Set.range xG

differences: The candidate concludes ∃ x with the diagonal enumeration properties, but the original theorem concludes False after applying hgen to that enumeration.
current_review_feedback.reason: The candidate formalizes hgen as applying to infinite L in the union of the tail-containing class and the class containing every negative integer, and for any enumeration e with range L it requires an eventual stage where h(prefix) lies in L and is not in the prefix. The candidate's conclusion constructs an injective x whose range is infinite and contains every negative integer, with arbitrarily late prefixes where h(prefix) is positive and outside range x. This matches the described diagonal enumeration xG and the late fresh positive record condition. However, the natural-language source explicitly says to 'derive False' by applying hgen to that late stage. The candidate theorem stops at the existence of x and the freshness condition; it does not conclude False or any contradiction. The final application of hgen to L = Set.range x and e = x is missing. Thus the formal statement is weaker than the stated theorem.

Assuming a generator h : List ℤ → ℤ and its union-generation property hgen, construct the diagonal enumeration xG of an infinite C₂ language (containing every negative point) and derive False by applying hgen to a late stage where h output is a fresh positive record outside that language.

Parent context (the parent theorem remains a goal, not a fact):
theorem fcs76_collections_exist :
  ∃ C1 C2 : Set {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
    (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C1 →
      ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
        g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
    (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C2 →
      ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
        g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
    ¬ (∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
      ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ (C1 ∪ C2) →
        ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
          ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
              List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))

theorem ProofReviewed_diag_records (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    (hgen : ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
      L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
          {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) :
    False

result.statement: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
result.proof: Take the nonnegative integers as points p_n = n and the negative integers as points m_n = −n−1. Let C₁ be the languages whose carrier contains some tail {p_{N+j} : j ≥ 0}, and C₂ the languages whose carrier contains every m_n. The sequence (p_n) is injective and generates each member of C₁ after its cutoff, giving non-uniform sample-free generation; the sequence (m_n) generates each member of C₂ from time zero, giving uniform sample-free generation. Freshness reduces to membership together with absence of earlier repetition, which holds because both sequences are injective. For the negative clause, assume some sample-based generator G generates the union in the limit. Build nested finite injective prefixes together with strictly increasing cutoffs: given a stage prefix s and cutoff N, enumerate s followed by the positive tail from N; this enumeration belongs to C₁, so G must eventually output a fresh value, which cannot be a previously listed element and hence is some p_k with k ≥ N. Extend the prefix by that observed enumeration prefix and append the next negative point m_n, choosing a fresh larger cutoff so that p_k occurs neither in the new prefix nor in its future positive tail. Induction shows p_k is never reproduced later. The nested prefixes converge to an injective sequence x whose range is infinite and contains every negative point, so it is the carrier of a language in C₂ that x enumerates. At each stage time the prefix of x agrees with the recorded stage prefix, so G outputs p_k, which lies outside this limiting language; since these failures occur arbitrarily late, G fails to generate in the limit, a contradiction. Hence the union is not generatable in the limit, and the constructed collections witness the claim.

let neg : ℕ → ℤ := fun n => (-(n : ℤ) - 1)
let last : ℕ → List ℤ := fun n => if n = 0 then [] else [neg (n-1)]
let State := ((List ℤ × List ℤ) × (ℕ × ℤ)) × (List ℤ × ℕ)

let q : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.1.1.2
let cut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.1.2.1
let recv : State → ℤ := fun p => p.1.2.2
let prev : State → List ℤ := fun p => p.2.1
let prevCut : State → ℕ := fun p => p.2.2
let mk : List ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → ℤ → List ℤ → ℕ → State :=
  fun f qq c r p pc => (((f, qq), (c, r)), (p, pc))
let Pre : ℕ → State → Prop := fun n p =>
  (full p).Nodup ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), z < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
  (∀ z ∈ (full p), neg n < z) ∧
  n ≤ (full p).length ∧
  (full p) = (q p) ++ (last n) ∧
  (∃ rest : List ℤ, (q p) = (prev p) ++ rest) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (0 < (recv p) ∧ (recv p) = h (q p) ∧ (recv p) ∉ (q p) ∧ (recv p) < ((cut p : ℕ) : ℤ))) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (prevCut p) < (cut p)) ∧
  (n = 0 ∨ (∀ z ∈ (q p), z ∈ (prev p) ∨ ((prevCut p : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ z))
let baseState : State := mk [] [] 0 0 [] 0
have hbase : Pre 0 baseState := by
  simp [Pre, baseState, full, q, cut, recv, prev, prevCut, mk, last]
skip
let Gfull : (k : ℕ) → {s : State // Pre k s} :=

    let s : State := ih.1
    let dt := ProofSteps.diag_tail h hgen (full s) (cut s) k ih.2.1 ih.2.2.1 ih.2.2.2.1
    let qq : List ℤ := Classical.choose dt
    let dt2 := Classical.choose_spec dt
    let N' : ℕ := Classical.choose dt2
    let dt3 := Classical.choose_spec dt2
    let v : ℤ := Classical.choose dt3
    let hspec := Classical.choose_spec dt3
    let s' : State := mk (qq ++ [neg k]) qq N' v (full s) (cut s)
    ⟨s', ?_⟩)
rcases hspec with ⟨hqf, hqnd, hqlen, hqlt, hqgt, hv0, hv_eq, hv_not, hcut_lt, hvN, hqsep⟩
rcases ih.2 with ⟨hnd, hlt, hgt, hlen, hfull, hqprev, hrec, hcut, hsep⟩

    omega

· simpa [last, Nat.succ_ne_zero k, Nat.add_sub_cancel_right]
· exact hqf
· right

· right

· right
  exact hqsep

let HPG : ∀ k, Pre k (G k) := fun k => (Gfull k).2
have hpre : ∀ k, full (G (k+1)) = q (G (k+1)) ++ last (k+1) :=

have hlast : ∀ k, last (k+1) = [neg k] := by

  intro k

  rw [hxG ((q (G (n+1))).length)]
  exact ProofSteps.diag_records_neg_diag full q G neg n ((q (G (n+1))).length) rfl hpref (hfullG n) hmem

have hLx : Lx ∈ {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1} := by

      recv (G (n+1)) ∉ q (G (n+1)) ∧

skip
let e : ℕ → ℤ := fun n => if hln : n < s.length then s.get ⟨n, hln⟩ else (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ)
have h1 : ∀ (n : ℕ) (hlt : n < s.length), e n = s.get ⟨n, hlt⟩ := by
  intro n hlt
  simp [e, hlt]
have h2 : ∀ n : ℕ, s.length ≤ n → e n = (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ) := by
  intro n hn
  simp [e, hn, not_lt_of_ge hn]
have hci : Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ Set.range e := ProofSteps.stage_enum_range_ci s N e h2
have hinf : (Set.range e).Infinite := ProofSteps.stage_enum_range_infinite s N e h2
let L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} := ⟨Set.range e, hinf⟩
have hC1 : L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
    {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) := by
  left
  exact ⟨N, hci⟩
obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := hgen L hC1 e rfl
let r : ℕ := max t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1))
have hsr : s.length < r := by
  dsimp [r]
  exact Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le (Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le (Nat.lt_succ_self s.length) (Nat.le_max_left (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
    (Nat.le_max_right t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
have hsr_le : s.length ≤ r := Nat.le_of_lt hsr
have hNr : N ≤ r := by
  dsimp [r]
  exact Nat.le_trans (Nat.le_trans (Nat.le_succ N) (Nat.le_max_right (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
    (Nat.le_max_right t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
have htr : h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ Set.range e ∧
    h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ))) ∉ List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ)) :=
    ht r (Nat.le_max_left t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))

let v : ℤ := h p
rcases htr.1 with ⟨m, hm⟩

  simpa [v, p] using hm
have hv_notin_p : v ∉ p := by
  simpa [p, v] using htr.2
have hm_ge_r : r ≤ m := by
  by_contra hcontra
  have hmr : m < r := Nat.lt_of_not_ge hcontra
  have hmem : e m ∈ p := by
    dsimp [p]
    rw [List.mem_ofFn]
    exact ⟨⟨m, hmr⟩, rfl⟩
  exact hv_notin_p (hmv ▸ hmem)

have hm_tail : e m = (N + (m - s.length) : ℤ) := h2 m hm_ge_s
have hv_tail : v = (N + (m - s.length) : ℤ) := by
  rw [← hmv, hm_tail]
have hNm : N ≤ m := le_trans hNr hm_ge_r
have hk : ∃ k : ℕ, N ≤ k ∧ e k = v := ⟨m, hNm, hmv⟩
let N' : ℕ := N + (m - s.length) + 1
have hv_ge_N : (N : ℤ) ≤ v := by
  rw [hv_tail]
  exact_mod_cast Nat.le_add_right N (m - s.length)
have hm_gt_s : s.length < m := lt_of_lt_of_le hsr hm_ge_r
have hv_pos : 0 < v := by
  rw [hv_tail]
  have hN_nonneg : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (N : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.zero_le N
  omega
have hv_lt_N' : v < (N' : ℤ) := by
  rw [hv_tail]

  omega
have hinj_fin : Function.Injective (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ)) := by
  intro i j hij
  change e (i : ℕ) = e (j : ℕ) at hij
  apply Fin.ext
  by_cases hi : (i : ℕ) < s.length
  · by_cases hj : (j : ℕ) < s.length
    · have hgeti : e (i : ℕ) = s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩ := h1 (i : ℕ) hi

        rw [h2 (j : ℕ) hj_ge]
        exact_mod_cast Nat.le_add_right N ((j : ℕ) - s.length)
      omega

    by_cases hj : (j : ℕ) < s.length
    · have hj_ltN : e (j : ℕ) < (N : ℤ) := by
        rw [h1 (j : ℕ) hj]
        exact hs_lt (s.get ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩) (List.get_mem s ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩)
      have hi_geN : (N : ℤ) ≤ e (i : ℕ) := by
        rw [h2 (i : ℕ) hi_ge]

lemma ProofSteps.diag_records_nmem_from_spec
    (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    {State : Type}
    (full q : State → List ℤ)
    (cut : State → ℕ)
    (recv : State → ℤ)
    (prev : State → List ℤ)
    (prevCut : State → ℕ)
    (neg : ℕ → ℤ)
    (last : ℕ → List ℤ)
    (G : ℕ → State)
    (xG : ℕ → ℤ)
    (n : ℕ)
    (Pre : ℕ → State → Prop)
    (hpre_spec : ∀ k p, Pre k p ↔
      (full p).Nodup ∧
      (∀ z ∈ full p, z < (cut p : ℤ)) ∧
      (∀ z ∈ full p, neg k < z) ∧
      k ≤ (full p).length ∧
      full p = q p ++ last k ∧
      (∃ rest : List ℤ, q p = prev p ++ rest) ∧
      (k = 0 ∨ (0 < recv p ∧ recv p = h (q p) ∧ recv p ∉ q p ∧ recv p < (cut p : ℤ))) ∧
      (k = 0 ∨ prevCut p < cut p) ∧
      (k = 0 ∨ ∀ z ∈ q p, z ∈ prev p ∨ (prevCut p : ℤ) ≤ z))
    (HPG : ∀ k, Pre k (G k))
    (hdlen : ∀ k, k < (full (G (k+1))).length)
    (hxG : ∀ k, xG k = (full (G (k+1))).get ⟨k, hdlen k⟩)
    (hprevG : ∀ k, prev (G (k+1)) = full (G k))
    (hprevCutG : ∀ k, prevCut (G (k+1)) = cut (G k))
    (hprefix : ∀ a b, a ≤ b → List.IsPrefix (full (G a)) (full (G b)))
    (hlast : ∀ k, last (k+1) = [neg k])
    (hneg_neg : ∀ k, neg k < 0) :
    h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin (q (G (n+1))).length => xG (i : ℕ))) ∉ Set.range xG

have hfull_n' : full (G (n + 1)) = q (G (n + 1)) ++ [neg n] := by
  rw [hfull_n, hlast_n]
have hlen_n : n ≤ (q (G (n + 1))).length := by
  simpa [hfull_n'] using hlen

  intro k
  rcases (hpre_spec (k + 1) (G (k + 1))).mp (HPG (k + 1)) with
    ⟨_, _, _, _, hf, _, _, _, _⟩
  rw [hf, hlast k]
have hsep : ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → ∀ z ∈ q (G k), z ∈ prev (G k) ∨ (prevCut (G k) : ℤ) ≤ z := by
  intro k hk z hz

  exact (hs.resolve_left (by omega)) z hz

    ⟨_, _, _, _, _, _, _, hc, _⟩
  have hc' : prevCut (G (k + 1)) < cut (G (k + 1)) := hc.resolve_left (Nat.succ_ne_zero k)
  simpa [hprevCutG k] using hc'

nodes.claim: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.
nodes.statement:
theorem fcs76_collections_exist :
  ∃ C1 C2 : Set {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
    (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C1 →
      ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
        g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
    (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C2 →
      ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
        g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
    ¬ (∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
      ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ (C1 ∪ C2) →
        ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
          ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
              List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))

nodes.claim: For any sequence of lists with nested prefixes and nodupness, the diagonal nth element of the (n+1)th list is injective.
nodes.proof_hint: Use the established prefix get equality and List.Nodup.get_inj_iff; split on whether a ≤ b and run the symmetric argument for the other case.

nodes.claim: For the diagonal stage, the entry at index m equals neg n when stage n+1 appends it and a prefix to stage m+1 includes it.
nodes.proof_hint: Convert get to getElem, use prefix get lemma, rewrite by the singleton append and append/singleton getElem lemmas.

nodes.claim: For neg : ℕ → ℤ and k, the stage-tail singleton list (if k+1 = 0 then [] else [neg (k+1-1)]) equals [neg k].
nodes.proof_hint: Use Nat.succ_ne_zero and rewrite the if with ite_eq_right, then Nat.add_sub_cancel_right.

nodes.claim: For stages whose full list at stage k+1 appends neg k after q, any value that first appears at or after stage n+1 but is not in q (G (n+1)) is either negative or at least cut (G (n+1)).
nodes.proof_hint: Strong induction on the stage index r. For r=t+1 rewrite full as q ++ [neg t]; the singleton tail is negative, and a q member either lies in prev (the previous full list, so apply induction to t) or is at least prevCut, which rewrites to cut (G t) and is at least cut (G (n+1)) by iterating hcut_inc. Handle r=0 as impossible.

nodes.claim: For State stages with nested prefixes and full (G (k+1)) = q (G (k+1)) ++ [neg k], if the stage record recv (G (n+1)) is positive, equals h (q (G (n+1))), avoids q (G (n+1)), and lies below cut (G (n+1)), then h of the q-length diagonal prefix is not in the diagonal range.
nodes.proof_hint: Rewrite the q-ofFn list by diag_q_ofFn_at and h rec to recv; assume recv is xG m; split m below/equal/above q length. Below uses ofFn membership to contradict recv not in q; equal uses diag_records_neg_diag and positivity of recv vs neg n; above uses an induction on stages: any new full entry after stage n+1 is negative or at least cut (G (n+1)), contradicting recv < cut.

nodes.claim: Repackage ProofSteps.diag_records_nmem under an iff specification of Pre, so the final branch of diag_records can obtain all specialized stage facts without unfolding the large let-defined Pre.
nodes.proof_hint: Use hpre_spec to project the nine Pre fields for n+1 and arbitrary stages, derive hrec, hlen_n, hfull, hsep, hcut_inc, then apply ProofSteps.diag_records_nmem.

nodes.claim: Definitional iff-spec for the Pre shape: for h, neg, last, the raw stage predicate is iff itself, so the final branch can build hpre_spec without unfolding the large local Pre.
nodes.proof_hint: intro k p; rfl

nodes.claim: Assuming a generator h : List ℤ → ℤ and its union-generation property hgen, construct the diagonal enumeration xG of an infinite C₂ language (containing every negative point) and derive False by applying hgen to a late stage where h output is a fresh positive record outside that language.
nodes.proof_hint: Recursively run diag_tail to build nested nodup prefixes and strictly increasing cutoffs; append negative points to make full stages. Define the diagonal sequence xG and use diag_prefix_injective for injectivity. Prove range xG is infinite and contains every negative point, so xG enumerates a C₂ language. Use diag_records_nmem to close the fresh positive record nonmembership for late stages.

lemma ProofSteps.negative_injective : Function.Injective (fun n : ℕ => (-(n : ℤ) - 1))

lemma ProofSteps.diag_step (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    (hgen : ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
      L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
          {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))
    (s : List ℤ) (N : ℕ)
    (hs_nd : s.Nodup)
    (hs_lt : ∀ z ∈ s, z < (N : ℤ)) :
    ∃ e : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ N' : ℕ, ∃ r : ℕ, ∃ v : ℤ,
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (hlt : n < s.length), e n = s.get ⟨n, hlt⟩) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, s.length ≤ n → e n = (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ)) ∧
      s.length < r ∧
      let p : List ℤ := List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ));
      p.Nodup ∧
      (∃ rest : List ℤ, p = s ++ rest) ∧
      v = h p ∧
      (∃ k : ℕ, N ≤ k ∧ e k = v) ∧
      v ∉ p ∧
      (N : ℤ) ≤ v ∧
      0 < v ∧
      v < (N' : ℤ)

      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))
    (s : List ℤ) (N n : ℕ)
    (hs_nd : s.Nodup)
    (hs_lt : ∀ z ∈ s, z < (N : ℤ))
    (hs_gt : ∀ z ∈ s, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) < z) :
    ∃ q : List ℤ, ∃ N' : ℕ, ∃ v : ℤ,
      (∃ rest : List ℤ, q = s ++ rest) ∧
      q.Nodup ∧
      s.length < q.length ∧
      (∀ z ∈ q, z < (N' : ℤ)) ∧
      (∀ z ∈ q, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) < z) ∧
      0 < v ∧
      v = h q ∧
      v ∉ q ∧
      (N : ℤ) < (N' : ℤ) ∧
      v < (N' : ℤ)

lemma ProofSteps.prefix_get_eq {α} (l₁ l₂ : List α)
    (hpref : List.IsPrefix l₁ l₂) (i : Fin l₁.length) :
    l₁.get i = l₂.get ⟨i.1, lt_of_lt_of_le i.2 (List.IsPrefix.length_le hpref)⟩

lemma ProofSteps.diag_q_ofFn_at {State : Type}
    (full q : State → List ℤ) (G : ℕ → State) (neg : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ)
    (hprefix : ∀ a b : ℕ, a ≤ b → List.IsPrefix (full (G a)) (full (G b)))
    (hsing : full (G (n + 1)) = q (G (n + 1)) ++ [neg n])
    (hdlen : ∀ k : ℕ, k < (full (G (k + 1))).length) :
    List.ofFn (fun i : Fin (q (G (n + 1))).length =>
      (full (G (i.1 + 1))).get ⟨i.1, hdlen i.1⟩) = q (G (n + 1))

lemma ProofSteps.diag_q_ofFn {State : Type} (full q : State → List ℤ) (G : ℕ → State) (neg : ℕ → ℤ)
    (hprefix : ∀ a b : ℕ, a ≤ b → List.IsPrefix (full (G a)) (full (G b)))
    (hqfull : ∀ n : ℕ, full (G (n + 1)) = q (G (n + 1)) ++ [neg n])
    (hdlen : ∀ n : ℕ, n < (full (G (n + 1))).length) :
    ∀ n : ℕ,
      List.ofFn (fun i : Fin (q (G (n + 1))).length =>
        (full (G (i.1 + 1))).get ⟨i.1, hdlen i.1⟩) = q (G (n + 1))

lemma ProofSteps.diag_prefix_injective {α : Type} (l : ℕ → List α)
    (hprefix : ∀ a b : ℕ, a ≤ b → List.IsPrefix (l a) (l b))
    (hnd : ∀ k : ℕ, (l k).Nodup)
    (hlen : ∀ n : ℕ, n < (l (n+1)).length) :
    Function.Injective (fun n : ℕ => (l (n+1)).get ⟨n, hlen n⟩)

lemma ProofSteps.diag_records_neg_diag {State : Type} (full q : State → List ℤ)
    (G : ℕ → State) (neg : ℕ → ℤ) (n m : ℕ)
    (hm : m = (q (G (n + 1))).length)
    (hpref : List.IsPrefix (full (G (n + 1))) (full (G (m + 1))))
    (hsing : full (G (n + 1)) = q (G (n + 1)) ++ [neg n])
    (hmem : m < (full (G (n + 1))).length) :
    (full (G (m + 1))).get ⟨m, lt_of_lt_of_le hmem (List.IsPrefix.length_le hpref)⟩ = neg n
lemma ProofSteps.last_succ_eq (neg : ℕ → ℤ) (k : ℕ) : (if k + 1 = 0 then ([] : List ℤ) else [neg (k + 1 - 1)]) = [neg k]

lemma ProofSteps.diag_records_nmem_tail
    {State : Type}
    (full q : State → List ℤ)
    (cut prevCut : State → ℕ)
    (prev : State → List ℤ)
    (neg : ℕ → ℤ)
    (G : ℕ → State)
    (n : ℕ)
    (hfull : ∀ k : ℕ, full (G (k + 1)) = q (G (k + 1)) ++ [neg k])
    (hsep : ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → ∀ z ∈ q (G k), z ∈ prev (G k) ∨ (prevCut (G k) : ℤ) ≤ z)
    (hprev : ∀ k : ℕ, prev (G (k + 1)) = full (G k))
    (hprevCut : ∀ k : ℕ, prevCut (G (k + 1)) = cut (G k))
    (hcut_inc : ∀ k : ℕ, cut (G k) < cut (G (k + 1)))
    (hneg_neg : ∀ k : ℕ, neg k < 0) :
    ∀ r : ℕ, n + 1 ≤ r → ∀ v : ℤ, v ∈ full (G r) → v ∉ q (G (n + 1)) →
      v < 0 ∨ (cut (G (n + 1)) : ℤ) ≤ v

lemma ProofSteps.diag_records_nmem
    (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    {State : Type}
    (full q : State → List ℤ)
    (cut : State → ℕ)
    (recv : State → ℤ)
    (prev : State → List ℤ)
    (prevCut : State → ℕ)
    (neg : ℕ → ℤ)
    (G : ℕ → State)
    (xG : ℕ → ℤ)
    (n : ℕ)
    (hdlen : ∀ k : ℕ, k < (full (G (k + 1))).length)
    (hxG : ∀ k : ℕ, xG k = (full (G (k + 1))).get ⟨k, hdlen k⟩)
    (hrec : 0 < recv (G (n + 1)) ∧ recv (G (n + 1)) = h (q (G (n + 1))) ∧ recv (G (n + 1)) ∉ q (G (n + 1)) ∧ recv (G (n + 1)) < (cut (G (n + 1)) : ℤ))
    (hlen_n : n ≤ (q (G (n + 1))).length)
    (hprefix : ∀ a b : ℕ, a ≤ b → List.IsPrefix (full (G a)) (full (G b)))
    (hfull : ∀ k : ℕ, full (G (k + 1)) = q (G (k + 1)) ++ [neg k])
    (hsep : ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → ∀ z ∈ q (G k), z ∈ prev (G k) ∨ (prevCut (G k) : ℤ) ≤ z)
    (hprev : ∀ k : ℕ, prev (G (k + 1)) = full (G k))
    (hprevCut : ∀ k : ℕ, prevCut (G (k + 1)) = cut (G k))
    (hcut_inc : ∀ k : ℕ, cut (G k) < cut (G (k + 1)))
    (hneg_neg : ∀ k : ℕ, neg k < 0) :
    h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin (q (G (n + 1))).length => xG (i : ℕ))) ∉ Set.range xG

lemma ProofSteps.diag_records_nmem_from_spec
    (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    {State : Type}
    (full q : State → List ℤ)
    (cut : State → ℕ)
    (recv : State → ℤ)
    (prev : State → List ℤ)
    (prevCut : State → ℕ)
    (neg : ℕ → ℤ)
    (last : ℕ → List ℤ)
    (G : ℕ → State)
    (xG : ℕ → ℤ)
    (n : ℕ)
    (Pre : ℕ → State → Prop)
    (hpre_spec : ∀ k p, Pre k p ↔
      (full p).Nodup ∧
      (∀ z ∈ full p, z < (cut p : ℤ)) ∧
      (∀ z ∈ full p, neg k < z) ∧
      k ≤ (full p).length ∧
      full p = q p ++ last k ∧
      (∃ rest : List ℤ, q p = prev p ++ rest) ∧
      (k = 0 ∨ (0 < recv p ∧ recv p = h (q p) ∧ recv p ∉ q p ∧ recv p < (cut p : ℤ))) ∧
      (k = 0 ∨ prevCut p < cut p) ∧
      (k = 0 ∨ ∀ z ∈ q p, z ∈ prev p ∨ (prevCut p : ℤ) ≤ z))
    (HPG : ∀ k, Pre k (G k))
    (hdlen : ∀ k, k < (full (G (k+1))).length)
    (hxG : ∀ k, xG k = (full (G (k+1))).get ⟨k, hdlen k⟩)
    (hprevG : ∀ k, prev (G (k+1)) = full (G k))
    (hprevCutG : ∀ k, prevCut (G (k+1)) = cut (G k))
    (hprefix : ∀ a b, a ≤ b → List.IsPrefix (full (G a)) (full (G b)))
    (hlast : ∀ k, last (k+1) = [neg k])
    (hneg_neg : ∀ k, neg k < 0) :
    h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin (q (G (n+1))).length => xG (i : ℕ))) ∉ Set.range xG

lemma ProofSteps.diag_records (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    (hgen : ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
      L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪

        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →

          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) :
    False

skip
let e : ℕ → ℤ := fun n => if hln : n < s.length then s.get ⟨n, hln⟩ else (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ)
have h1 : ∀ (n : ℕ) (hlt : n < s.length), e n = s.get ⟨n, hlt⟩ := by
  intro n hlt
  simp [e, hlt]
have h2 : ∀ n : ℕ, s.length ≤ n → e n = (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ) := by
  intro n hn
  simp [e, hn, not_lt_of_ge hn]
have hci : Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ Set.range e := ProofSteps.stage_enum_range_ci s N e h2
have hinf : (Set.range e).Infinite := ProofSteps.stage_enum_range_infinite s N e h2
let L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} := ⟨Set.range e, hinf⟩
have hC1 : L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
    {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) := by
  left
  exact ⟨N, hci⟩
obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := hgen L hC1 e rfl
let r : ℕ := max t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1))
have hsr : s.length < r := by
  dsimp [r]
  exact Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le (Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le (Nat.lt_succ_self s.length) (Nat.le_max_left (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
    (Nat.le_max_right t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
have hsr_le : s.length ≤ r := Nat.le_of_lt hsr
have hNr : N ≤ r := by
  dsimp [r]
  exact Nat.le_trans (Nat.le_trans (Nat.le_succ N) (Nat.le_max_right (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
    (Nat.le_max_right t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
have htr : h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ Set.range e ∧
    h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ))) ∉ List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ)) :=
    ht r (Nat.le_max_left t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))

let v : ℤ := h p
rcases htr.1 with ⟨m, hm⟩
have hmv : e m = v := by
  simpa [v, p] using hm
have hv_notin_p : v ∉ p := by
  simpa [p, v] using htr.2
have hm_ge_r : r ≤ m := by
  by_contra hcontra
  have hmr : m < r := Nat.lt_of_not_ge hcontra
  have hmem : e m ∈ p := by
    dsimp [p]
    rw [List.mem_ofFn]
    exact ⟨⟨m, hmr⟩, rfl⟩
  exact hv_notin_p (hmv ▸ hmem)

have hm_tail : e m = (N + (m - s.length) : ℤ) := h2 m hm_ge_s
have hv_tail : v = (N + (m - s.length) : ℤ) := by
  rw [← hmv, hm_tail]
have hNm : N ≤ m := le_trans hNr hm_ge_r
have hk : ∃ k : ℕ, N ≤ k ∧ e k = v := ⟨m, hNm, hmv⟩
let N' : ℕ := N + (m - s.length) + 1
have hv_ge_N : (N : ℤ) ≤ v := by
  rw [hv_tail]
  exact_mod_cast Nat.le_add_right N (m - s.length)
have hm_gt_s : s.length < m := lt_of_lt_of_le hsr hm_ge_r
have hv_pos : 0 < v := by
  rw [hv_tail]
  have hN_nonneg : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (N : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.zero_le N
  omega
have hv_lt_N' : v < (N' : ℤ) := by
  rw [hv_tail]
  dsimp [N']
  omega
have hinj_fin : Function.Injective (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ)) := by
  intro i j hij
  change e (i : ℕ) = e (j : ℕ) at hij
  apply Fin.ext
  by_cases hi : (i : ℕ) < s.length
  · by_cases hj : (j : ℕ) < s.length

        rw [h2 (j : ℕ) hj_ge]
        exact_mod_cast Nat.le_add_right N ((j : ℕ) - s.length)
      omega

    by_cases hj : (j : ℕ) < s.length
    · have hj_ltN : e (j : ℕ) < (N : ℤ) := by
        rw [h1 (j : ℕ) hj]
        exact hs_lt (s.get ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩) (List.get_mem s ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩)

nodes.claim: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

lemma ProofSteps.stage_enum_range_infinite (s : List ℤ) (N : ℕ) (e : ℕ → ℤ)
    (he_tail : ∀ n : ℕ, s.length ≤ n → e n = (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ)) :
    (Set.range e).Infinite

apply Set.Infinite.mono
exact ProofSteps.stage_enum_range_ci s N e he_tail
have hinj : Function.Injective (fun i : ℕ => (N + i : ℤ)) := by
  intro a b hab
  norm_num at hab
  omega
simpa [ProofSteps.pos_tail_range N] using (Set.infinite_range_of_injective hinj)

nodes.claim: Given generator h and its union property, a finite injective prefix f : Fin l → ℤ and cutoff N, there is a longer finite injective prefix f' starting with f, a fresh positive value p_k with k ≥ N achieved by h on the stage enumeration, and a larger cutoff N' avoiding p_k on future positive tails.

lemma ProofSteps.diag_step (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    (hgen : ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
      L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
          {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))
    (s : List ℤ) (N : ℕ)
    (hs_nd : s.Nodup)
    (hs_lt : ∀ z ∈ s, z < (N : ℤ)) :
    ∃ e : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ N' : ℕ, ∃ r : ℕ, ∃ v : ℤ,
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (hlt : n < s.length), e n = s.get ⟨n, hlt⟩) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, s.length ≤ n → e n = (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ)) ∧
      s.length < r ∧
      let p : List ℤ := List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ));
      p.Nodup ∧
      (∃ rest : List ℤ, p = s ++ rest) ∧
      v = h p ∧
      (∃ k : ℕ, N ≤ k ∧ e k = v) ∧
      v ∉ p ∧
      (N : ℤ) ≤ v ∧
      0 < v ∧
      v < (N' : ℤ)
nodes.body:
skip
let e : ℕ → ℤ := fun n => if hln : n < s.length then s.get ⟨n, hln⟩ else (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ)
have h1 : ∀ (n : ℕ) (hlt : n < s.length), e n = s.get ⟨n, hlt⟩ := by
  intro n hlt
  simp [e, hlt]
have h2 : ∀ n : ℕ, s.length ≤ n → e n = (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ) := by
  intro n hn
  simp [e, hn, not_lt_of_ge hn]
have hci : Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ Set.range e := ProofSteps.stage_enum_range_ci s N e h2
have hinf : (Set.range e).Infinite := ProofSteps.stage_enum_range_infinite s N e h2
let L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} := ⟨Set.range e, hinf⟩
have hC1 : L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
    {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) := by
  left
  exact ⟨N, hci⟩
obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := hgen L hC1 e rfl
let r : ℕ := max t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1))
have hsr : s.length < r := by
  dsimp [r]
  exact Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le (Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le (Nat.lt_succ_self s.length) (Nat.le_max_left (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
    (Nat.le_max_right t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
have hsr_le : s.length ≤ r := Nat.le_of_lt hsr
have hNr : N ≤ r := by
  dsimp [r]
  exact Nat.le_trans (Nat.le_trans (Nat.le_succ N) (Nat.le_max_right (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
    (Nat.le_max_right t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
have htr : h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ Set.range e ∧
    h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ))) ∉ List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ)) :=
    ht r (Nat.le_max_left t (max (s.length + 1) (N + 1)))
let p : List ℤ := List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ))
let v : ℤ := h p
rcases htr.1 with ⟨m, hm⟩
have hmv : e m = v := by
  simpa [v, p] using hm
have hv_notin_p : v ∉ p := by
  simpa [p, v] using htr.2
have hm_ge_r : r ≤ m := by
  by_contra hcontra
  have hmr : m < r := Nat.lt_of_not_ge hcontra
  have hmem : e m ∈ p := by
    dsimp [p]
    rw [List.mem_ofFn]
    exact ⟨⟨m, hmr⟩, rfl⟩
  exact hv_notin_p (hmv ▸ hmem)
have hm_ge_s : s.length ≤ m := le_trans hsr_le hm_ge_r
have hm_tail : e m = (N + (m - s.length) : ℤ) := h2 m hm_ge_s
have hv_tail : v = (N + (m - s.length) : ℤ) := by
  rw [← hmv, hm_tail]
have hNm : N ≤ m := le_trans hNr hm_ge_r
have hk : ∃ k : ℕ, N ≤ k ∧ e k = v := ⟨m, hNm, hmv⟩
let N' : ℕ := N + (m - s.length) + 1
have hv_ge_N : (N : ℤ) ≤ v := by
  rw [hv_tail]
  exact_mod_cast Nat.le_add_right N (m - s.length)
have hm_gt_s : s.length < m := lt_of_lt_of_le hsr hm_ge_r
have hv_pos : 0 < v := by
  rw [hv_tail]
  have hN_nonneg : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (N : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.zero_le N
  omega
have hv_lt_N' : v < (N' : ℤ) := by
  rw [hv_tail]
  dsimp [N']
  omega
have hinj_fin : Function.Injective (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ)) := by
  intro i j hij
  change e (i : ℕ) = e (j : ℕ) at hij
  apply Fin.ext
  by_cases hi : (i : ℕ) < s.length
  · by_cases hj : (j : ℕ) < s.length
    · have hgeti : e (i : ℕ) = s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩ := h1 (i : ℕ) hi
      have hgetj : e (j : ℕ) = s.get ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩ := h1 (j : ℕ) hj
      have hsij : s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩ = s.get ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩ := by
        rw [← hgeti, ← hgetj]
        exact hij
      have hfin : (⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩ : Fin s.length) = ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩ :=
        (hs_nd.get_inj_iff).mp hsij
      exact congrArg (fun x : Fin s.length => (x : ℕ)) hfin
    · have hj_ge : s.length ≤ (j : ℕ) := Nat.le_of_not_gt hj
      have hi_ltN : e (i : ℕ) < (N : ℤ) := by
        rw [h1 (i : ℕ) hi]
        exact hs_lt (s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩) (List.get_mem s ⟨(i : ℕ), hi⟩)
      have hj_geN : (N : ℤ) ≤ e (j : ℕ) := by
        rw [h2 (j : ℕ) hj_ge]
        exact_mod_cast Nat.le_add_right N ((j : ℕ) - s.length)
      omega
  · have hi_ge : s.length ≤ (i : ℕ) := Nat.le_of_not_gt hi
    by_cases hj : (j : ℕ) < s.length
    · have hj_ltN : e (j : ℕ) < (N : ℤ) := by
        rw [h1 (j : ℕ) hj]
        exact hs_lt (s.get ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩) (List.get_mem s ⟨(j : ℕ), hj⟩)
      have hi_geN : (N : ℤ) ≤ e (i : ℕ) := by
        rw [h2 (i : ℕ) hi_ge]
        exact_mod_cast Nat.le_add_right N ((i : ℕ) - s.length)
      omega
    · have hj_ge : s.length ≤ (j : ℕ) := Nat.le_of_not_gt hj
      rw [h2 (i : ℕ) hi_ge, h2 (j : ℕ) hj_ge] at hij
      omega
have hp_nd : p.Nodup := by
  dsimp [p]
  rw [List.nodup_ofFn]
  exact hinj_fin
have hp_take : List.take s.length p = s := by
  apply List.ext_getElem
  · simp [p, List.length_take, List.length_ofFn]
    omega
  · intro i hi₁ hi₂
    simp [p, List.getElem_take, List.getElem_ofFn]
    exact h1 i hi₂
have hp_extend : ∃ rest : List ℤ, p = s ++ rest := by
  refine ⟨List.drop s.length p, ?_⟩
  calc
    p = List.take s.length p ++ List.drop s.length p := (List.take_append_drop s.length p).symm
    _ = s ++ List.drop s.length p := by rw [hp_take]

refine ⟨e, N', r, v, h1, h2, hsr, hp_nd, hp_extend, rfl, hk,
    hv_notin_p, hv_ge_N, hv_pos, hv_lt_N'⟩

refine ⟨q, N', v, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
· exact hv_eq
· exact hrest
· simpa [q] using hsr
rcases hv_not with ⟨k, hNk, hk_eq⟩
have hk_ge_s : s.length ≤ k := by
  by_contra hnot

  have hmem_k : e k ∈ s := by

intro z hz

rw [← hiz]
by_cases hi_lt : (i : ℕ) < s.length
· have hmemi : s.get ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩ ∈ s := List.get_mem s ⟨(i : ℕ), hi_lt⟩

lemma ProofSteps.diag_next_spec (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    (hgen : ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
      L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪

          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))
    (s : List ℤ) (N n : ℕ)

nodes.claim: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

theorem fcs76_collections_exist :
  ∃ C1 C2 : Set {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
    (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C1 →
      ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
        g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
    (∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ C2 →
      ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
        g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n) ∧
    ¬ (∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
      ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}, L ∈ (C1 ∪ C2) →
        ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
          ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
            h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
              List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

data.helper_source:
namespace Fcs76

def Language : Type := {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}

def prefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => prefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def UniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.BijOn e Set.univ L

def GeneratableInLimit (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Enumerates e (L : Set ℤ) →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (prefixOf e n) ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧
          h (prefixOf e n) ∉ prefixOf e n

end Fcs76

def fcs76PrefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => fcs76PrefixOf e n ++ [e n]

  g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → fcs76Fresh g n L

data.source_fragment: definitions of languages over integers, sample-free freshness, non-uniform and uniform generation without samples, enumeration of a language as a surjective range, and sample-based generation in the limit
data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

The languages are represented as subtypes of infinite sets of integers, matching the universe and infinite-language requirement. The C1 clause has one generator g and, for each L∈C1, a member-dependent t after which every g n is in L and differs from all earlier g m; this matches non-uniform sample-free generation. statement.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

namespace Fcs76

def Language : Type := {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}

def prefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => prefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def UniformGeneratable (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → Fresh g n L

def Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.BijOn e Set.univ L

def GeneratableInLimit (C : Set Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Enumerates e (L : Set ℤ) →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (prefixOf e n) ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧
          h (prefixOf e n) ∉ prefixOf e n

end Fcs76

data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : Language, L ∈ C →

def fcs76Language : Type := {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}

def fcs76PrefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => fcs76PrefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def fcs76Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def fcs76NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → fcs76Fresh g n L

def fcs76UniformGeneratable (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → fcs76Fresh g n L

def fcs76Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.BijOn e Set.univ L

def fcs76GeneratableInLimit (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, fcs76Enumerates e (L : Set ℤ) →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (fcs76PrefixOf e n) ∈ (L : Set ℤ) ∧
          h (fcs76PrefixOf e n) ∉ fcs76PrefixOf e n

data.source_fragment: definitions of languages over integers, sample-free freshness, non-uniform and uniform generation without samples, enumeration of a language, and sample-based generation in the limit
data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

def fcs76Language : Type := {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite}

def fcs76PrefixOf (e : ℕ → ℤ) : ℕ → List ℤ
  | 0 => []
  | n + 1 => fcs76PrefixOf e n ++ [e n]

def fcs76Fresh (g : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (L : fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  g n ∈ L.1 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → g m ≠ g n

def fcs76NonUniformGeneratable (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → fcs76Fresh g n L

def fcs76UniformGeneratable (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
    ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n → fcs76Fresh g n L

def fcs76Enumerates (e : ℕ → ℤ) (L : Set ℤ) : Prop :=
  Set.range e = L

def fcs76GeneratableInLimit (C : Set fcs76Language) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : List ℤ → ℤ,
    ∀ L : fcs76Language, L ∈ C →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, fcs76Enumerates e L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (fcs76PrefixOf e n) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (fcs76PrefixOf e n) ∉ fcs76PrefixOf e n

data.source_fragment: definitions of languages over integers, sample-free freshness, non-uniform and uniform generation without samples, enumeration of a language as a surjective range, and sample-based generation in the limit
data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

data.reason: Set.range e = L.1 is the actual predicate that every element of L occurs as some e n, so e is an enumeration/surjection of L. The languages are represented as subtypes of infinite sets of integers, matching the universe and infinite-language requirement. The C1 clause has one generator g and, for each L∈C1, a member-dependent t after which every g n is in L and differs from all earlier g m; this matches non-uniform sample-free generation. The C2 clause fixes the same g and t for every L∈C2 with the same freshness condition, matching uniform sample-free generation. The negated sample-based clause quantifies over h:List ℤ→ℤ, every L∈C1∪C2, and every enumeration e of L, and requires after some t that h(prefix of length n) lies in L and avoids the prefix; this matches sample-based generation in the limit. data.source_text: Work over the universe of integers, where a language is an infinite set of integers and a collection is any set of such languages. A sample-free generator is an integer sequence; its output at a time is fresh for a language if that output lies in the language and never appeared earlier. A collection is non-uniformly generatable without samples if a single sample-free generator's outputs become fresh for every member after a member-dependent time, and uniformly generatable if the freshness time can be chosen once for all members. A sample-based generator maps an ordered prefix of enumerated strings to an output, and generates a collection in the limit if for every member and every enumeration of it there is a time after which all outputs lie in the member yet avoid the strings already seen. The theorem asserts that there exist collections C₁ and C₂ such that C₁ is non-uniformly generatable without samples, C₂ is uniformly generatable without samples, but the union C₁ ∪ C₂ is not generatable in the limit.

theorem ProofReviewed_diag_step (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    (hgen : ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
      L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
          {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))
    (s : List ℤ) (N : ℕ) (y : ℤ)
    (hs_nd : s.Nodup)
    (hs_lt : ∀ z ∈ s, z < (N : ℤ))
    (hy_lt : y < (N : ℤ))
    (hy_notin : y ∉ s) :
    ∃ e : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ N' : ℕ, ∃ r : ℕ, ∃ v : ℤ,
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (hlt : n < s.length), e n = s.get ⟨n, hlt⟩) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, s.length ≤ n → e n = (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ)) ∧
      s.length ≤ r ∧
      let p : List ℤ := List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ));
      p.Nodup ∧
      (∃ rest : List ℤ, p = s ++ rest) ∧
      v = h p ∧
      v ∈ Set.range e ∧
      v ∉ p ∧
      (N : ℤ) ≤ v ∧
      v < (N' : ℤ) ∧
      (p ++ [y]).Nodup ∧
      (∀ z ∈ p ++ [y], z < (N' : ℤ))

      L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
          {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))
    (s : List ℤ) (N : ℕ)
    (hs_nd : s.Nodup)
    (hs_lt : ∀ z ∈ s, z < (N : ℤ)) :

theorem ProofReviewed_diag_step (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    (hgen : ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
      L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
          {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))
    (s : List ℤ) (N : ℕ)
    (hs_nd : s.Nodup)
    (hs_lt : ∀ z ∈ s, z < (N : ℤ)) :
    ∃ e : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ N' : ℕ, ∃ r : ℕ, ∃ v : ℤ,
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (hlt : n < s.length), e n = s.get ⟨n, hlt⟩) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, s.length ≤ n → e n = (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ)) ∧
      s.length < r ∧
      let p : List ℤ := List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ));
      p.Nodup ∧
      (∃ rest : List ℤ, p = s ++ rest) ∧
      v = h p ∧
      v ∈ Set.range e ∧
      v ∉ p ∧
      (N : ℤ) ≤ v ∧
      v < (N' : ℤ)

differences: The conclusion requires only N ≤ v, not 0 < v, so it does not ensure the fresh value is positive.
data.reason: The Lean conclusion constructs e and p and obtains v = h p with v ∈ Set.range e, v ∉ p, and (N : ℤ) ≤ v, v < N'. The natural-language theorem, however, explicitly requires a fresh positive value, i.e. a value satisfying 0 < v. The Lean statement only gives v ≥ N, and since N is an arbitrary natural number not assumed positive, it permits v = 0 when N = 0. Thus the positivity condition is not faithfully formalized.

data.source_text:
Given generator h and its union property, a finite injective prefix f : Fin l → ℤ and cutoff N, there is a longer finite injective prefix f' starting with f, a fresh positive value p_k with k ≥ N achieved by h on the stage enumeration, and a larger cutoff N' avoiding p_k on future positive tails.

    (hgen : ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},

          {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))
    (s : List ℤ) (N : ℕ)
    (hs_nd : s.Nodup)
    (hs_lt : ∀ z ∈ s, z < (N : ℤ)) :
    ∃ e : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ N' : ℕ, ∃ r : ℕ, ∃ v : ℤ,
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (hlt : n < s.length), e n = s.get ⟨n, hlt⟩) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, s.length ≤ n → e n = (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ)) ∧
      s.length < r ∧
      let p : List ℤ := List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ));
      p.Nodup ∧
      (∃ rest : List ℤ, p = s ++ rest) ∧
      v = h p ∧

theorem ProofReviewed_diag_step (h : List ℤ → ℤ)
    (hgen : ∀ L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite},
      L ∈ ({L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∃ N : ℕ, Set.Ici (N : ℤ) ⊆ L.1} ∪
          {L : {L : Set ℤ // L.Infinite} | ∀ n : ℕ, (-(n : ℤ) - 1) ∈ L.1}) →
      ∀ e : ℕ → ℤ, Set.range e = L.1 →
        ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, t ≤ n →
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∈ L.1 ∧
          h (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ))) ∉
            List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => e (i : ℕ)))
    (s : List ℤ) (N : ℕ)
    (hs_nd : s.Nodup)
    (hs_lt : ∀ z ∈ s, z < (N : ℤ)) :
    ∃ e : ℕ → ℤ, ∃ N' : ℕ, ∃ r : ℕ, ∃ v : ℤ,
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (hlt : n < s.length), e n = s.get ⟨n, hlt⟩) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, s.length ≤ n → e n = (N + (n - s.length) : ℤ)) ∧
      s.length < r ∧
      let p : List ℤ := List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r => e (i : ℕ));
      p.Nodup ∧
      (∃ rest : List ℤ, p = s ++ rest) ∧
      v = h p ∧
      v ∈ Set.range e ∧
      v ∉ p ∧
      (N : ℤ) ≤ v ∧
      0 < v ∧
      v < (N' : ℤ)

differences: The conclusion imposes a value lower bound `N ≤ v` rather than the source's index condition `k ≥ N` for the stage at which p_k is achieved.
data.reason: The natural theorem requires a fresh value p_k with k ≥ N, i.e., the value is produced at an index/stage at least N. The formal candidate instead requires only `(N : ℤ) ≤ v` and `v ∈ Set.range e`; it does not assert the existence of an index `k` with `e k = v` and `N ≤ k`. A sequence could satisfy the candidate by having `v ≥ N` while the witnessing index is below `N`, so the stage condition from the source is lost.
